1.55.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
hate hiraṇyakaśipau dānave devakaṇṭake ..
hataśeṣāstu daiteyāḥ pātālatalamāśritāḥ .. 1 ..
1.55.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
हते हिरण्यकशिपौ दानवे देवकण्टके ॥
हतशेषास्तु दैतेयाः पातालतलमाश्रिताः ॥ 1 ॥
1.55.m: Śaṅkara said: / When Hiraṇyakaśipu, the Dānava who was a thorn in the side of the gods, was slain, / the surviving Daiteyas took refuge in the depths of Pātāla.

1.55.s:
pātālatalasaṃstheṣu dānaveṣu mahāyaśāḥ ..
prahrādapautro dharmātmā virocanasuto baliḥ .. 2 ..
1.55.d:
पातालतलसंस्थेषु दानवेषु महायशाः ॥
प्रह्रादपौत्रो धर्मात्मा विरोचनसुतो बलिः ॥ 2 ॥
1.55.m: While the Dānavas resided in the depths of Pātāla, the illustrious, / righteous Bali, grandson of Prahrāda and son of Virocana,

1.55.s:
ārādhya tapasogreṇa varaṃ lebhe pitāmahāt ..
avadhyatvamajeyatvaṃ samareṣu surāsuraiḥ .. .. 3 ..
1.55.d:
आराध्य तपसोग्रेण वरं लेभे पितामहात् ॥
अवध्यत्वमजेयत्वं समरेषु सुरासुरैः ॥ ॥ 3 ॥
1.55.m: worshipped with fierce austerity and obtained a boon from his grandfather: / invulnerability and unconquerability in battles by gods and asuras.

1.55.s:
varalabdhaṃ baliṃ jñātvā punaścakrurditeḥ sutāḥ ..
prahṛṣṭā daityarājānaṃ prahrādānumaterbalim .. 4 ..
1.55.d:
वरलब्धं बलिं ज्ञात्वा पुनश्चक्रुर्दितेः सुताः ॥
प्रहृष्टा दैत्यराजानं प्रह्रादानुमतेर्बलिम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.55.m: Knowing that Bali had obtained the boon, the sons of Diti, rejoiced, / made Bali king of the Daityas once more, with Prahrāda's consent.

1.55.s:
saṃprāpya daityarājyaṃ tu balena caturaṃgiṇā ..
jitvā deveśvaraṃ śakramājahārā'marāvatīm .. 5 ..
1.55.d:
संप्राप्य दैत्यराज्यं तु बलेन चतुरंगिणा ॥
जित्वा देवेश्वरं शक्रमाजहाराऽमरावतीम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.55.m: Having attained the kingship of the Daityas, with a fourfold army, / he defeated Śakra, the lord of the gods, and seized Amarāvatī.

1.55.s:
sthānabhraṣṭo mahendro'pi kaśyapaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ..
kaśyapena tadā sārdhaṃ brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ .. 6 ..
1.55.d:
स्थानभ्रष्टो महेन्द्रोऽपि कश्यपं शरणं गतः ॥
कश्यपेन तदा सार्धं ब्रह्माणं शरणं गतः ॥ 6 ॥
1.55.m: Deprived of his realm, Mahendra took refuge with Kaśyapa; / then together with Kaśyapa, he took refuge with Brahmā.

1.55.s:
brahmaṇā'bhihito devaṃ jagāma śaraṇaṃ harim ..
amṛtādhmātameghābhaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam .. 7 ..
1.55.d:
ब्रह्मणाऽभिहितो देवं जगाम शरणं हरिम् ॥
अमृताध्मातमेघाभं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.55.m: Directed by Brahmā, he went for refuge to the god Hari, / who resembles a cloud swollen with nectar, holding the conch, discus, and mace.

1.55.s:
devo'pyabhayadānena saṃyojya balasūdanam ..
uvāca vacanaṃ kāle meghagambhīrayā girā..8..
1.55.d:
देवोऽप्यभयदानेन संयोज्य बलसूदनम् ॥
उवाच वचनं काले मेघगम्भीरया गिरा॥8॥
1.55.m: The god, too, assuring the slayer of Bala of safety, / spoke these words at that time in a voice deep as a thundercloud:

1.55.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca..
gaccha śakra bhaviṣyāmi trātā te balasūdana ..
devarūpadharo bhūtvā vañcayiṣyāmi taṃ balim ..9 ..
1.55.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच॥
गच्छ शक्र भविष्यामि त्राता ते बलसूदन ॥
देवरूपधरो भूत्वा वञ्चयिष्यामि तं बलिम् ॥9 ॥
1.55.m: The holy Lord said: / Go, Śakra; I shall be your protector, O slayer of Bala! / Assuming the form of a god, I shall deceive that Bali.

1.55.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
evamuktastadā śakraḥ prayayau kaśyapāśramam..
ādideśā'dittergarbhaṃ cāṃśenā'tha ca sarvadā ..1.55.1 0..
1.55.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
एवमुक्तस्तदा शक्रः प्रययौ कश्यपाश्रमम्॥
आदिदेशाऽदित्तेर्गर्भं चांशेनाऽथ च सर्वदा ॥1.55.1 0॥
1.55.m: Śaṅkara said: / Having been addressed thus, Śakra then went to the hermitage of Kaśyapa; / and [Viṣṇu] entered the womb of Aditi by a portion [of himself] forever.

1.55.s:
garbhastha eva tejāṃsi dānavebhyaḥ sa ādade ..
tataḥ kālena suṣuve aditirvāmanākṛtim .. 11 ..
1.55.d:
गर्भस्थ एव तेजांसि दानवेभ्यः स आददे ॥
ततः कालेन सुषुवे अदितिर्वामनाकृतिम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.55.m: Even while in the womb, he took away the energies of the Dānavas; / then in due time Aditi gave birth to [him in] the form of a dwarf.

1.55.s:
yasmiñjāte suragaṇāḥ praharṣamatulaṃ gatāḥ ..
ṛṣayaśca mahābhāgāstraikālyāmaladarśinaḥ .. 12 ..
1.55.d:
यस्मिञ्जाते सुरगणाः प्रहर्षमतुलं गताः ॥
ऋषयश्च महाभागास्त्रैकाल्यामलदर्शिनः ॥ 12 ॥
1.55.m: Upon whose birth the hosts of gods attained unequalled joy, / as did the illustrious ṛṣis, who perceive the three times without blemish.

1.55.s:
etasminneva kāle tu hayamedhāya dīkṣitaḥ ..
balirdaityapatiḥ śrīmānspāligrāmamupāśritaḥ .. 13 ..
1.55.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु हयमेधाय दीक्षितः ॥
बलिर्दैत्यपतिः श्रीमान्स्पालिग्राममुपाश्रितः ॥ 13 ॥
1.55.m: At that very time, consecrated for a horse-sacrifice, / the glorious Bali, lord of the Daityas, was staying at Śāligrāma.

1.55.s:
vāmaskandhe tamādāya tasya yajñe bṛhaspatiḥ ..
anayadbhṛguśārdūla nūnaṃ tasyaiva māyayā .. 14 ..
1.55.d:
वामस्कन्धे तमादाय तस्य यज्ञे बृहस्पतिः ॥
अनयद्भृगुशार्दूल नूनं तस्यैव मायया ॥ 14 ॥
1.55.m: Taking him upon his left shoulder, Bṛhaspati led him / to his sacrifice, O tiger among the Bhṛgus, surely through his own divine illusion.

1.55.s:
yajñavāṭaṃ sa saṃprāpya yajñaṃ tuṣṭāva vāmanaḥ ..
ātmānamātmanā brahmanbhasmacchanna ivā'nalaḥ .. 15 ..
1.55.d:
यज्ञवाटं स संप्राप्य यज्ञं तुष्टाव वामनः ॥
आत्मानमात्मना ब्रह्मन्भस्मच्छन्न इवाऽनलः ॥ 15 ॥
1.55.m: Having reached the sacrificial enclosure, the dwarf praised the sacrifice, / [concealing] himself by himself, O brahmin, like fire covered with ashes.

1.55.s:
praveśayāmāsa ca taṃ balirdharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ..
dadarśa ca mahābhāgaṃ vāmanaṃ sumanoharam .. 16 ..
1.55.d:
प्रवेशयामास च तं बलिर्धर्मभृतां वरः ॥
ददर्श च महाभागं वामनं सुमनोहरम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.55.m: And Bali, the foremost of the upholders of dharma, ushered him in, / and saw the illustrious, exceedingly charming dwarf,

1.55.s:
saṃyuktasarvāvayavaiḥ pīnaiḥ saṃkṣiptaparvabhiḥ ..
kṛṣṇājinajaṭādaṇḍakamaṇḍaluvirājitam ...17..
1.55.d:
संयुक्तसर्वावयवैः पीनैः संक्षिप्तपर्वभिः ॥
कृष्णाजिनजटादण्डकमण्डलुविराजितम् ॥.17॥
1.55.m: with all limbs fully formed, plump, with compact joints, / resplendent with a black antelope skin, matted hair, staff, and water pot,

1.55.s:
vikramiṣyanyathā vyāghro līyati sma svavigrahe ..
vikramiṣyam̐stathaivorvīṃ līnagātraḥ svavigrahe .. 18 ..
1.55.d:
विक्रमिष्यन्यथा व्याघ्रो लीयति स्म स्वविग्रहे ॥
विक्रमिष्यम्̐स्तथैवोर्वीं लीनगात्रः स्वविग्रहे ॥ 18 ॥
1.55.m: who crouched within his own body like a tiger about to pounce, / limbs retracted within his own body, about to stride across the earth.

1.55.s:
etanminneva kāle tu hayamedhāya dīkṣitaḥ ..
tasmāttu prārthayadrājandehi mahyaṃ kramatrayam .. 19 ..
1.55.d:
एतन्मिन्नेव काले तु हयमेधाय दीक्षितः ॥
तस्मात्तु प्रार्थयद्राजन्देहि मह्यं क्रमत्रयम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.55.m: At that very time, [Bali] consecrated for the horse-sacrifice; / from him, O king, he requested: "Grant me three strides!"

1.55.s:
evamuktastu devena balirdaityagaṇādhipaḥ ..
pradadāvudakaṃ tasya pāvayasveti cābravīt .. 1.55.20 ..
1.55.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु देवेन बलिर्दैत्यगणाधिपः ॥
प्रददावुदकं तस्य पावयस्वेति चाब्रवीत् ॥ 1.55.20 ॥
1.55.m: Addressed thus by the god, Bali, the lord of the hosts of Daityas, / gave water to him and said: "Purify [me]!

1.55.s:
anyacca yadabhīṣṭaṃ te tadgṛhāṇa dvijottama ..
pratijagrāha ca jalaṃ pravātyeva tadā hariḥ .. 21 ..
1.55.d:
अन्यच्च यदभीष्टं ते तद्गृहाण द्विजोत्तम ॥
प्रतिजग्राह च जलं प्रवात्येव तदा हरिः ॥ 21 ॥
1.55.m: And whatever else is desired by you, take that, O foremost of the twice-born!" / And Hari accepted the water as it flowed then.

1.55.s:
udaṅmukherdaityavarairvīkṣyamāṇa ivāmbudaḥ ..
ākramattu harirlokāndānavāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ .. 22 ..
1.55.d:
उदङ्मुखेर्दैत्यवरैर्वीक्ष्यमाण इवाम्बुदः ॥
आक्रमत्तु हरिर्लोकान्दानवाः शस्त्रपाणयः ॥ 22 ॥
1.55.m: Watched by the foremost Daityas facing north like a cloud [in the sky], / Hari strode over the worlds, [while] the Dānavas with weapons in hand,

1.55.s:
abhidravanti vegena nānavaktraśirodharāḥ ..
garuḍānanāḥ khaḍgamukhā mayūravadanāstathā .. 23 ..
1.55.d:
अभिद्रवन्ति वेगेन नानवक्त्रशिरोधराः ॥
गरुडाननाः खड्गमुखा मयूरवदनास्तथा ॥ 23 ॥
1.55.m: with diverse faces and necks, rushed forward with speed: / some with faces of Garuḍas, with sword-like mouths, and with peacock faces;

1.55.s:
ghorā makaravaktrāśca kroṣṭuvaktrāśca dānavā. ..
ākhudarduravaktrāśca ghora vṛkamukhāstathā .. 24 ..
1.55.d:
घोरा मकरवक्त्राश्च क्रोष्टुवक्त्राश्च दानवा॥।
आखुदर्दुरवक्त्राश्च घोर वृकमुखास्तथा ॥ 24 ॥
1.55.m: and terrible Dānavas with crocodile faces and jackal faces, / with rat and frog faces, and terrible wolf faces;

1.55.s:
mārjāraśaśavaktrāśca haṃsakākānanāstathā ..
godhāśalyakavaktrāśca ajāvimahiṣānanāḥ .. 26 ..
1.55.d:
मार्जारशशवक्त्राश्च हंसकाकाननास्तथा ॥
गोधाशल्यकवक्त्राश्च अजाविमहिषाननाः ॥ 26 ॥
1.55.m: with faces of cats and hares, and faces of swans and crows, / with faces of monitor lizards and porcupines, and faces of goats, sheep, and buffaloes;

1.55.s:
siṃhavyāghraśṛgālānāṃ dvīpivānarapakṣiṇām ..
hastyaśvagokharoṣṭrāṇāṃ bhujagānāṃ samānanāḥ .. 26..
1.55.d:
सिंहव्याघ्रशृगालानां द्वीपिवानरपक्षिणाम् ॥
हस्त्यश्वगोखरोष्ट्राणां भुजगानां समाननाः ॥ 26॥
1.55.m: having faces resembling lions, tigers, and jackals; leopards, monkeys, and birds; / elephants, horses, cattle, donkeys, and camels; and serpents.

1.55.s:
pratigrahajalaṃ prāpya vyavardhata tadā hariḥ ..
udaṅmukhairdevagaṇairīkṣyamāṇa ivāmbudaḥ .. 27 ..
1.55.d:
प्रतिग्रहजलं प्राप्य व्यवर्धत तदा हरिः ॥
उदङ्मुखैर्देवगणैरीक्ष्यमाण इवाम्बुदः ॥ 27 ॥
1.55.m: Having received the water of acceptance, Hari then expanded, / like a cloud watched by the hosts of gods facing north.

1.55.s:
vikramantaṃ hariṃ lokāndānavāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ ..
matsyakacchapavaktrāṇāṃ dardurāṇāṃ samānanāḥ .. 28 ..
1.55.d:
विक्रमन्तं हरिं लोकान्दानवाः शस्त्रपाणयः ॥
मत्स्यकच्छपवक्त्राणां दर्दुराणां समाननाः ॥ 28 ॥
1.55.m: As Hari strode across the worlds, the Dānavas, weapons in hand, / having faces like those of fish, tortoises, and frogs,

1.55.s:
sthūladantā vivṛttākṣā lamboṣṭhajaṭharāstathā ..
piṅgalākṣo vivṛttāsyā nānābāhuśirodharāḥ .. 29 ..
1.55.d:
स्थूलदन्ता विवृत्ताक्षा लम्बोष्ठजठरास्तथा ॥
पिङ्गलाक्षो विवृत्तास्या नानाबाहुशिरोधराः ॥ 29 ॥
1.55.m: with large teeth, rolled-back eyes, pendulous lips and bellies, / reddish-brown eyes, wide-open mouths, and diverse arms and necks,

1.55.s:
sthūlāgranāsāścipiṭā mahāhanukapālinaḥ ..
cīnāṃśukottarāsaṃgāḥ kecitkṛṣṇājināmbarāḥ .. 1.55.30 ..
1.55.d:
स्थूलाग्रनासाश्चिपिटा महाहनुकपालिनः ॥
चीनांशुकोत्तरासंगाः केचित्कृष्णाजिनाम्बराः ॥ 1.55.30 ॥
1.55.m: with broad-tipped, flat noses, large jaws and skulls, / some wearing upper garments of Chinese silk, some clad in black antelope skins,

1.55.s:
bhujaṅgābharaṇāścānye kecinmukuṭabhūṣitāḥ ..
sakuṇḍalāḥ sakaṭakāḥ saśirastrāṇamastakāḥ .. 31 ..
1.55.d:
भुजङ्गाभरणाश्चान्ये केचिन्मुकुटभूषिताः ॥
सकुण्डलाः सकटकाः सशिरस्त्राणमस्तकाः ॥ 31 ॥
1.55.m: others with serpent ornaments, some adorned with diadems, / wearing earrings, bracelets, and helmets on their heads,

1.55.s:
dhanurbāṇadharāścā'nye tathā tomarapāṇayaḥ ..
khaḍgacarmadharāścā'nye tathā parighapāṇayaḥ .. 32 ..
1.55.d:
धनुर्बाणधराश्चाऽन्ये तथा तोमरपाणयः ॥
खड्गचर्मधराश्चाऽन्ये तथा परिघपाणयः ॥ 32 ॥
1.55.m: others carrying bows and arrows, as well as javelins in hand, / others bearing swords and shields, as well as iron bars in hand,

1.55.s:
śataghnīcakrahastāśca gadāmuśalapāṇayaḥ ..
aśmayantrāyudhopetā bhiṇḍipālāyudhāstathā .. 33 ..
1.55.d:
शतघ्नीचक्रहस्ताश्च गदामुशलपाणयः ॥
अश्मयन्त्रायुधोपेता भिण्डिपालायुधास्तथा ॥ 33 ॥
1.55.m: holding hundred-killers and discuses in their hands, clubs and pestles in hand, / equipped with stone-throwing catapults as weapons, and slings as weapons,

1.55.s:
śūlolūkhalahastāśca paraśvadhadharāstathā ..
mahāvṛkṣapravahaṇā mahāparvatayodhinaḥ .. 34 ..
1.55.d:
शूलोलूखलहस्ताश्च परश्वधधरास्तथा ॥
महावृक्षप्रवहणा महापर्वतयोधिनः ॥ 34 ॥
1.55.m: holding spears and pestles in their hands, and bearing battle-axes, / carrying great trees, warriors fighting with huge mountains,

1.55.s:
kramamāṇaṃ hṛṣīkeśamupāvarttanta sarvaśaḥ ..
sa tānmamarda sarvātmā tanmukhāndaityadānavān .. 35 ..
1.55.d:
क्रममाणं हृषीकेशमुपावर्त्तन्त सर्वशः ॥
स तान्ममर्द सर्वात्मा तन्मुखान्दैत्यदानवान् ॥ 35 ॥
1.55.m: approached Hṛṣīkeśa from all sides as he strode. / He, the self of all, crushed those Daityas and Dānavas having those faces,

1.55.s:
sarasīva mahāpadmānmahāhastīva dānavān ..
pramathya sarvāndaiteyānhastapādatalaistataḥ ..36 ..
1.55.d:
सरसीव महापद्मान्महाहस्तीव दानवान् ॥
प्रमथ्य सर्वान्दैतेयान्हस्तपादतलैस्ततः ॥36 ॥
1.55.m: like a great elephant crushing large lotuses in a lake. / Having crushed all the Daiteyas with the soles of his hands and feet,

1.55.s:
rūpaṃ kṛtvā mahābhīmamājahārā''śu medinīm..
tasya vikramato bhūmiṃ candrādityau stanāntare .. 37 ..
1.55.d:
रूपं कृत्वा महाभीममाजहारा'ऽशु मेदिनीम्॥
तस्य विक्रमतो भूमिं चन्द्रादित्यौ स्तनान्तरे ॥ 37 ॥
1.55.m: and assuming an immensely terrifying form, he swiftly seized the earth. / As he strode over the earth, the moon and the sun were between his breasts;

1.55.s:
paraṃ prakramamāṇasya nābhideśe vyavasthitau ..
tataḥ prakramamāṇasya jānudeśe vyavasthitau .. 38 ..
1.55.d:
परं प्रक्रममाणस्य नाभिदेशे व्यवस्थितौ ॥
ततः प्रक्रममाणस्य जानुदेशे व्यवस्थितौ ॥ 38 ॥
1.55.m: as he strode further, the two were situated at his navel; / then as he strode onward, the two were situated at his knees;

1.55.s:
tatopi kramamāṇasya padbhyāṃ devau vyavasthitau ..
jitvā sa medinīṃ kṛtsnāṃ hatvā cāsurapuṃgavān .. 39 ..
1.55.d:
ततोपि क्रममाणस्य पद्भ्यां देवौ व्यवस्थितौ ॥
जित्वा स मेदिनीं कृत्स्नां हत्वा चासुरपुंगवान् ॥ 39 ॥
1.55.m: and as he strode still further, the two gods were situated at his feet. / Having conquered the entire earth and slain the foremost of the asuras,

1.55.s:
dadau śakrāya vasudhāṃ viṣṇurbalavatāṃ varaḥ ..
svaṃ rūpañca tathā''sādya dānavendramabhāṣata .. 1.55.40 ..
1.55.d:
ददौ शक्राय वसुधां विष्णुर्बलवतां वरः ॥
स्वं रूपञ्च तथा'ऽसाद्य दानवेन्द्रमभाषत ॥ 1.55.40 ॥
1.55.m: Viṣṇu, the foremost among the strong, gave the earth to Śakra; / and resuming his own form, he addressed the lord of the Dānavas:

1.55.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
yajñavāṭaṃ tvadīye'sminsāligrāme mahāsura ..
mayā niviṣṭapādena māpiteyaṃ vasundharā .. 41 ..
1.55.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
यज्ञवाटं त्वदीयेऽस्मिन्सालिग्रामे महासुर ॥
मया निविष्टपादेन मापितेयं वसुन्धरा ॥ 41 ॥
1.55.m: The holy Lord said: / In this sacrificial enclosure of yours at Śāligrāma, O great asura, / this earth has been measured by me with placed feet.

1.55.s:
prathamaṃ tu padaṃ jātaṃ naurbandhaśikhare mama ..
dvitīyaṃ meruśikhare tṛtīyaṃ nā'bhavatkvacit .. 42 ..
1.55.d:
प्रथमं तु पदं जातं नौर्बन्धशिखरे मम ॥
द्वितीयं मेरुशिखरे तृतीयं नाऽभवत्क्वचित् ॥ 42 ॥
1.55.m: My first step was placed on the peak of Naubandha; / the second on the peak of Meru; the third could find no place at all.

1.55.s:
tanme varaya daityendra yanmayāptaṃ pratigraham..
baliruvāca ..
yāvatī vasudhā deva tvayaiva parinirmitā .. 43 ..
1.55.d:
तन्मे वरय दैत्येन्द्र यन्मयाप्तं प्रतिग्रहम्॥
बलिरुवाच ॥
यावती वसुधा देव त्वयैव परिनिर्मिता ॥ 43 ॥
1.55.m:
Therefore, O lord of Daityas, choose for me that which I obtained as acceptance of gifts.
Bali said:
As much as the earth is, O God, created by you alone,

1.55.s:
tāvatī te na saṃpūrṇā devadeva kramatrayam ..
na kṛtaṃ yattvayā deva kutastanme maheśvara .. 44 ..
1.55.d:
तावती ते न संपूर्णा देवदेव क्रमत्रयम् ॥
न कृतं यत्त्वया देव कुतस्तन्मे महेश्वर ॥ 44 ॥
1.55.m: so much, O God of gods, was not sufficient for your three paces. / Since that was not done by you, O God, whence can it come from me, O Maheśvara?

1.55.s:
na ca tadvidyate deva tathaivā'nyasya kasyacit ..
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
na me tvayāpūryate me dānavendra yathāśrutam .. 45 ..
1.55.d:
न च तद्विद्यते देव तथैवाऽन्यस्य कस्यचित् ॥
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
न मे त्वयापूर्यते मे दानवेन्द्र यथाश्रुतम् ॥ 45 ॥
1.55.m:
Nor does it exist, O God, for anyone else in that way.
The Holy One said:
My [vow] has not been fulfilled by you, O lord of Dānavas, as promised.

1.55.s:
sutalaṃ nāma pātālaṃ vasa tatra susaṃyataḥ ..
mayaiva nirmitā tatra manasā śobhanā purī ..46..
1.55.d:
सुतलं नाम पातालं वस तत्र सुसंयतः ॥
मयैव निर्मिता तत्र मनसा शोभना पुरी ॥46॥
1.55.m: There is a subterranean realm named Sutala; dwell there with utmost self-restraint. / There I myself, by my mind, have fashioned a splendid city.

1.55.s:
jñātibhiḥ sahadharmiṣṭhairvasa tatra yathāsukham..
tatra tvaṃ bhokṣyase bhogānviśiṣṭānbalasūdanāt ..47..
1.55.d:
ज्ञातिभिः सहधर्मिष्ठैर्वस तत्र यथासुखम्॥
तत्र त्वं भोक्ष्यसे भोगान्विशिष्टान्बलसूदनात् ॥47॥
1.55.m: Dwell there in comfort together with your righteous kinsmen. / There you shall enjoy pleasures superior to [those of] the Slayer of Bala.

1.55.s:
avāpsyasi tathā bhogām̐lokādvidhivivarjitān..
prākāmyayuktaśca tathā lokeṣu vihariṣyasi ..48..
1.55.d:
अवाप्स्यसि तथा भोगाम्̐लोकाद्विधिविवर्जितान्॥
प्राकाम्ययुक्तश्च तथा लोकेषु विहरिष्यसि ॥48॥
1.55.m: You shall also obtain pleasures from the world that are exempt from ritual rules; / and endowed with irresistible will, you shall wander through the worlds.

1.55.s:
manvantare dvitīye ca mahendratvaṃ kariṣyasi ..
tejasā ca madīyena śakratve yokṣyase bale .. 49 ..
1.55.d:
मन्वन्तरे द्वितीये च महेन्द्रत्वं करिष्यसि ॥
तेजसा च मदीयेन शक्रत्वे योक्ष्यसे बले ॥ 49 ॥
1.55.m: And in the second Manu-period you shall exercise the sovereignty of Mahendra; / and by my splendor you will be endowed with the state of Śakra, O Bali.

1.55.s:
tava śatrugaṇānsarvānghātayiṣyāmyahaṃ tadā ..
brahmaṇyastvaṃ śaraṇyastvaṃ yajñaśīlaḥ priyaṃvadaḥ .. 1.55.50 ..
1.55.d:
तव शत्रुगणान्सर्वान्घातयिष्याम्यहं तदा ॥
ब्रह्मण्यस्त्वं शरण्यस्त्वं यज्ञशीलः प्रियंवदः ॥ 1.55.50 ॥
1.55.m: At that time I will slay all your hosts of enemies. / You are devoted to brahmins, a refuge [for others], observant of sacrifice, sweet-spoken,

1.55.s:
tapasvī dānaśīlaśca vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ ..
tasmādyaśobhivṛddhyarthaṃ mayā tvamabhisandhitaḥ .. 51 ..
1.55.d:
तपस्वी दानशीलश्च वेदवेदांगपारगः ॥
तस्माद्यशोभिवृद्ध्यर्थं मया त्वमभिसन्धितः ॥ 51 ॥
1.55.m: an ascetic, generous, and one who has mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. / Therefore, for the increase of your fame, you have been thus addressed by me.

1.55.s:
devarājādhikānbhogānpātālastho'pi bhokṣyase ..
sannidhānaśca tatrāhaṃ kariṣyāmyasurādhipa ..52..
1.55.d:
देवराजाधिकान्भोगान्पातालस्थोऽपि भोक्ष्यसे ॥
सन्निधानश्च तत्राहं करिष्याम्यसुराधिप ॥52॥
1.55.m: Even while residing in the underworld, you will enjoy pleasures surpassing those of the king of gods. / And I will maintain my presence there, O ruler of Asuras.

1.55.s:
mayā ca raṃsyase sārdhaṃ spṛhaṇīyaḥ surairapi..
śakratvaṃ ca tathā kṛtvā bhāvye sāvarṇike'ntare .. 53 ..
1.55.d:
मया च रंस्यसे सार्धं स्पृहणीयः सुरैरपि॥
शक्रत्वं च तथा कृत्वा भाव्ये सावर्णिकेऽन्तरे ॥ 53 ॥
1.55.m: And you shall take delight with me, an object of longing even for the gods. / And having exercised the state of Śakra in the future Sāvarṇi Manu-period,

1.55.s: sarvasaṃdhivinirmukto mayaiva saha raṃsyase ..54..
1.55.d: सर्वसंधिविनिर्मुक्तो मयैव सह रंस्यसे ॥54॥
1.55.m: freed from all bonds, you will take delight with me alone.

1.55.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
ityevamuktvā sajalāmbudābhaḥ prataptacāmīkaradhautavastraḥ ..
adarśanaṃ devavaro jagāma śakraśca lebhe sakalāṃ trilokīm .. 55 ..
1.55.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा सजलाम्बुदाभः प्रतप्तचामीकरधौतवस्त्रः ॥
अदर्शनं देववरो जगाम शक्रश्च लेभे सकलां त्रिलोकीम् ॥ 55 ॥
1.55.m:
Śaṅkara said:
Having spoken thus, [the Lord], radiant as a water-laden cloud, clothed in washed garments of purified gold, / the foremost of gods vanished from sight; and Śakra obtained the entire threefold world.

1.56.s:
rāma uvāca ..
tasya devātidevasya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ ..
tvatto'haṃ śrotumicchāmi divyā ātmavibhūtayaḥ .. 1 ..
1.56.d:
राम उवाच ॥
तस्य देवातिदेवस्य विष्णोरमिततेजसः ॥
त्वत्तोऽहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि दिव्या आत्मविभूतयः ॥ 1 ॥
1.56.m:
Rāma said:
I wish to hear from you the divine manifestations of the self / belonging to that God of gods, Viṣṇu of boundless splendor.

1.56.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
na śakyā vistarādvaktuṃ devadevasya bhūtayaḥ ..
prādhānyataste vakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā dvija ..2 ..
1.56.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
न शक्या विस्तराद्वक्तुं देवदेवस्य भूतयः ॥
प्राधान्यतस्ते वक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमना द्विज ॥2 ॥
1.56.m:
Śaṅkara said:
The manifestations of the God of gods cannot be described in full detail. / I will tell them to you by their preeminence; listen with a single-minded focus, O twice-born.

1.56.s:
sarge brahmā sthitau viṣṇuḥ saṃhāre ca tathā haraḥ ..
varuṇo vāyurākāśo jyotiśca pṛthivī tathā .. 3 ..
1.56.d:
सर्गे ब्रह्मा स्थितौ विष्णुः संहारे च तथा हरः ॥
वरुणो वायुराकाशो ज्योतिश्च पृथिवी तथा ॥ 3 ॥
1.56.m: In creation [he is] Brahmā, in preservation Viṣṇu, and in destruction Hara; / he is Varuṇa, Vāyu, ether, light, and also the earth;

1.56.s:
diśaśca vidiśaścā'pi tathā ye ca digīśvarāḥ ..
ādityā vasavo rudrā bhṛgavoṃ'girasastathā .. 4 ..
1.56.d:
दिशश्च विदिशश्चाऽपि तथा ये च दिगीश्वराः ॥
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा भृगवोंऽगिरसस्तथा ॥ 4 ॥
1.56.m: and the cardinal directions, intermediate directions, and those who are lords of the directions; / the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases;

1.56.s:
sādhyāśca maruto devā viśvedevāstathaiva ca ..
aśvinau puruhūtaśca gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 5 ..
1.56.d:
साध्याश्च मरुतो देवा विश्वेदेवास्तथैव च ॥
अश्विनौ पुरुहूतश्च गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ॥ 5 ॥
1.56.m: and the Sādhyas, the Maruts, the Viśvedevas; / the two Aśvins, Puruhūta, and the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases;

1.56.s:
parvatodadhipātālā lokā dvīpāśca bhārgava ..
tiryagūrdhvamadhaścaiva tviṅgitaṃ yaśca neṅgate .. 6 ..
1.56.d:
पर्वतोदधिपाताला लोका द्वीपाश्च भार्गव ॥
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव त्विङ्गितं यश्च नेङ्गते ॥ 6 ॥
1.56.m: mountains, oceans, subterranean realms, worlds, and islands, O Bhārgava; / whatever is horizontal, above, or below, that which moves and that which does not move;

1.56.s:
saccā'sacca mahābhāga prakṛtirvikṛtiśca yaḥ ..
kṛmikīṭapataṅgānāṃ vayasāṃ yonayastathā .. 7 ..
1.56.d:
सच्चाऽसच्च महाभाग प्रकृतिर्विकृतिश्च यः ॥
कृमिकीटपतङ्गानां वयसां योनयस्तथा ॥ 7 ॥
1.56.m: the real and the unreal, O fortunate one, Prakṛti and Vikṛti; / the wombs of worms, insects, winged creatures, and birds;

1.56.s:
vidyādharāstathā yakṣā nāgāḥ sarpāḥ sakinnarāḥ ..
rākṣasāśca piśācāśca pitaraḥ kālasaṃdhayaḥ . .8 ..
1.56.d:
विद्याधरास्तथा यक्षा नागाः सर्पाः सकिन्नराः ॥
राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च पितरः कालसंधयः ॥8 ॥
1.56.m: Vidyādharas, Yakṣas, Nāgas, snakes with Kinnaras, / Rākṣasas, Piśācas, the ancestors, and the junctures of time;

1.56.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣāśca dharmadvārāṇi yāni ca ..
yajñāṅgāni ca sarvāṇi bhūtagrāmaṃ caturvidham..9..
1.56.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाश्च धर्मद्वाराणि यानि च ॥
यज्ञाङ्गानि च सर्वाणि भूतग्रामं चतुर्विधम्॥9॥
1.56.m: dharma, wealth, pleasure, liberation, and the gateways of dharma; / all the constituents of sacrifice, and the fourfold assemblage of beings:

1.56.s:
jarāyujāṇḍajāścaiva saṃsvedajamathodbhijam ..
ekajyotiḥ sa marutāṃ vasūnāṃ sa ca pāvakaḥ..1.56.1 0..
1.56.d:
जरायुजाण्डजाश्चैव संस्वेदजमथोद्भिजम् ॥
एकज्योतिः स मरुतां वसूनां स च पावकः॥1.56.1 0॥
1.56.m: the womb-born, egg-born, sweat-born, and sprout-born. / He is Ekajyotis among the Maruts, and he is Fire among the Vasus;

1.56.s:
ahirbudhnyaśca rudrāṇāṃ nādaivāśvinayostathā ..
nārāyaṇaśca sādhyānāṃ bhṛgūṇāñca tathā kratuḥ ..11..
1.56.d:
अहिर्बुध्न्यश्च रुद्राणां नादैवाश्विनयोस्तथा ॥
नारायणश्च साध्यानां भृगूणाञ्च तथा क्रतुः ॥11॥
1.56.m: he is Ahirbudhnya among the Rudras, and Nāsatya among the two Aśvins; / Nārāyaṇa among the Sādhyas, and Kratu among the Bhṛgus;

1.56.s:
ādityānāṃ tathā viṣṇurāyuraṅgirasāṃ tathā ..
viśveṣāñcaiva devānāṃ rocamānaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ ..12..
1.56.d:
आदित्यानां तथा विष्णुरायुरङ्गिरसां तथा ॥
विश्वेषाञ्चैव देवानां रोचमानः स कीर्तितः ॥12॥
1.56.m: Viṣṇu among the Ādityas, and Āyus among the Aṅgirases; / and he is declared Rocamāna among all the gods;

1.56.s:
vāsavaḥ sarvadevānāṃ jyotiṣāṃ ca hutāśanaḥ ..
yamaḥ saṃyamaśīlānāṃ virūpākṣaḥ kṣamābhṛtām .. 13 ..
1.56.d:
वासवः सर्वदेवानां ज्योतिषां च हुताशनः ॥
यमः संयमशीलानां विरूपाक्षः क्षमाभृताम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.56.m: Vāsava among all the deities, and Fire among luminous bodies; / Yama among those of restrained nature, Virūpākṣa among the supporters of the earth;

1.56.s:
yādasāṃ varuṇaścaiva pavanaḥ plavatāṃ tathā ..
dhanādhyakṣaśca yakṣāṇāṃ rudro raudrastathāntaraḥ .. 14 ..
1.56.d:
यादसां वरुणश्चैव पवनः प्लवतां तथा ॥
धनाध्यक्षश्च यक्षाणां रुद्रो रौद्रस्तथान्तरः ॥ 14 ॥
1.56.m: Varuṇa among aquatic creatures, and the Wind among those that move; / Kubera among the Yakṣas, Rudra the terrible among those within;

1.56.s:
anantaḥ sarvanāgānāṃ sūryastejasvināṃ tathā ..
grahāṇāñca tathā candro nakṣatrāṇāñca kṛttikā .. 15 ..
1.56.d:
अनन्तः सर्वनागानां सूर्यस्तेजस्विनां तथा ॥
ग्रहाणाञ्च तथा चन्द्रो नक्षत्राणाञ्च कृत्तिका ॥ 15 ॥
1.56.m: Ananta among all Nāgas, the Sun among luminous entities; / the Moon among planets, and Kṛttikā among lunar mansions;

1.56.s:
kālaḥ kalayatāṃ śreṣṭho yugānāṃ ca kṛtaṃ yugam ..
kalpaṃ manvantareśāśca manavaśca caturdaśa .. 16 ..
1.56.d:
कालः कलयतां श्रेष्ठो युगानां च कृतं युगम् ॥
कल्पं मन्वन्तरेशाश्च मनवश्च चतुर्दश ॥ 16 ॥
1.56.m: Time, the highest among reckoning forces, and the Kṛta age among ages; / an aeon, the lords of Manu-periods, and the fourteen Manus;

1.56.s:
sa eva devaḥ sarvātmā ye ca deveśvarāstathā ..
saṃvatsarastu varṣāṇāṃ cāyanānāṃ tathottaraḥ .. 17 ..
1.56.d:
स एव देवः सर्वात्मा ये च देवेश्वरास्तथा ॥
संवत्सरस्तु वर्षाणां चायनानां तथोत्तरः ॥ 17 ॥
1.56.m: he is that God who is the Self of all, and those who are lords of the gods; / the year among years, and the northern course among solstices;

1.56.s:
mārgaśīrṣastu māsānāṃ ṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ ..
śuklapakṣastu pakṣāṇāṃ tithīnāṃ pūrṇimā tithiḥ ...18..
1.56.d:
मार्गशीर्षस्तु मासानां ऋतूनां कुसुमाकरः ॥
शुक्लपक्षस्तु पक्षाणां तिथीनां पूर्णिमा तिथिः ॥.18॥
1.56.m: Mārgaśīrṣa among months, and spring among seasons; / the bright fortnight among fortnights, and the full moon among lunar days;

1.56.s:
kāraṇānāṃ vadhaḥ prokto muhūrttānāṃ tathā'bhijit ..
pātālānāṃ sutalaśca samudrāṇāṃ payodadhiḥ .. 19 ..
1.56.d:
कारणानां वधः प्रोक्तो मुहूर्त्तानां तथाऽभिजित् ॥
पातालानां सुतलश्च समुद्राणां पयोदधिः ॥ 19 ॥
1.56.m: Vadha is proclaimed among instruments, and Abhijit among muhūrtas; / Sutala among subterranean realms, and the ocean of milk among seas;

1.56.s:
jambūdvīpaśca dvīpānāṃ lokānāṃ satya ucyate ..
meruḥ śiloccayānāṃ ca varṣeṣvapi ca bhāratam .. 1.56.20 ...
1.56.d:
जम्बूद्वीपश्च द्वीपानां लोकानां सत्य उच्यते ॥
मेरुः शिलोच्चयानां च वर्षेष्वपि च भारतम् ॥ 1.56.20 ॥।
1.56.m: Jambūdvīpa among islands, and Satyaloka among worlds; / Meru among mountain ranges, and Bhārata among regions;

1.56.s:
himālayaḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ jāhnavī saritāṃ tathā ..
puṣkaraḥ sarvatīrthānāṃ garuḍaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ tathā .. 21 ..
1.56.d:
हिमालयः स्थावराणां जाह्नवी सरितां तथा ॥
पुष्करः सर्वतीर्थानां गरुडः पक्षिणां तथा ॥ 21 ॥
1.56.m: the Himālaya among immovable things, and the Gaṅgā among rivers; / Puṣkara among all sacred bathing places, and Garuḍa among birds;

1.56.s:
gandharvāṇāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ..
ṛṣīṇāñca bhṛgurdevo devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ ..22..
1.56.d:
गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथः सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः॥
ऋषीणाञ्च भृगुर्देवो देवर्षीणां च नारदः ॥22॥
1.56.m: Citraratha among Gandharvas, Kapila the sage among perfected beings; / the divine Bhṛgu among ṛṣis, and Nārada among celestial sages;

1.56.s:
tathā brahmaṛṣīṇāñca aṃgirāḥ parikīrtitaḥ ..
vidyādharāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ devaścitrāṃgadastathā ..23..
1.56.d:
तथा ब्रह्मऋषीणाञ्च अंगिराः परिकीर्तितः ॥
विद्याधराणां सर्वेषां देवश्चित्रांगदस्तथा ॥23॥
1.56.m: and Aṅgiras is declared among divine sages; / among all Vidyādharas, the god Citrāṅgada;

1.56.s:
kaṃbaraḥ kinnarāṇāṃ ca sarpāṇāmatha vāsukiḥ ..
prahrādaḥ sarvadaityānāṃ rambhā cāpsarasāṃ tathā .. 24 ..
1.56.d:
कंबरः किन्नराणां च सर्पाणामथ वासुकिः ॥
प्रह्रादः सर्वदैत्यानां रम्भा चाप्सरसां तथा ॥ 24 ॥
1.56.m: Kambara among Kinnaras, and Vāsuki among snakes; / Prahrāda among all Daityas, and Rambhā among Apsarases;

1.56.s:
uccaiḥśravasamaśvānāṃ dhenūnāṃ caiva kāmadhuk ..
airāvato gajendrāṇāṃ mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgādhipaḥ .. 25 ..
1.56.d:
उच्चैःश्रवसमश्वानां धेनूनां चैव कामधुक् ॥
ऐरावतो गजेन्द्राणां मृगाणां च मृगाधिपः ॥ 25 ॥
1.56.m: Uccaiḥśravas among horses, and Kāmadhenu among cows; / Airāvata among lordly elephants, and the lion among beasts;

1.56.s:
āyudhānāṃ tathā vajro narāṇāñca narādhipaḥ ..
kṣamā kṣamāvatāṃ devo buddhirbuddhimatāmapi .. 26 ..
1.56.d:
आयुधानां तथा वज्रो नराणाञ्च नराधिपः ॥
क्षमा क्षमावतां देवो बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामपि ॥ 26 ॥
1.56.m: the thunderbolt among weapons, and the king among men; / forgiveness, the divine, among the forgiving, and intellect among the intelligent;

1.56.s:
dharmāviruddhaḥ kāmaśca tathā dharmabhṛtāṃ nṛṇām ..
dharmmo dharmabhṛtāṃ devastapaścaiva tapasvinām..27..
1.56.d:
धर्माविरुद्धः कामश्च तथा धर्मभृतां नृणाम् ॥
धर्म्मो धर्मभृतां देवस्तपश्चैव तपस्विनाम्॥27॥
1.56.m: desire not opposed to dharma among men who uphold dharma; / dharma among upholders of dharma, the divine, and asceticism among ascetics;

1.56.s:
yajñānāṃ japayajñaśca satyaḥ satyavatāṃ tathā ..
vedānāṃ sāmā vedaśca aṃśūnāṃ jyotiṣāṃ patiḥ .. 28..
1.56.d:
यज्ञानां जपयज्ञश्च सत्यः सत्यवतां तथा ॥
वेदानां सामा वेदश्च अंशूनां ज्योतिषां पतिः ॥ 28॥
1.56.m: the sacrifice of recitation among sacrifices, and truth among the truthful; / the Sāmaveda among Vedas, and the lord of lights among radiant beings;

1.56.s:
gāyatrī sarvamaṃtrāṇāṃ vācaḥ pravadatāṃ tathā ..
akṣarāṇāmakāraśca yantrāṇāñca tathā dhanuḥ..29..
1.56.d:
गायत्री सर्वमंत्राणां वाचः प्रवदतां तथा ॥
अक्षराणामकारश्च यन्त्राणाञ्च तथा धनुः॥29॥
1.56.m: Gāyatrī among all mantras, and speech among speakers; / the letter 'a' among syllables, and the bow among weapons.

1.56.s:
adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṃ kavīnāmuśanā kaviḥ ..
cetanā sarvabhūtānāmindriyāṇāṃ manastathā .. 1.56.30 ..
1.56.d:
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां कवीनामुशना कविः ॥
चेतना सर्वभूतानामिन्द्रियाणां मनस्तथा ॥ 1.56.30 ॥
1.56.m: Among sciences [I am] the science of the inner self; among poets, the poet Uśanas. / [I am] the consciousness of all beings, and likewise the mind among the senses.

1.56.s:
brahmā brahmavidāṃ devo jñānaṃ jñānavatāṃ tathā ..
kīrtiḥ śrīrvāk ca nārīṇāṃ smṛtirmedhā tathā kṣamā .. 31 ..
1.56.d:
ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मविदां देवो ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतां तथा ॥
कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक् च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा तथा क्षमा ॥ 31 ॥
1.56.m: Among knowers of the Brahman [I am] the god Brahmā; and knowledge among the knowledgeable. / Among women [I am] fame, fortune, speech, memory, intellect, and patience.

1.56.s:
āśramāṇāṃ caturthaśca varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇastathā ..
skandaḥ senāpraṇetṝṇāṃ sadayaśca dayā vatām .. 32 ..
1.56.d:
आश्रमाणां चतुर्थश्च वर्णानां ब्राह्मणस्तथा ॥
स्कन्दः सेनाप्रणेतॄणां सदयश्च दया वताम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.56.m: Among the stages of life [I am] the fourth; and among castes, the brahmin. / Among commanders of armies [I am] Skanda; and the compassionate among those who have compassion.

1.56.s:
jayaśca vyavasāyaśca tathotsāhavatāṃ prabhuḥ ..
aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāmoṣadhīnāṃ tathā yavaḥ .. 33 ..
1.56.d:
जयश्च व्यवसायश्च तथोत्साहवतां प्रभुः ॥
अश्वत्थः सर्ववृक्षाणामोषधीनां तथा यवः ॥ 33 ॥
1.56.m: I am victory, resolve, and the lord of the energetic. / Among all trees [I am] the sacred fig tree; and barley among plants.

1.56.s:
mṛtyuḥ sa eva mriyatāmudbhavaśca bhaviṣyatām ..
jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraścaiva dyūtaṃ chalayatāṃ tathā .. 34 ..
1.56.d:
मृत्युः स एव म्रियतामुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् ॥
झषाणां मकरश्चैव द्यूतं छलयतां तथा ॥ 34 ॥
1.56.m: He alone is death for those who die, and origin for those yet to be. / Among aquatic monsters [I am] the makara; and dice among cheats.

1.56.s:
mānaśca sarvaguhyānāṃ ratnānāṃ kanakaṃ tathā ..
dhṛtirbhūmau rasastejastejaścaiva hutāśane .. 35 ..
1.56.d:
मानश्च सर्वगुह्यानां रत्नानां कनकं तथा ॥
धृतिर्भूमौ रसस्तेजस्तेजश्चैव हुताशने ॥ 35 ॥
1.56.m: And silence among all secrets, and gold among gems. / [I am] firmness in the earth, taste [in water], and radiance in fire.

1.56.s:
vāyuḥ sparśaguṇānāṃ ca khañca śabdaguṇastathā ..
evaṃ vibhūtibhiḥ sarvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhati bhārgava .. 36 ..
1.56.d:
वायुः स्पर्शगुणानां च खञ्च शब्दगुणस्तथा ॥
एवं विभूतिभिः सर्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठति भार्गव ॥ 36 ॥
1.56.m: [I am] wind among the qualities of touch, and ether among the quality of sound. / Pervading everything thus with his divine powers, O Bhārgava, he remains.

1.56.s:
ekāṃśena bhṛguśreṣṭha tasyāṃśatritayaṃ divi ..
devāśca ṛṣayaścaiva brahmā cā'haṃ ca bhārgava .. 37 ..
1.56.d:
एकांशेन भृगुश्रेष्ठ तस्यांशत्रितयं दिवि ॥
देवाश्च ऋषयश्चैव ब्रह्मा चाऽहं च भार्गव ॥ 37 ॥
1.56.m: With one portion, O best of the Bhṛgus, [while] his three-portioned [nature] is in heaven. / The gods, the ṛṣis, Brahmā, and myself, O Bhārgava,

1.56.s:
cakṣuṣā yanna paśyaṃti vinā jñānagatiṃ dvija ..
jñātā jñeyastathā dhyātā dhyeyaścokto janārdanaḥ .. 38 ..
1.56.d:
चक्षुषा यन्न पश्यंति विना ज्ञानगतिं द्विज ॥
ज्ञाता ज्ञेयस्तथा ध्याता ध्येयश्चोक्तो जनार्दनः ॥ 38 ॥
1.56.m: do not see him with the physical eye without the path of knowledge, O twice-born. / Janārdana is declared to be the knower, the object of knowledge, the meditator, and the object of meditation.

1.56.s:
yajño yaṣṭā ca govindaḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetrajña eva ca ..
annamannāda evoktaḥ sa eva ca guṇatrayam .. 39 ..
1.56.d:
यज्ञो यष्टा च गोविन्दः क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञ एव च ॥
अन्नमन्नाद एवोक्तः स एव च गुणत्रयम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.56.m: Govinda is the sacrifice and the sacrificer, the field and the knower of the field. / He is declared to be the food and the eater of food, and he is the three qualities.

1.56.s:
gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayatyojasā vibhuḥ ..
puṣṇāti cauṣadhīḥ sarvā somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ .. 1.56.40 ..
1.56.d:
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयत्योजसा विभुः ॥
पुष्णाति चौषधीः सर्वा सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥ 1.56.40 ॥
1.56.m: Entering the earth, the all-pervading lord sustains living beings by his vigour; / and becoming the sap-rich moon, he nourishes all plants.

1.56.s:
prāṇināṃ jaṭharastho'gnirbhuktapācī sa bhārgava ..
ceṣṭākṛtprāṇināṃ brahmansa ca vāyuḥ śarīragaḥ .. 41 ..
1.56.d:
प्राणिनां जठरस्थोऽग्निर्भुक्तपाची स भार्गव ॥
चेष्टाकृत्प्राणिनां ब्रह्मन्स च वायुः शरीरगः ॥ 41 ॥
1.56.m: He is the fire in the belly of living beings that digests what is eaten, O Bhārgava; / and he is the bodily wind causing movement in living beings, O brahmin.

1.56.s:
yathādityagataṃ tejo jagadbhāsayate'khilam ..
yaccandramasi yaccā'gnau tattejastatra kīrtitam .. 42 ..
1.56.d:
यथादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् ॥
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाऽग्नौ तत्तेजस्तत्र कीर्तितम् ॥ 42 ॥
1.56.m: The splendour that, situated in the sun, illumines the entire universe, / and that which is in the moon and in fire—that splendour is proclaimed to be his.

1.56.s:
sarvasya cā'sau hṛdi sanniviṣṭastasmātsmṛtirjñānamapohanañca ..
sarvaiśca devaiśca sa eva vandyo vedāntakṛdvedakṛdeva cā'sau .. 43 ..
1.56.d:
सर्वस्य चाऽसौ हृदि सन्निविष्टस्तस्मात्स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनञ्च ॥
सर्वैश्च देवैश्च स एव वन्द्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदकृदेव चाऽसौ ॥ 43 ॥
1.56.m: He is seated in the heart of all: from him come memory, knowledge, and loss [of both]; / he alone is to be praised by all the gods, the maker of the Vedānta, and the maker of the Veda.

1.57.s:
.. rāma uvāca .. ..
ārādhyate sa bhagavānkarmaṇā yena śaṅkara ..
tatsamācakṣva bhagavansarvasattvasukhapradam .. 1 ..
1.57.d:
॥ राम उवाच ॥ ॥
आराध्यते स भगवान्कर्मणा येन शङ्कर ॥
तत्समाचक्ष्व भगवन्सर्वसत्त्वसुखप्रदम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.57.m: Rāma said: / By what rite is that Lord worshipped, O Śaṅkara? / Declare that, O Lord, which bestows happiness upon all beings.

1.57.s:
.. śaṅkara uvāca ..
sādhu rāma mahābhāga sādhu dānavanāśana ..
yanmāṃ pṛcchasi dharmajña keśavārādhanaṃ prati .. 2 ..
1.57.d:
॥ शङ्कर उवाच ॥
साधु राम महाभाग साधु दानवनाशन ॥
यन्मां पृच्छसि धर्मज्ञ केशवाराधनं प्रति ॥ 2 ॥
1.57.m: Śaṅkara said: / Well said, O fortunate Rāma, well said, O destroyer of Dānavas, / that you ask me, O knower of dharma, about the worship of Keśava!

1.57.s:
divasaṃ divasārdhaṃ vā muhūrttamekameva vā ..
nāśaścā'śeṣapāpasya bhaktirbhavati keśave .. 3 ..
1.57.d:
दिवसं दिवसार्धं वा मुहूर्त्तमेकमेव वा ॥
नाशश्चाऽशेषपापस्य भक्तिर्भवति केशवे ॥ 3 ॥
1.57.m: [Even for] a day, half a day, or a single muhūrta, / devotion toward Keśava is the destruction of all sins.

1.57.s:
anekajanmasāhasrairnānāyonyantareṣu ca ..
jantoḥ kalmaṣahīnasya bhaktirbhavati keśave .. .. 4 ..
1.57.d:
अनेकजन्मसाहस्रैर्नानायोन्यन्तरेषु च ॥
जन्तोः कल्मषहीनस्य भक्तिर्भवति केशवे ॥ ॥ 4 ॥
1.57.m: Through many thousands of births and in various wombs, / devotion toward Keśava arises in a living being free of sin.

1.57.s:
nā'dhanyaḥ keśavaṃ stauti nā'dhanyorcayati prabhum ..
namatyadhanyaśca hariṃ nā'dhanyo vetti mādhavam .. 5 ..
1.57.d:
नाऽधन्यः केशवं स्तौति नाऽधन्योर्चयति प्रभुम् ॥
नमत्यधन्यश्च हरिं नाऽधन्यो वेत्ति माधवम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.57.m: The unfortunate does not praise Keśava, the unfortunate does not worship the Lord, / the unfortunate bows not to Hari, nor does the unfortunate know Mādhava.

1.57.s:
manaśca taddhi dharmajña keśave yatpravartate ..
sā buddhistadvratāyaiva satataṃ pratitiṣṭhati .. 6 ..
1.57.d:
मनश्च तद्धि धर्मज्ञ केशवे यत्प्रवर्तते ॥
सा बुद्धिस्तद्व्रतायैव सततं प्रतितिष्ठति ॥ 6 ॥
1.57.m: That is indeed mind, O knower of dharma, which engages with Keśava; / that is intellect which remains constantly resolved upon vows unto him.

1.57.s:
sā vāṇī keśavaṃ devaṃ yā stauti bhṛgunandana ..
śravaṇau tau śrutā yābhyāṃ satataṃ tatkathāḥ śubhāḥ .. 7 ..
1.57.d:
सा वाणी केशवं देवं या स्तौति भृगुनन्दन ॥
श्रवणौ तौ श्रुता याभ्यां सततं तत्कथाः शुभाः ॥ 7 ॥
1.57.m: That is voice which praises the god Keśava, O delight of the Bhṛgus; / those are ears by which auspicious narratives of him are constantly heard.

1.57.s:
avehi dharmajña tathā tatpūjākaraṇātkarau ..
tadekaṃ saphalaṃ karma keśavārthāya yatkṛtam .. 8 ..
1.57.d:
अवेहि धर्मज्ञ तथा तत्पूजाकरणात्करौ ॥
तदेकं सफलं कर्म केशवार्थाय यत्कृतम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.57.m: Know the two hands to be such, O knower of dharma, from performing worship of him; / that alone is fruitful action which is done for the sake of Keśava.

1.57.s:
yato mukhyaphalāvāptau karaṇaṃ saprayojanam ..
manasā tena kiṃ kāryyaṃ yanna tiṣṭhati keśave .. 9 ..
1.57.d:
यतो मुख्यफलावाप्तौ करणं सप्रयोजनम् ॥
मनसा तेन किं कार्य्यं यन्न तिष्ठति केशवे ॥ 9 ॥
1.57.m: Since an instrument has purpose [only] in the attainment of the principal fruit, / what use is that mind which does not rest upon Keśava?

1.57.s:
buddhyā vā bhārgavaśreṣṭha tayā nāsti prayojanam ..
rogaḥ sā rasanā vā'pi yayā na stūyate hariḥ .. 1.57.10 ..
1.57.d:
बुद्ध्या वा भार्गवश्रेष्ठ तया नास्ति प्रयोजनम् ॥
रोगः सा रसना वाऽपि यया न स्तूयते हरिः ॥ 1.57.10 ॥
1.57.m: Or what purpose is there with that intellect, O best of the Bhārgavas? / That tongue is a disease by which Hari is not praised.

1.57.s:
gartau brahmavratau karṇau yābhyāṃ tatkarma na śrutam ..
bhārabhūtaiḥ karaiḥ kāryaṃ ki tasya nṛpaśordvija .. 11 ..
1.57.d:
गर्तौ ब्रह्मव्रतौ कर्णौ याभ्यां तत्कर्म न श्रुतम् ॥
भारभूतैः करैः कार्यं कि तस्य नृपशोर्द्विज ॥ 11 ॥
1.57.m: Ears by which his deeds are not heard are mere pits, O observer of holy vows; / what use are hands that are merely a burden to that beast of a man, O twice-born,

1.57.s:
yairna saṃpūjito devaḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ ..
pādau tau saphalau rāma keśavālayagāminau .. 12 ..
1.57.d:
यैर्न संपूजितो देवः शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ॥
पादौ तौ सफलौ राम केशवालयगामिनौ ॥ 12 ॥
1.57.m: by which the god bearing the conch, discus, and mace is not worshipped? / Those feet are fruitful, O Rāma, that walk to the abode of Keśava.

1.57.s:
te ca netre mahābhāga yābhyāṃ saṃdṛśyate hariḥ ..
kiṃ tasya caraṇaiḥ kāryaṃ kṛtasya nipuṇairdvija .. 13 ..
1.57.d:
ते च नेत्रे महाभाग याभ्यां संदृश्यते हरिः ॥
किं तस्य चरणैः कार्यं कृतस्य निपुणैर्द्विज ॥ 13 ॥
1.57.m: And those eyes, O fortunate one, are the ones by which Hari is seen. / What use has that man, fashioned skilfully, of his feet, O twice-born,

1.57.s:
yābhyāṃ na vrajate jantuḥ keśavālayadarśane ..
jātyandhatulyaṃ taṃ manye puruṣaṃ puruṣottama .. 14 ..
1.57.d:
याभ्यां न व्रजते जन्तुः केशवालयदर्शने ॥
जात्यन्धतुल्यं तं मन्ये पुरुषं पुरुषोत्तम ॥ 14 ॥
1.57.m: by which a creature does not go to see the abode of Keśava? / I consider that man equal to one born blind, O best among men,

1.57.s:
yo na paśyati dharmajña keśavārcāṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..
kleśasaṃjananaṃ karma vṛthā tadbhṛgunandana .. 15 ..
1.57.d:
यो न पश्यति धर्मज्ञ केशवार्चां पुनःपुनः ॥
क्लेशसंजननं कर्म वृथा तद्भृगुनन्दन ॥ 15 ॥
1.57.m: who does not behold the image of Keśava again and again, O knower of dharma. / An action that causes distress is in vain, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.57.s:
keśavaṃ prati yadrāma kriyate'hani sarvadā ..
paśya keśavamārādhya modamānaṃ śacīpatim .. 16 ..
1.57.d:
केशवं प्रति यद्राम क्रियतेऽहनि सर्वदा ॥
पश्य केशवमाराध्य मोदमानं शचीपतिम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.57.m: [Fruitful is] what is done daily toward Keśava at all times, O Rāma. / Behold the lord of Śacī rejoicing after having worshipped Keśava,

1.57.s:
yamañca varuṇañcaiva tathā vaiśravaṇaṃ prabhum ..
devendratvamatisphītaṃ sarvabhūtismitaṃ padam .. 17 '.
haribhaktidrumātpuṣpaṃ rājasātsāttvikaṃ phalam ..
aṇimā mahimā prāptiḥ prākāmyaṃ laghimā tathā .. 18 ..
1.57.d:
यमञ्च वरुणञ्चैव तथा वैश्रवणं प्रभुम् ॥
देवेन्द्रत्वमतिस्फीतं सर्वभूतिस्मितं पदम् ॥ 17 '.
हरिभक्तिद्रुमात्पुष्पं राजसात्सात्त्विकं फलम् ॥
अणिमा महिमा प्राप्तिः प्राकाम्यं लघिमा तथा ॥ 18 ॥
1.57.m: and Yama, Varuṇa, and the lord Vaiśravaṇa as well; / the sovereign state of the gods, exceedingly flourishing, a position radiant with all prosperity! / From the tree of devotion to Hari, the flower is rājasika, and the fruit is sāttvika: / lightness, greatness, reach, freedom of will, lightness,

1.57.s:
īthitvañca vaśitvañca yatra kāmāvasāyitā ..
ārādhya keśavaṃ devaṃ prāpyante nā'tra saṃśayaḥ .. 19 ..
1.57.d:
ईथित्वञ्च वशित्वञ्च यत्र कामावसायिता ॥
आराध्य केशवं देवं प्राप्यन्ते नाऽत्र संशयः ॥ 19 ॥
1.57.m: lordship, subjugation, and where desires are accomplished at will— / these are attained by worshipping the god Keśava, there is no doubt here.

1.57.s:
hatapratyaṅgamātaṅgo rudhirāruṇabhūtale ..
saṃgrāme vijayaṃ rāma prāpyate tatprasādataḥ .. .. 1.57.20 ..
1.57.d:
हतप्रत्यङ्गमातङ्गो रुधिरारुणभूतले ॥
संग्रामे विजयं राम प्राप्यते तत्प्रसादतः ॥ ॥ 1.57.20 ॥
1.57.m: Upon the earth reddened with blood, with elephants having their limbs destroyed, / victory in battle is obtained, O Rāma, through his grace.

1.57.s:
mahākaṭitaṭaśroṇyaḥ pīnonnatapayodharāḥ ..
akalaṅkaśaśāṅkābhavadanā nīlamūrdhajāḥ .. 21 ..
1.57.d:
महाकटितटश्रोण्यः पीनोन्नतपयोधराः ॥
अकलङ्कशशाङ्काभवदना नीलमूर्धजाः ॥ 21 ॥
1.57.m: Possessing broad hips and buttocks, full and elevated breasts, / faces resembling the spotless moon, and dark black hair,

1.57.s:
ramayanti naraṃ svapne devarāmā manoharāḥ ..
sakṛdyenārcito devo helayā vā namaskṛtaḥ .. 22 ..
1.57.d:
रमयन्ति नरं स्वप्ने देवरामा मनोहराः ॥
सकृद्येनार्चितो देवो हेलया वा नमस्कृतः ॥ 22 ॥
1.57.m: charming celestial women delight a man even in sleep, / by whom the god has been worshipped once, or saluted even playfully.

1.57.s:
vedavedāṅgavapuṣāṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām ..
ṛṣitvamapi dharmajña vijñeyaṃ tatprasādajam .. 23 ..
1.57.d:
वेदवेदाङ्गवपुषां मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम् ॥
ऋषित्वमपि धर्मज्ञ विज्ञेयं तत्प्रसादजम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.57.m: The status of being an inspired seer among sages who embody the Vedas and auxiliary sciences and who are purified in self / is also to be known as born of his grace, O knower of dharma.

1.57.s:
ramante saha rāmābhiḥ prāpya vaidyādharaṃ padam ..
anyabhāvatayā nāmnaḥ kīrtanādapi bhārgava .. 24 ..
1.57.d:
रमन्ते सह रामाभिः प्राप्य वैद्याधरं पदम् ॥
अन्यभावतया नाम्नः कीर्तनादपि भार्गव ॥ 24 ॥
1.57.m: Attaining the status of Vidyādharas, they delight with women, / even from reciting his name with a distracted mind, O Bhārgava.

1.57.s:
ratnaparyaṅkaśayitā mahābhogāśca bhoginaḥ ..
vījyante saha rāmābhiḥ keśavasmaraṇādapi .. 25 ..
1.57.d:
रत्नपर्यङ्कशयिता महाभोगाश्च भोगिनः ॥
वीज्यन्ते सह रामाभिः केशवस्मरणादपि ॥ 25 ॥
1.57.m: Lying upon jewelled couches, experiencing great pleasures, sensualists / are fanned together with lovely women merely from remembering Keśava.

1.57.s:
saugandhike vane ramye kailāsaparvate dvija ..
yadyakṣā viharanti sma tatprāhuḥ kusumaṃ nateḥ .. 26 ..
1.57.d:
सौगन्धिके वने रम्ये कैलासपर्वते द्विज ॥
यद्यक्षा विहरन्ति स्म तत्प्राहुः कुसुमं नतेः ॥ 26 ॥
1.57.m: That the Yakṣas disport in the charming Saugandhika forest on Mount Kailāsa, / that, O twice-born, they call the flower of prostration [to him].

1.57.s:
ratnacitrāsu ramyāsu nandanodyānabhūmiṣu ..
krīḍanti ca saha strībhirgandharvībhiḥ kathāśruteḥ .. 27 ..
1.57.d:
रत्नचित्रासु रम्यासु नन्दनोद्यानभूमिषु ॥
क्रीडन्ति च सह स्त्रीभिर्गन्धर्वीभिः कथाश्रुतेः ॥ 27 ॥
1.57.m: In the delightful grounds of the Nandana garden, varied with jewels, / they play with Gandharva women from having heard his stories.

1.57.s:
catussamudravelāyāṃ meruvindhyapayodharām ..
dharāṃ ye bhuñjate bhūpāḥ praṇipātasya tatphalam .. 28 ..
1.57.d:
चतुस्समुद्रवेलायां मेरुविन्ध्यपयोधराम् ॥
धरां ये भुञ्जते भूपाः प्रणिपातस्य तत्फलम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.57.m: Those kings who enjoy the earth, whose breasts are Meru and Vindhya, / bounded by the shores of the four oceans—that is the fruit of bowing down to him.

1.57.s:
tasmāttavā'haṃ vakṣyāmi yadyadācarataḥ sadā ..
puruṣasyeha bhagavānsutoṣastuṣyate hariḥ .. 29 ..
1.57.d:
तस्मात्तवाऽहं वक्ष्यामि यद्यदाचरतः सदा ॥
पुरुषस्येह भगवान्सुतोषस्तुष्यते हरिः ॥ 29 ॥
1.57.m: Therefore, I will tell you what, when practiced constantly / by a man here, pleases the Lord Hari, who is easily pleased.

1.57.s:
pūjyaḥ sa nityaṃ varado mahātmā stavyaḥ sa nityaṃ jagadekavandyaḥ ..
dhyeyaḥ sa nityaṃ sakalāghahartā caitāvaduktaṃ tava rāma guhyam .. 1.57.30 ..
1.57.d:
पूज्यः स नित्यं वरदो महात्मा स्तव्यः स नित्यं जगदेकवन्द्यः ॥
ध्येयः स नित्यं सकलाघहर्ता चैतावदुक्तं तव राम गुह्यम् ॥ 1.57.30 ॥
1.57.m: He, the granter of boons, the great-souled one, is always to be worshipped; he, the sole object of praise for the world, is always to be praised; / he, the remover of all sins, is always to be meditated upon. This much secret [truth] has been spoken to you, O Rāma.

1.58.s:
.. śaṅkara uvāca ..
ahiṃsā satyavacanaṃ dayā bhūteṣvanugraham ..
yasyaitāni sadā rāma tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 1 ..
1.58.d:
॥ शङ्कर उवाच ॥
अहिंसा सत्यवचनं दया भूतेष्वनुग्रहम् ॥
यस्यैतानि सदा राम तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 1 ॥
1.58.m: Śaṅkara said: / Non-violence, speaking truth, compassion, [and] kindness toward living beings— / he who always possesses these, O Rāma, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
mātāpitṛgurūṇāñca yaḥ samyagiha varttate ..
varjako madhumāṃsasya tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 2 ..
1.58.d:
मातापितृगुरूणाञ्च यः सम्यगिह वर्त्तते ॥
वर्जको मधुमांसस्य तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 2 ॥
1.58.m: He who conducts himself properly here toward mother, father, and teachers, / [and] who abstains from liquor and meat, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
varāhamatsyamāṃsāni yo nātti bhṛgunandana ..
virato madyapānācca tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 3 ..
1.58.d:
वराहमत्स्यमांसानि यो नात्ति भृगुनन्दन ॥
विरतो मद्यपानाच्च तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 3 ॥
1.58.m: He who does not eat the flesh of boar or fish, O son of Bhṛgu, / and who desists from drinking liquor, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
na dhārayati nirmālyamanyadevoddhṛtaṃ tu yaḥ ..
bhuṃkte na cānyanaivedyaṃ tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 4 ..
1.58.d:
न धारयति निर्माल्यमन्यदेवोद्धृतं तु यः ॥
भुंक्ते न चान्यनैवेद्यं तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 4 ॥
1.58.m: He who does not wear the floral offerings taken from another deity, / and does not eat another [deity's] food offering, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
avaiṣṇave devadhṛtaṃ nirmālyaṃ yaḥ prayacchati ..
naivedyaṃ vā mahābhāga tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 5 ..
1.58.d:
अवैष्णवे देवधृतं निर्माल्यं यः प्रयच्छति ॥
नैवेद्यं वा महाभाग तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 5 ॥
1.58.m: He who gives to a non-Vaiṣṇava the floral offering worn by a deity, / or the food offering, O fortunate one, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
bibharti mūrdhni nirmālyaṃ keśavārcādhṛtaṃ tu yaḥ..
anivedya na cāśnāti tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 6..
1.58.d:
बिभर्ति मूर्ध्नि निर्माल्यं केशवार्चाधृतं तु यः॥
अनिवेद्य न चाश्नाति तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 6॥
1.58.m: He who wears upon his head the floral offering borne by an image of Keśava, / and does not eat without having [first] offered, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
parapīḍākaraṃ karma yasya nā'sti mahātmanaḥ..
saṃvibhāgī ca bhūtānāṃ tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 7 ..
1.58.d:
परपीडाकरं कर्म यस्य नाऽस्ति महात्मनः॥
संविभागी च भूतानां तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 7 ॥
1.58.m: That great-souled one who has no action causing harm to others, / and who shares [his food] with living beings, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
śṛṇute sarvadharmāṃśca sarvāndevānnamasyati ..
anasūyurjitakrodhastasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 8 ..
1.58.d:
शृणुते सर्वधर्मांश्च सर्वान्देवान्नमस्यति ॥
अनसूयुर्जितक्रोधस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 8 ॥
1.58.m: He who listens to all dharmas, bows to all deities, / is free from envy, and has conquered anger, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
tīrthopavāsasevī ca dvijātigaṇasevakaḥ ..
pūjako viṣṇubhaktānāṃ tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 9 ..
1.58.d:
तीर्थोपवाससेवी च द्विजातिगणसेवकः ॥
पूजको विष्णुभक्तानां तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 9 ॥
1.58.m: He who frequents sacred bathing places and observes fasts, serves the company of the twice-born, / and worships the devotees of Viṣṇu, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
pañcarātravido mukhyānyastu saṃpūjayetsadā ..
devavadbhṛguśārdūla tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 1.58.10 ..
1.58.d:
पञ्चरात्रविदो मुख्यान्यस्तु संपूजयेत्सदा ॥
देववद्भृगुशार्दूल तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 1.58.10 ॥
1.58.m: He who always worships the foremost knowers of the Pañcarātra / like gods, O tiger among the Bhṛgus, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
pitṛdevārcanarataḥ svadāranirataḥ sadā ..
ṛtukālābhigāmī ca tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ ..11..
1.58.d:
पितृदेवार्चनरतः स्वदारनिरतः सदा ॥
ऋतुकालाभिगामी च तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥11॥
1.58.m: Devoted to worshipping the ancestors and deities, always devoted to his own wife, / and approaching [her only] at the proper time of her season, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
nāmnāṃ sahasreṇa tathā yaśca gāyati tanmanāḥ ..
satataṃ kalyamutthāya tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ ..12..
1.58.d:
नाम्नां सहस्रेण तथा यश्च गायति तन्मनाः ॥
सततं कल्यमुत्थाय तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥12॥
1.58.m: And he who, with his mind fixed on him, sings with the thousand names [of Viṣṇu], / having risen early in the morning every day, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
pauruṣeṇa ca sūktena japyahomādikaṃ sadā..
yaḥ karotyamitaprajñastasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 13 ..
1.58.d:
पौरुषेण च सूक्तेन जप्यहोमादिकं सदा॥
यः करोत्यमितप्रज्ञस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 13 ॥
1.58.m: And he who, endowed with immeasurable wisdom, always performs recitation, oblation, and the like / with the hymn to the Cosmic Person, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
mitrasvāmigurudroho yasya nā'sti mahātmanaḥ ..
paradāradhanecchā na tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 14 ..
1.58.d:
मित्रस्वामिगुरुद्रोहो यस्य नाऽस्ति महात्मनः ॥
परदारधनेच्छा न तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 14 ॥
1.58.m: That great-souled one who has no treachery toward friend, master, or teacher, / and no desire for another's wife or wealth, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
rājā śāstropadeśena rājyaṃ yaśca praśāsati ..
rājadharmaratirnityaṃ tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ..15..
1.58.d:
राजा शास्त्रोपदेशेन राज्यं यश्च प्रशासति ॥
राजधर्मरतिर्नित्यं तस्य तुष्यति केशवः॥15॥
1.58.m: A king who governs his realm according to the teaching of the treatises, / and always takes delight in the duties of kings, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
yā tu nārī patiprāṇā patibhaktā pativratā ..
tasyāḥ sutoṣo bhagavām̐stoṣamāyāti keśavaḥ..16..
1.58.d:
या तु नारी पतिप्राणा पतिभक्ता पतिव्रता ॥
तस्याः सुतोषो भगवाम्̐स्तोषमायाति केशवः॥16॥
1.58.m: As for that woman whose husband is her very life, devoted to her husband, faithful to her husband, / the Lord Keśava, easily pleased, attains satisfaction through her.

1.58.s:
agnihotraparo vidvānyajñairnityamatandritaḥ ..
yastu tarpayate devāṃstasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ..17..
1.58.d:
अग्निहोत्रपरो विद्वान्यज्ञैर्नित्यमतन्द्रितः ॥
यस्तु तर्पयते देवांस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः॥17॥
1.58.m: The learned man devoted to the agnihotra fire, who, ever untiring, / pleases the deities with sacrifices, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
svavarṇāśramadharmasthaḥ pūjayanmadhusūdanam ..
kālaṃ nayati yo brahmam̐stasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ ..18..
1.58.d:
स्ववर्णाश्रमधर्मस्थः पूजयन्मधुसूदनम् ॥
कालं नयति यो ब्रह्मम्̐स्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥18॥
1.58.m: Standing in the dharma of his own class and stage of life, worshipping Madhusūdana, / he who passes his time [thus], O holy one, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
sopavāsastu pakṣānte dvādaśyāṃ vā bhṛgūttama ..
baudhe'hni śravaṇarkṣe vā tṛtīyāyāntu vā punaḥ ..
sopavāso'rcayati yastasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 19 ..
1.58.d:
सोपवासस्तु पक्षान्ते द्वादश्यां वा भृगूत्तम ॥
बौधेऽह्नि श्रवणर्क्षे वा तृतीयायान्तु वा पुनः ॥
सोपवासोऽर्चयति यस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 19 ॥
1.58.m: Fasting at the end of a fortnight, or on the twelfth day [of a lunar fortnight], O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / or on a Wednesday, or under the asterism Śravaṇa, or again on the third day [of a lunar fortnight], / he who worships while fasting, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
puṣpaṃ vinā hariṃ prāpya phalī ratnaṃ kṣumāpi vā ..
nivedayati yaḥ kṛṣṇe tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ..1.58.20..
1.58.d:
पुष्पं विना हरिं प्राप्य फली रत्नं क्षुमापि वा ॥
निवेदयति यः कृष्णे तस्य तुष्यति केशवः॥1.58.20॥
1.58.m: Having approached Hari without flowers, he who, bearing fruit, offers / a jewel or even flax to Kṛṣṇa, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
kṛṣṇe paśyati yatsarvaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sarvatra paśyati ..
mahātmā buddhisampannastasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 21 ..
1.58.d:
कृष्णे पश्यति यत्सर्वं कृष्णं सर्वत्र पश्यति ॥
महात्मा बुद्धिसम्पन्नस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 21 ॥
1.58.m: He who sees everything in Kṛṣṇa, and sees Kṛṣṇa everywhere, / that great-souled one endowed with discernment, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
tatkathāyāñca ramate tatkathāṃ yaḥ karoti ca ..
tanmanāstadgataprāṇastasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ ..22..
1.58.d:
तत्कथायाञ्च रमते तत्कथां यः करोति च ॥
तन्मनास्तद्गतप्राणस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥22॥
1.58.m: He who delights in narratives about him, and tells narratives about him, / his mind fixed on him, his life-breath dedicated to him, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
sarvabhūtahite yuktaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ ..
sarvabhūtānukampī ca tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 23 ..
1.58.d:
सर्वभूतहिते युक्तः सर्वभूतहिते रतः ॥
सर्वभूतानुकम्पी च तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 23 ॥
1.58.m: Dedicated to the welfare of all beings, delighting in the welfare of all beings, / and compassionate toward all beings, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
apraṇamya kriyāṃ kāṃcidyastu nā''rabhate harim ..
asaṃbhinnārthamaryādastasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 24 ..
1.58.d:
अप्रणम्य क्रियां कांचिद्यस्तु ना'ऽरभते हरिम् ॥
असंभिन्नार्थमर्यादस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 24 ॥
1.58.m: He who does not begin any rite without having bowed to Hari, / and does not transgress the bounds of righteousness, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
nāmasaṃkīrtanaṃ nityaṃ kṣuta praskhalanādiṣu ..
yaḥ karoti mahābhāgastasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 25 ..
1.58.d:
नामसंकीर्तनं नित्यं क्षुत प्रस्खलनादिषु ॥
यः करोति महाभागस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 25 ॥
1.58.m: He who, O fortunate one, constantly chants the names [of the Lord] / upon sneezing, stumbling, and the like, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
navaṃ patraṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ nivedya madhusūdane ..
paścādbhuṅkte svayaṃ yaśca tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 26
1.58.d:
नवं पत्रं फलं पुष्पं निवेद्य मधुसूदने ॥
पश्चाद्भुङ्क्ते स्वयं यश्च तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 26
1.58.m: Having offered a fresh leaf, fruit, or flower to Madhusūdana, / he who afterwards eats [it] himself, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
āpadyapi ca kaṣṭāyāṃ deveśaśapathaṃ naraḥ ..
na karoti hi yo brahmaṃstasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 27 ..
1.58.d:
आपद्यपि च कष्टायां देवेशशपथं नरः ॥
न करोति हि यो ब्रह्मंस्तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 27 ॥
1.58.m: Even in severe distress, that man who never swears / an oath by the Lord of the gods, O holy one, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
devāduddhṛtya nirmālyaṃ chāyāṃ nākramate ca yaḥ ..
dhūpāgnibhasma ca tathā tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ ..28..
1.58.d:
देवादुद्धृत्य निर्माल्यं छायां नाक्रमते च यः ॥
धूपाग्निभस्म च तथा तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥28॥
1.58.m: Having removed the floral offering from the deity, he who does not step on its shadow, / and likewise on the incense, fire, or ashes, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
dṛṣṭvā saṃpūjitāmarcā yaśca bhaktyābhinandati ..
svayaṃ saṃpūjayedyastu tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 29 ..
1.58.d:
दृष्ट्वा संपूजितामर्चा यश्च भक्त्याभिनन्दति ॥
स्वयं संपूजयेद्यस्तु तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 29 ॥
1.58.m: He who, seeing an image that has been worshipped, rejoices with devotion, / and who worships [it] himself, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
nityaṃ saṃpūjayedyastu devadevasya bhaktitaḥ ..
yathāśaktyā mahābhāga tasya tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 1.58.30 ..
1.58.d:
नित्यं संपूजयेद्यस्तु देवदेवस्य भक्तितः ॥
यथाशक्त्या महाभाग तस्य तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 1.58.30 ॥
1.58.m: He who, O fortunate one, constantly worships with devotion / the God of gods according to his ability, Keśava is pleased with him.

1.58.s:
na rāma vividhairdānairna ratnadhanasaṃcayaiḥ ..
toṣamāyāti deveśo bhaktyā tuṣyati keśavaḥ .. 31 ..
1.58.d:
न राम विविधैर्दानैर्न रत्नधनसंचयैः ॥
तोषमायाति देवेशो भक्त्या तुष्यति केशवः ॥ 31 ॥
1.58.m: Not by manifold gifts, O Rāma, nor by heaps of jewels and wealth / does the Lord of the gods attain satisfaction; Keśava is pleased by devotion.

1.58.s:
dānairbhṛguśreṣṭha bahuprakāraistīrthopavāsavratadarśanaiśca ..
tathā na toṣaṃ bhagavānprayāti bhaktyā yathā tadgatamānasānām .. 32 ..
1.58.d:
दानैर्भृगुश्रेष्ठ बहुप्रकारैस्तीर्थोपवासव्रतदर्शनैश्च ॥
तथा न तोषं भगवान्प्रयाति भक्त्या यथा तद्गतमानसानाम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.58.m: Not by gifts of many kinds, O best of the Bhṛgus, nor by visits to sacred bathing places, fasts, and vows, / does the Lord attain such satisfaction as by the devotion of those whose minds are fixed on him.

1.58.s:
etāvaduktaṃ tava rāma guhyaṃ na deyametadbhuvi matsarāṇām ..
na tarkaśāstrākulamānasānāṃ nā'vaiṣṇavānāṃ na ca nāstikānām .. 33 ..
1.58.d:
एतावदुक्तं तव राम गुह्यं न देयमेतद्भुवि मत्सराणाम् ॥
न तर्कशास्त्राकुलमानसानां नाऽवैष्णवानां न च नास्तिकानाम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.58.m: This much secret [truth] has been spoken to you, O Rāma; on earth this is not to be given to the envious, / nor to those whose minds are bewildered by the treatises of logic, nor to non-Vaiṣṇavas, nor to materialists.

1.59.s:
śrīrāma uvāca..
upoṣitena yeneha yaṃyaṃ kāmaṃ prayacchati ..
tadahaṃ śrotumicchāmi gadataste vṛṣadhvaja .. 1 ..
1.59.d:
श्रीराम उवाच॥
उपोषितेन येनेह यंयं कामं प्रयच्छति ॥
तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि गदतस्ते वृषध्वज ॥ 1 ॥
1.59.m: Glorious Rāma said: / Which specific desire he grants here to one who has fasted— / that I wish to hear as you tell it, O god who has a bull for his emblem.

1.59.s:
śaṃkara uvāca..
pūjitaḥ prayataiḥ snānaiḥ sopavāsairdine raveḥ..
saṃvatsaraṃ mahābhāga dīrghamāyuḥ prayacchati .. 2 ..
1.59.d:
शंकर उवाच॥
पूजितः प्रयतैः स्नानैः सोपवासैर्दिने रवेः॥
संवत्सरं महाभाग दीर्घमायुः प्रयच्छति ॥ 2 ॥
1.59.m: Śaṅkara said: / Worshipped with restrained baths and with fasts on the day of the Sun / for a year, O fortunate one, he grants a long life.

1.59.s:
somavāre mahābhāga cārogyaṃ saṃprayacchati ..
tathā bhaumadine rāma vaiśvaryaṃ saṃprayacchati .. 3 ..
1.59.d:
सोमवारे महाभाग चारोग्यं संप्रयच्छति ॥
तथा भौमदिने राम वैश्वर्यं संप्रयच्छति ॥ 3 ॥
1.59.m: On a Monday, O fortunate one, he grants health; / likewise on a Tuesday, O Rāma, he grants sovereign power.

1.59.s:
vāsare somaputrasya sarvānkāmānprayacchati ..
abhīṣṭāñca tathā vidyāmākhaṇḍalagurordine .. 4 ..
1.59.d:
वासरे सोमपुत्रस्य सर्वान्कामान्प्रयच्छति ॥
अभीष्टाञ्च तथा विद्यामाखण्डलगुरोर्दिने ॥ 4 ॥
1.59.m: On the day of the Moon's son, he grants all desires; / and on the day of Indra's teacher, he grants desired knowledge.

1.59.s:
saubhāgyamatulaṃ loke bhārgavāhni prayacchati ..
tathā śanaiścarasyāhni ripūnsarvānvyapohati .. 5 ..
1.59.d:
सौभाग्यमतुलं लोके भार्गवाह्नि प्रयच्छति ॥
तथा शनैश्चरस्याह्नि रिपून्सर्वान्व्यपोहति ॥ 5 ॥
1.59.m: On the day of Bhṛgu's descendant, he grants peerless good fortune in the world; / likewise on the day of Saturn, he drives away all enemies.

1.59.s:
kṛttikāsu tathā'bhyarcya yajñānprāpnotyanuttamān ..
prājāpatye tathā'bhyarcya prajāṃ prāpnoti śobhanām .. 6 ..
1.59.d:
कृत्तिकासु तथाऽभ्यर्च्य यज्ञान्प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमान् ॥
प्राजापत्ये तथाऽभ्यर्च्य प्रजां प्राप्नोति शोभनाम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.59.m: And by worshipping [Him] during Kṛttikā, one obtains unsurpassed sacrifices; / and by worshipping during Prājāpatya (Rohiṇī), one obtains noble offspring.

1.59.s:
vindate brahmavarcasyaṃ mṛgaśīrṣe'rcayanharim ..
raudrakarmatvamāpnoti siddhiṃ raudre samarcayan .. 7 ..
1.59.d:
विन्दते ब्रह्मवर्चस्यं मृगशीर्षेऽर्चयन्हरिम् ॥
रौद्रकर्मत्वमाप्नोति सिद्धिं रौद्रे समर्चयन् ॥ 7 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping Hari during Mṛgaśīrṣa, one finds spiritual splendour; / worshipping during Raudra (Ārdrā), one obtains the power to perform fierce deeds and succeeds.

1.59.s:
cyutaḥ sthānamavāpnoti pūjayānaḥ punarvasau ..
puṣye saṃpūjito devaḥ puṣṭimagryāṃ prayacchati ..8 ..
1.59.d:
च्युतः स्थानमवाप्नोति पूजयानः पुनर्वसौ ॥
पुष्ये संपूजितो देवः पुष्टिमग्र्यां प्रयच्छति ॥8 ॥
1.59.m: One who has fallen gains a high place by worshipping during Punarvasu; / worshipped during Puṣya, the Lord grants supreme nourishment.

1.59.s:
aśleṣāyāṃ tathā'bhyarcya śriyaṃ vindati mānavaḥ ..
pitṛprasādamāpnoti pitrye saṃpūjanharim .. 9 ..
1.59.d:
अश्लेषायां तथाऽभ्यर्च्य श्रियं विन्दति मानवः ॥
पितृप्रसादमाप्नोति पित्र्ये संपूजन्हरिम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.59.m: And by worshipping during Āśleṣā, a person finds prosperity; / worshipping Hari during Pitrya (Maghā), one attains the grace of the ancestors.

1.59.s:
saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti phālgunīṣvarcayaṃstathā ..
tathaiva cottarāyoge gatiṃ vindati śobhanām .. 1.59.10 ..
1.59.d:
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति फाल्गुनीष्वर्चयंस्तथा ॥
तथैव चोत्तरायोगे गतिं विन्दति शोभनाम् ॥ 1.59.10 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping during the Phālgunīs, one obtains great good fortune; / and similarly, during the conjunction of Uttarā, one finds an auspicious destiny.

1.59.s:
haste saṃpūjayandevaṃ gajānprāpnotyanuttamān ..
citrāsu ca tathā'bhyarcya vastrāṇyāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 11 ..
1.59.d:
हस्ते संपूजयन्देवं गजान्प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमान् ॥
चित्रासु च तथाऽभ्यर्च्य वस्त्राण्याप्नोति मानवः ॥ 11 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping the Lord during Hasta, one obtains unsurpassed elephants; / and by worshipping during Citrā, a person obtains garments.

1.59.s:
āpye samarcayandevaṃ ratnabhāgī bhavennaraḥ ..
tathottarāsvāṣāḍhāsu kīrtiṃ prāpnoti śāśvatīm .. 12 ..
1.59.d:
आप्ये समर्चयन्देवं रत्नभागी भवेन्नरः ॥
तथोत्तरास्वाषाढासु कीर्तिं प्राप्नोति शाश्वतीम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping the Lord during Āpya (Pūrvāṣāḍhā), a man becomes an owner of jewels; / and during Uttarāṣāḍhā, one attains everlasting fame.

1.59.s:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti śravaṇe'bhyarcayanharim ..
dhaniṣṭhāsu tathā vittamārogyaṃ vāruṇe tathā .. 13 ..
1.59.d:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति श्रवणेऽभ्यर्चयन्हरिम् ॥
धनिष्ठासु तथा वित्तमारोग्यं वारुणे तथा ॥ 13 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping Hari during Śravaṇa, one obtains all desires; / during Dhaniṣṭhā, wealth; and during Vāruṇa (Śatabhiṣaj), health.

1.59.s:
āje paśūnavāpnoti gāvaśca tadanantaram ..
pauṣṇe śīlamavāpnoti cāśvānprāpnoti cā'śvine .. 14 ..
1.59.d:
आजे पशूनवाप्नोति गावश्च तदनन्तरम् ॥
पौष्णे शीलमवाप्नोति चाश्वान्प्राप्नोति चाऽश्विने ॥ 14 ॥
1.59.m: During Āja (Pūrvabhādrapadā), one obtains livestock, and immediately thereafter cows; / during Pauṣṇa (Revatī), one obtains virtuous character; and during Aśvinī, horses.

1.59.s:
dīrghajīvitamāpnoti bharaṇīṣu mahābhuja ..
pratipadyarthamāpnoti kupyaṃ prāpnotyanuttamama .. 15 ..
1.59.d:
दीर्घजीवितमाप्नोति भरणीषु महाभुज ॥
प्रतिपद्यर्थमाप्नोति कुप्यं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम ॥ 15 ॥
1.59.m: O large-armed one, during Bharaṇī, one attains a long life; / on the first lunar day, one obtains wealth and unsurpassed base metals.

1.59.s:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoni tṛtīyāyāṃ samarcayan ..
paśūm̐ścaturthyāmāpnoti pañcamyāṃ śriyamuttamām .. 16 ..
1.59.d:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोनि तृतीयायां समर्चयन् ॥
पशूम्̐श्चतुर्थ्यामाप्नोति पञ्चम्यां श्रियमुत्तमाम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping on the third lunar day, one obtains all desires; / on the fourth, one obtains livestock; and on the fifth, supreme prosperity.

1.59.s:
ṣaṣṭhayāṃ prāpnotyathā''rogyaṃ saptamyāṃ suhṛdastathā ..
aṣṭamyāṃ ca tathā bhṛtyānnavamyāṃ ca tathā yaśaḥ .. 17 ..
1.59.d:
षष्ठयां प्राप्नोत्यथा'ऽरोग्यं सप्तम्यां सुहृदस्तथा ॥
अष्टम्यां च तथा भृत्यान्नवम्यां च तथा यशः ॥ 17 ॥
1.59.m: On the sixth, one obtains health; and on the seventh, friends; / and on the eighth, servants; and on the ninth, fame.

1.59.s:
karmasiddhimavāpnoti daśamyāṃ pūjayanharim ..
ekādaśyāṃ pūjayānaḥ śrībhāgī sa sadā bhaveta .. 18 ..
1.59.d:
कर्मसिद्धिमवाप्नोति दशम्यां पूजयन्हरिम् ॥
एकादश्यां पूजयानः श्रीभागी स सदा भवेत ॥ 18 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping Hari on the tenth, one obtains success in action; / worshipping on the eleventh, one always shares in good fortune.

1.59.s:
abhīṣṭāṃ gatimāpnoti dvādaśyāṃ pūjayanharim ..
trayodaśyāṃ pūjayāno rūpaṃ prāpnotyanuttamam .. 19 ..
1.59.d:
अभीष्टां गतिमाप्नोति द्वादश्यां पूजयन्हरिम् ॥
त्रयोदश्यां पूजयानो रूपं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping Hari on the twelfth, one obtains a desired destiny; / worshipping on the thirteenth, one attains unsurpassed beauty.

1.59.s:
na durgatimavāpnoti pūjayānaścaturdaśīma ..
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti pañcadaśyāṃ mahāmune .. 1.59.20 ..
1.59.d:
न दुर्गतिमवाप्नोति पूजयानश्चतुर्दशीम ॥
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति पञ्चदश्यां महामुने ॥ 1.59.20 ॥
1.59.m: Worshipping on the fourteenth, one meets no misfortune; / on the fifteenth, O great sage, one obtains all desires.

1.59.s:
ityetaduktaṃ tava mānavānāṃ kāmyaṃ phalaṃ samyagupoṣitānām ..
deveśvaraṃ pūjayatāṃ yathāvatparaṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ vareṇyam .. 21 ..
1.59.d:
इत्येतदुक्तं तव मानवानां काम्यं फलं सम्यगुपोषितानाम् ॥
देवेश्वरं पूजयतां यथावत्परं पुराणं पुरुषं वरेण्यम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.59.m: Thus has been declared to you the desired fruit for men who have fasted properly, / worshipping the Lord of gods, the supreme, ancient, and most excellent Cosmic Person as prescribed.

1.60.s:
.. rāma uvāca ..
upavāsāsamarthānāṃ kiṃ syādekamupoṣitam ..
mahāphalaṃ mahādeva tatsamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ ..1..
1.60.d:
॥ राम उवाच ॥
उपवासासमर्थानां किं स्यादेकमुपोषितम् ॥
महाफलं महादेव तत्समाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥1॥
1.60.m: Rāma said: / For those unable to observe [regular] fasts, what single fast / would yield great fruit? O Mahādeva, explain that to me who am asking.

1.60.s:
.. śaṅkara uvāca ..
yā rāma śravaṇopetā dvādaśī mahatī ca sā ..
tasyāmupoṣitaḥ snātaḥ pūjayitvā janārdanam .. 2 ..
1.60.d:
॥ शङ्कर उवाच ॥
या राम श्रवणोपेता द्वादशी महती च सा ॥
तस्यामुपोषितः स्नातः पूजयित्वा जनार्दनम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.60.m: Śaṅkara said: / O Rāma, that twelfth lunar day which is joined with the Śravaṇa asterism is indeed great; / fasting on it, bathed and having worshipped Janārdana,

1.60.s:
prāpnotyayatnāddharmajña dvādaśadvādaśīphalam ..
dadhyodanayutaṃ tasyāṃ jalapūrṇaṃ ghaṭaṃ dvije .. 3 ..
1.60.d:
प्राप्नोत्ययत्नाद्धर्मज्ञ द्वादशद्वादशीफलम् ॥
दध्योदनयुतं तस्यां जलपूर्णं घटं द्विजे ॥ 3 ॥
1.60.m: one effortlessly obtains the fruit of twelve twelfth days, O knower of dharma. / On that day, giving a water-filled pot with curd-rice to a twice-born,

1.60.s:
vastrasaṃveṣṭitaṃ dattvā chatropānahameva ca ..
na durgatimavāpnoti gatimanyāñca vindati .. 4 ..
1.60.d:
वस्त्रसंवेष्टितं दत्त्वा छत्रोपानहमेव च ॥
न दुर्गतिमवाप्नोति गतिमन्याञ्च विन्दति ॥ 4 ॥
1.60.m: wrapped in cloth, along with an umbrella and sandals, / one does not meet misfortune and attains the highest destiny.

1.60.s:
akṣayyaṃ sthānamāpnoti nā'tra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
śravaṇadvādaśīyoge budhavāro bhavedyadi .. 5 ..
1.60.d:
अक्षय्यं स्थानमाप्नोति नाऽत्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
श्रवणद्वादशीयोगे बुधवारो भवेद्यदि ॥ 5 ॥
1.60.m: One attains an imperishable station; no doubt should be entertained on this. / If a Wednesday occurs during the conjunction of the twelfth day and Śravaṇa,

1.60.s:
atyantaṃ mahatī nāma dvādaśī sā prakīrtitā ..
snānaṃ japyaṃ tathā dānaṃ homaṃ śrāddhaṃ surārcanam .. 6 ..
1.60.d:
अत्यन्तं महती नाम द्वादशी सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
स्नानं जप्यं तथा दानं होमं श्राद्धं सुरार्चनम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.60.m: that twelfth day is renowned as "Extremely Great." / Bathing, reciting mantras, making gifts, offering oblations, ancestral rites, and worshipping the gods—

1.60.s:
sarvamakṣayyamāpnoti tasya bhṛgukulodvaha ..
tasmindine tathā snāto yatra kvacana saṃgame .. 7 ..
1.60.d:
सर्वमक्षय्यमाप्नोति तस्य भृगुकुलोद्वह ॥
तस्मिन्दिने तथा स्नातो यत्र क्वचन संगमे ॥ 7 ॥
1.60.m: all become imperishable for him, O scion of Bhṛgu's lineage. / Bathed on that day at any confluence [of rivers],

1.60.s:
sa kratusnānajaṃ puṇyaṃ phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam ..
śravaṇe saṃgamāḥ sarve phalapuṣṭipradāḥ sadā .. 8 ..
1.60.d:
स क्रतुस्नानजं पुण्यं फलमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥
श्रवणे संगमाः सर्वे फलपुष्टिप्रदाः सदा ॥ 8 ॥
1.60.m: he undoubtedly attains the meritorious fruit born of bathing at a Vedic sacrifice. / Confluences during Śravaṇa always bestow fruit and nourishment,

1.60.s:
viśeṣāddvādaśīyukte budhayukte viśeṣataḥ ..
yathaiva dvādaśī proktā budhaśravaṇasaṃyutā .. 9 ..
1.60.d:
विशेषाद्द्वादशीयुक्ते बुधयुक्ते विशेषतः ॥
यथैव द्वादशी प्रोक्ता बुधश्रवणसंयुता ॥ 9 ॥
1.60.m: especially when combined with the twelfth day, and even more so when combined with Wednesday. / Just as the twelfth day joined with Wednesday and Śravaṇa has been described,

1.60.s:
tṛtīyā ca tathā jñeyā sarvakāmasamanvitā ..
yathā tṛtīyā dharmajña tathā pañcadaśī śubhā .. 1.60.10 ..
1.60.d:
तृतीया च तथा ज्ञेया सर्वकामसमन्विता ॥
यथा तृतीया धर्मज्ञ तथा पञ्चदशी शुभा ॥ 1.60.10 ॥
1.60.m: so too the third day is to be known as fulfilling all desires; / just as the third day, O knower of dharma, so also the auspicious fifteenth day.

1.60.s:
tryahaḥspṛśe'pi divase copavāse mahāphalaḥ ..
keśavābhyarcane rāma dānajapyādikeṣu ca .. 11 ..
1.60.d:
त्र्यहःस्पृशेऽपि दिवसे चोपवासे महाफलः ॥
केशवाभ्यर्चने राम दानजप्यादिकेषु च ॥ 11 ॥
1.60.m: Fasting even on a day that touches three days yields great fruit, / O Rāma, in the worship of Keśava, and in gifts, recitation of mantras, and the like.

1.60.s:
rāma uvāca ..
tryahaḥspṛgdivasaḥ kīdṛkkadā bhavati vā prabho ..
tasya me saṃśayaṃ brūhi devadeva vṛṣadhvaja .. 12 ..
1.60.d:
राम उवाच ॥
त्र्यहःस्पृग्दिवसः कीदृक्कदा भवति वा प्रभो ॥
तस्य मे संशयं ब्रूहि देवदेव वृषध्वज ॥ 12 ॥
1.60.m: Rāma said: / What kind of day is a day that touches three days, or when does it occur, O Lord? / Clear that doubt of mine, O God of gods, O You whose banner bears a bull.

1.60.s:
śaṃkara uvāca ..
divā vinirgatā yatra vyatītā syāttithirdvija ..
rātri śeṣe tathāveśya bhaviṣyā spṛśatī tithiḥ .. 13 ..
1.60.d:
शंकर उवाच ॥
दिवा विनिर्गता यत्र व्यतीता स्यात्तिथिर्द्विज ॥
रात्रि शेषे तथावेश्य भविष्या स्पृशती तिथिः ॥ 13 ॥
1.60.m: Śaṃkara said: / Where one lunar day passes during daylight, O twice-born, / and having entered at the remainder of the night, the subsequent lunar day touches it—

1.60.s:
tithitritayasaṃsparśādahorātre bhṛgūttama ..
tryahaspṛksa vinirdiṣṭaḥ puṇyaḥ paramapāvana .. 14 ..
1.60.d:
तिथित्रितयसंस्पर्शादहोरात्रे भृगूत्तम ॥
त्र्यहस्पृक्स विनिर्दिष्टः पुण्यः परमपावन ॥ 14 ॥
1.60.m: because of the contact of three lunar days within a single day and night, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / it is designated as touching three days; it is auspicious and supremely purifying.

1.60.s:
tatropoṣya śiraḥsnātaiḥ karttavyaṃ devatārcanam ..
japaṃ homaṃ tathā dānaṃ kāmayadbhirmahatphalam .. 15 ..
1.60.d:
तत्रोपोष्य शिरःस्नातैः कर्त्तव्यं देवतार्चनम् ॥
जपं होमं तथा दानं कामयद्भिर्महत्फलम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.60.m: Having fasted there with heads washed, the worship of deities should be performed / by those desiring great fruit, along with recitation of mantras, oblations, and gifts.

1.60.s:
karmaṇāṃ pariśeṣāṇāmakarmmaṇyaṃ hi taddinam ..
bhojyaṃ trimadhuraṃ rāma brāhmaṇām̐statra bhojayet .. 16..
1.60.d:
कर्मणां परिशेषाणामकर्म्मण्यं हि तद्दिनम् ॥
भोज्यं त्रिमधुरं राम ब्राह्मणाम्̐स्तत्र भोजयेत् ॥ 16॥
1.60.m: For all remaining duties, that day is indeed unsuitable. / There, O Rāma, one should feed brahmins food containing the three sweets.

1.60.s:
mahatpūrṇā bhavatyekā paurṇamāsī dvijottama ..
pratisaṃvatsaraṃ tasyāṃ sopavāso janārdanam ...37..
1.60.d:
महत्पूर्णा भवत्येका पौर्णमासी द्विजोत्तम ॥
प्रतिसंवत्सरं तस्यां सोपवासो जनार्दनम् ॥.37॥
1.60.m: There is one full-moon day called Mahāpūrṇā, O best of the twice-born; / each year, fasting on it and [worshipping] Janārdana,

1.60.s:
yaḥ pūjayati dharmajña tena saṃvatsaraṃ hari ..
pūjitaḥ paurṇamāsīṣu bhavatīti ha niścayaḥ .. 18 ..
1.60.d:
यः पूजयति धर्मज्ञ तेन संवत्सरं हरि ॥
पूजितः पौर्णमासीषु भवतीति ह निश्चयः ॥ 18 ॥
1.60.m: he who worships, O knower of dharma, by him Hari is worshipped / on all full-moon days throughout the year—this is certain.

1.60.s:
tasyāṃ dānaṃ svalpamapi mahadbhavati bhārgava ..
dānaṃ japyaṃ tato homo yaścānyatsukṛtaṃ bhavet .. 39 ..
1.60.d:
तस्यां दानं स्वल्पमपि महद्भवति भार्गव ॥
दानं जप्यं ततो होमो यश्चान्यत्सुकृतं भवेत् ॥ 39 ॥
1.60.m: A gift on that day, even if very small, becomes immense, O descendant of Bhṛgu: / gifts, recitation of mantras, then oblations, and whatever other good deed there may be.

1.60.s:
rāma uvāca ..
saṃvatsare paurṇamāsī mahatpūrvā vṛṣadhvaja ..
kathaṃ jñeyā jagannātha tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ .. 1.60.20 ..
1.60.d:
राम उवाच ॥
संवत्सरे पौर्णमासी महत्पूर्वा वृषध्वज ॥
कथं ज्ञेया जगन्नाथ तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 1.60.20 ॥
1.60.m: Rāma said: / How is that full-moon day called Mahāpūrvā in a year / to be recognised, O Lord of the universe, O You whose banner bears a bull? Tell me who am asking.

1.60.s:
śaṃkara uvāca ..
yasyāṃ pūrṇeṃdunā yogaṃ yāyājjīvo mahābalaḥ ..
paurṇamāsī tu sā jñeyā mahatpūrvā dvijottama .. 21 ..
1.60.d:
शंकर उवाच ॥
यस्यां पूर्णेंदुना योगं यायाज्जीवो महाबलः ॥
पौर्णमासी तु सा ज्ञेया महत्पूर्वा द्विजोत्तम ॥ 21 ॥
1.60.m: Śaṃkara said: / That on which very powerful Jupiter enters conjunction with the full moon— / that full-moon day is to be known as Mahāpūrvā, O best of the twice-born.

1.60.s:
ādityagrahaṇe rāma grahaṇe vā niśābhṛtaḥ ..
upavāsādavāpnoti sarvakilviṣanāśanam .. 22 ..
1.60.d:
आदित्यग्रहणे राम ग्रहणे वा निशाभृतः ॥
उपवासादवाप्नोति सर्वकिल्विषनाशनम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.60.m: During a solar eclipse, O Rāma, or during an eclipse of the moon, / by fasting one attains the destruction of all sins.

1.60.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ tathā japyaṃ cā kṣayyaṃ parikīrttitam ..
śrāddhañca bhārgavaśreṣṭha vahnisaṃpūjanaṃ tathā .. 23 ..
1.60.d:
स्नानं दानं तथा जप्यं चा क्षय्यं परिकीर्त्तितम् ॥
श्राद्धञ्च भार्गवश्रेष्ठ वह्निसंपूजनं तथा ॥ 23 ॥
1.60.m: Bathing, giving gifts, and recitation of mantras are declared imperishable, / as are ancestral rites and the worship of fire, O best of the descendants of Bhṛgu.

1.60.s:
rāma uvāca ..
nakṣatraṃ devadeveśa tithiñcātra vinirgatām ..
dṛṣṭvā yathāvatkartavyaṃ tithiṃ śaṅkara jānatā .. 24 ..
1.60.d:
राम उवाच ॥
नक्षत्रं देवदेवेश तिथिञ्चात्र विनिर्गताम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा यथावत्कर्तव्यं तिथिं शङ्कर जानता ॥ 24 ॥
1.60.m: Rāma said: / Seeing the asterism, O Lord of the god of gods, and the lunar day that has departed here, / how should a man who knows the lunar day perform [his duties], O Śaṅkara?

1.60.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
sā tithistadahorātraṃ yasyāmevodito raviḥ ..
tayā karmāṇi kurvīta hrāsavṛddhirna kāraṇam ..25..
1.60.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
सा तिथिस्तदहोरात्रं यस्यामेवोदितो रविः ॥
तया कर्माणि कुर्वीत ह्रासवृद्धिर्न कारणम् ॥25॥
1.60.m: Śaṅkara said: / That lunar day in which the sun has risen is [the lunar day for] that day and night; / by that day one should perform the rites; decrease or increase is no cause [for change].

1.60.s:
śuklapakṣe tithirjñeyā yasyāmabhyudito raviḥ ..
upoṣitavyaṃ nakṣatraṃ yenāstaṃ yāti bhāskaraḥ .. 26 ..
1.60.d:
शुक्लपक्षे तिथिर्ज्ञेया यस्यामभ्युदितो रविः ॥
उपोषितव्यं नक्षत्रं येनास्तं याति भास्करः ॥ 26 ॥
1.60.m: In the bright fortnight, that lunar day is to be known on which the sun rises; / [and] that lunar mansion is to be observed for fasting under which the sun sets,

1.60.s: yaśca vā yujyate rāma niśīthe śaśinā saha ..27..
1.60.d: यश्च वा युज्यते राम निशीथे शशिना सह ॥27॥
1.60.m: or that which, O Rāma, is joined with the moon at midnight.

1.61.s:
rāma uvāca ..
tasya māyāśarīrasya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ ..
prāpnuvanti kathaṃ sthānaṃ nityamakṣayyamavyayam .. 1 ..
1.61.d:
राम उवाच ॥
तस्य मायाशरीरस्य विष्णोरमिततेजसः ॥
प्राप्नुवन्ति कथं स्थानं नित्यमक्षय्यमव्ययम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.61.m: Rāma said: / How do [men] attain the eternal, imperishable, and immutable abode / of that Viṣṇu of boundless splendour, whose body is māyā?

1.61.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
akhaṇḍakāriṇo rāma viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ ..
prāpnuvanti paraṃ sthānaṃ nityamakṣayyamavyayam .. 2 ..
1.61.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
अखण्डकारिणो राम विष्णोरमिततेजसः ॥
प्राप्नुवन्ति परं स्थानं नित्यमक्षय्यमव्ययम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.61.m: Śaṅkara said: / Those who perform without interruption, O Rāma, attain the supreme, / eternal, imperishable, and immutable abode of Viṣṇu of boundless splendour.

1.61.s:
rāma uvāca ..
akhaṇḍakārī bhagavankathaṃ bhavati śaṅkara ..
etanme saṃśayaṃ brūhi devadeva vṛṣadhvaja .. 3 ..
1.61.d:
राम उवाच ॥
अखण्डकारी भगवन्कथं भवति शङ्कर ॥
एतन्मे संशयं ब्रूहि देवदेव वृषध्वज ॥ 3 ॥
1.61.m: Rāma said: / O Lord, how does one become an uninterrupted performer, O Śaṅkara? / Tell me this doubt, O God of gods whose emblem is the bull.

1.61.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
pañcakālavidhānajñastatkarmakaraṇe rataḥ ..
akhaṇḍakārī bhavati rāma dānavanāśana .. 4 ..
1.61.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
पञ्चकालविधानज्ञस्तत्कर्मकरणे रतः ॥
अखण्डकारी भवति राम दानवनाशन ॥ 4 ॥
1.61.m: Śaṅkara said: / He who knows the ritual of the five times and is devoted to the performance of its rites / becomes an uninterrupted performer, O Rāma, destroyer of the Dānavas.

1.61.s:
rāma uvāca ..
bhagavanpañca ke kālāḥ kathaṃ teṣāṃ tathā vidhiḥ ..
etanme devadeveśa kautūhalamapānuda .. 5 ..
1.61.d:
राम उवाच ॥
भगवन्पञ्च के कालाः कथं तेषां तथा विधिः ॥
एतन्मे देवदेवेश कौतूहलमपानुद ॥ 5 ॥
1.61.m: Rāma said: / O Lord, what are the five times, and how is their rule? / Dispel this curiosity of mine, O God of gods.

1.61.s:
śaṅkara uvāca ..
rāmābhigamanaṃ pūrvamupādānamataḥ param ..
ijyāsvādhyāyakālau ca yogakālastathaiva ca ..6..
1.61.d:
शङ्कर उवाच ॥
रामाभिगमनं पूर्वमुपादानमतः परम् ॥
इज्यास्वाध्यायकालौ च योगकालस्तथैव च ॥6॥
1.61.m: Śaṅkara said: / O Rāma, the first is approaching (abhigamana), next to that is gathering materials (upādāna), / and the times of worship (ijyā) and self-study (svādhyāya), and likewise the time of union (yoga).

1.61.s:
teṣāṃ pratyekaśo vakṣye vidhiṃ te bhṛgunandana ..
tannibodha mahābhāga prayatenāntarātmanā .. 7 ..
1.61.d:
तेषां प्रत्येकशो वक्ष्ये विधिं ते भृगुनन्दन ॥
तन्निबोध महाभाग प्रयतेनान्तरात्मना ॥ 7 ॥
1.61.m: I shall speak their rule to you individually, O son of Bhṛgu; / understand that, O fortunate one, with a restrained inner self.

1.61.s:
rāma kalye samutthāya dantadhāvanapūrvakam ..
snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāśāstraṃ svācāntaḥ susamāhitaḥ .. 8 ..
1.61.d:
राम कल्ये समुत्थाय दन्तधावनपूर्वकम् ॥
स्नानं कृत्वा यथाशास्त्रं स्वाचान्तः सुसमाहितः ॥ 8 ॥
1.61.m: O Rāma, having risen at dawn, preceded by the cleansing of the teeth, / having bathed according to the scriptures, having sipped water properly, highly concentrated,

1.61.s:
yaśceha bhagavanmantraṃ paṭhandevagṛhaṃ viśet ..
pravindyādrāma jānubhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ śirasā tathā .. 9 ..
1.61.d:
यश्चेह भगवन्मन्त्रं पठन्देवगृहं विशेत् ॥
प्रविन्द्याद्राम जानुभ्यां पाणिभ्यां शिरसा तथा ॥ 9 ॥
1.61.m: and reciting the mantra of the Lord here, one should enter the house of the deity; / one should bow, O Rāma, with both knees, both hands, and the head.

1.61.s:
oṃkāraṃ sanamaskāraṃ prayujya susamāhitaḥ ..
yogakālaṃ tu sandadhyādupādadhyādanantaram..1.61.10..
1.61.d:
ओंकारं सनमस्कारं प्रयुज्य सुसमाहितः ॥
योगकालं तु सन्दध्यादुपादध्यादनन्तरम्॥1.61.10॥
1.61.m: Having applied the syllable Om together with obeisance, highly concentrated, / one should contemplate the time of union, and then take up [the ritual].

1.61.s:
rāmābhigamakālaṃ tu tatra mantraṃ tathārpayet..
bhagavato baleneti vīryeṇaitena tejasā..11..
1.61.d:
रामाभिगमकालं तु तत्र मन्त्रं तथार्पयेत्॥
भगवतो बलेनेति वीर्येणैतेन तेजसा॥11॥
1.61.m: At the time of approaching, O Rāma, one should offer the mantra there: / 'By the power, by this valour, by the splendour of the Lord.'

1.61.s:
suprakīrtitatoyena vediṃ prakṣālayedbudhaḥ ..
sauvarṇīṃ rājatīṃ tāmrīṃ mṛnmayīmāyasīṃ tathā..12..
1.61.d:
सुप्रकीर्तिततोयेन वेदिं प्रक्षालयेद्बुधः ॥
सौवर्णीं राजतीं ताम्रीं मृन्मयीमायसीं तथा॥12॥
1.61.m: The wise man should wash the altar with well-renowned water, / [an altar] made of gold, silver, copper, clay, or iron,

1.61.s:
