दत्त्वोवाच स तं रामं हुताशनसमप्रभम् ॥
पश्चिमेन समुद्रेण प्रविश्य वरुणालयम्॥9 ॥
1.68.m:
Having given it, he spoke to that Rāma, whose splendour was equal to the sacrificial fire:
“Entering by the western ocean into the abode of Varuṇa,

1.68.s:
saṃpūjya varuṇaṃ rāmastasyaivānumate tadā..
śakraśatrūndurācārānpātālanilayañjahi ..
anena cāparatnena vaiṣṇavena mahābala ..
daiteyānsamare hatvā gatvā ca varuṇālayam.. 1.68.10 ..
1.68.d:
संपूज्य वरुणं रामस्तस्यैवानुमते तदा॥
शक्रशत्रून्दुराचारान्पातालनिलयञ्जहि ॥
अनेन चापरत्नेन वैष्णवेन महाबल ॥
दैतेयान्समरे हत्वा गत्वा च वरुणालयम्॥ 1.68.10 ॥
1.68.m:
having worshipped Varuṇa, O Rāma, and with his permission at that time,
slay the wicked enemies of Śakra who dwell in Pātāla.
Having slain the Daiteyas in battle with this jewel of a bow of Viṣṇu, O one of great might,
and having gone to the abode of Varuṇa,

1.68.s:
praṣṭavyo varuṇo devastvayā dharmānsanātanān ..
sa putra varuṇāddharmāñchrutvā rāma yathāvidhi .. 11 ..
1.68.d:
प्रष्टव्यो वरुणो देवस्त्वया धर्मान्सनातनान् ॥
स पुत्र वरुणाद्धर्माञ्छ्रुत्वा राम यथाविधि ॥ 11 ॥
1.68.m:
the god Varuṇa must be questioned by you regarding the eternal dharmas.
Having heard, O son, the dharmas from Varuṇa in accordance with injunction, O Rāma,

1.68.s:
āgacchethā yathākālaṃ matsamīpaṃ mahābhuja ..
evamuktastadā rāmaḥ pitrā dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ .. 12 ..
1.68.d:
आगच्छेथा यथाकालं मत्समीपं महाभुज ॥
एवमुक्तस्तदा रामः पित्रा धर्मभृतां वरः ॥ 12 ॥
1.68.m:
you should return to my presence in due time, O mighty-armed one.”
Having been spoken to thus at that time by his father, the best of the upholders of dharma,

1.68.s:
pitaraṃ mātaraṃ bhrātṝnabhivādya yathāvidhi ..
jagāma varuṇāvāsaṃ rāmo vaiśvānaradyutiḥ .. 13 ..
1.68.d:
पितरं मातरं भ्रातॄनभिवाद्य यथाविधि ॥
जगाम वरुणावासं रामो वैश्वानरद्युतिः ॥ 13 ॥
1.68.m:
Rāma, of the splendour of the sacrificial fire, having greeted his father, mother, and brothers in accordance with injunction,
went to the dwelling of Varuṇa.

1.68.s:
sa praviśya samudreṇa mahādevaprasādataḥ ..
tato'śma nagaraṃ rāmo dadarśa puramuttamam .. 14 ..
1.68.d:
स प्रविश्य समुद्रेण महादेवप्रसादतः ॥
ततोऽश्म नगरं रामो ददर्श पुरमुत्तमम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.68.m:
Having entered by the ocean by the grace of Mahādeva,
Rāma then beheld the excellent city, the stone city [Aśmanagara],

1.68.s:
mano'bhirāmaṃ sphaṭikāśmacitraṃ turaṅganāgendrakulākulaṃ ca ..
vibhūṣitaṃ pannagadaityanāthairudyānavāpīśata saṃkulaṃ ca .. 15 ..
1.68.d:
मनोऽभिरामं स्फटिकाश्मचित्रं तुरङ्गनागेन्द्रकुलाकुलं च ॥
विभूषितं पन्नगदैत्यनाथैरुद्यानवापीशत संकुलं च ॥ 15 ॥
1.68.m:
delightful to the mind, adorned with crystal stones, crowded with herds of horses and lordly elephants,
adorned with lords of serpents and Daityas, and filled with hundreds of gardens and ponds.

1.69.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
tasminpuravare ramye ratnacitrasabhāgatam ..
ratnāsanagataṃ vīraṃ cārukuṇḍalalocanam .. 1 ..
1.69.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
तस्मिन्पुरवरे रम्ये रत्नचित्रसभागतम् ॥
रत्नासनगतं वीरं चारुकुण्डललोचनम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.69.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In that charming, excellent city, [he saw] the hero seated in an assembly hall varied with jewels,
seated on a jewelled throne, with lovely earrings and eyes,

1.69.s:
snigdhavaiḍūryasaṃkāśaṃ śuklāmbaravibhūṣitam ..
hārabhārārpitatanuṃ cārukesaradhāriṇam .. 2 ..
1.69.d:
स्निग्धवैडूर्यसंकाशं शुक्लाम्बरविभूषितम् ॥
हारभारार्पिततनुं चारुकेसरधारिणम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.69.m:
resembling glossy lapis lazuli, adorned with white garments,
his body laden with a burden of garlands, wearing lovely saffron,

1.69.s:
pravālamaṇimuktāḍhyaṃ gambhīraṃ bhujagāśrayam ..
kirīṭottaṃsasaṃchannaṃ yādogaṇasamāśrayam .. 3 ..
1.69.d:
प्रवालमणिमुक्ताढ्यं गम्भीरं भुजगाश्रयम् ॥
किरीटोत्तंससंछन्नं यादोगणसमाश्रयम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.69.m:
rich in coral, gems, and pearls, profound, the refuge of serpents,
covered with a diadem and crest-ornament, the refuge of hosts of aquatic monsters,

1.69.s:
ādityamudakāvāsamaṃbhasāṃ patimūrjitam ..
lokanāthaṃ mahadbhūtaṃ bhaktānāmabhayapradam .. 4 ..
1.69.d:
आदित्यमुदकावासमंभसां पतिमूर्जितम् ॥
लोकनाथं महद्भूतं भक्तानामभयप्रदम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.69.m:
the Āditya whose abode is the waters, the powerful lord of waters,
the protector of the world, the mighty being, who grants fearlessness to devotees,

1.69.s:
viṣṇorbhāgaṃ viśālāṃsaṃ viśālākṣaṃ mahābhujam ..
sevyamānaṃ mahābhāgaistridaśairbrāhmaṇaistathā .. 5 ..
1.69.d:
विष्णोर्भागं विशालांसं विशालाक्षं महाभुजम् ॥
सेव्यमानं महाभागैस्त्रिदशैर्ब्राह्मणैस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
1.69.m:
a portion of Viṣṇu, broad-shouldered, large-eyed, mighty-armed,
being attended by highly fortunate gods and brahmins,

1.69.s:
daiteyaiśca mahābhāgairbhīmairbhīmaparākramaiḥ ..
sundopasundaśakrākṣaśambarāmarakaṇṭakaiḥ .. 6 ..
1.69.d:
दैतेयैश्च महाभागैर्भीमैर्भीमपराक्रमैः ॥
सुन्दोपसुन्दशक्राक्षशम्बरामरकण्टकैः ॥ 6 ॥
1.69.m:
and by highly fortunate, terrifying Daiteyas of terrifying valour,
Sunda, Upasunda, Śakrākṣa, and Śambara, thorns to the immortals,

1.69.s:
hayagrīvamahāgrīvadaśagrīvasurāntakaiḥ ..
bhīmabhīmākṣanarakavikaṭotkaṭamāraṇaiḥ .. 7 ..
1.69.d:
हयग्रीवमहाग्रीवदशग्रीवसुरान्तकैः ॥
भीमभीमाक्षनरकविकटोत्कटमारणैः ॥ 7 ॥
1.69.m:
Hayagrīva, Mahāgrīva, Daśagrīva, enders of the gods,
Bhīma, Bhīmākṣa, Naraka, Vikaṭa, Utkaṭa, and Māraṇa,

1.69.s:
atikāyamahākāyabhīmakāyabaloddhataiḥ ..
nāgaiśca sumahākāyairmahābhogairjagaddhitaiḥ .. 8 ..
1.69.d:
अतिकायमहाकायभीमकायबलोद्धतैः ॥
नागैश्च सुमहाकायैर्महाभोगैर्जगद्धितैः ॥ 8 ॥
1.69.m:
Atikāya, Mahākāya, and Bhīmakāya, arrogant in strength;
and by very huge-bodied Nāgas of great coils, beneficent to the world,

1.69.s:
nāgarājñā vāsukinā śaṅkhena kuruṇā tathā ..
( mahāpadmena padmena karkoṭakadhanaṃjayaiḥ .. 9 ..
1.69.d:
नागराज्ञा वासुकिना शङ्खेन कुरुणा तथा ॥
( महापद्मेन पद्मेन कर्कोटकधनंजयैः ॥ 9 ॥
1.69.m:
by the king of Nāgas Vāsuki, by Śaṅkha, and by Kuru,
by Mahāpadma, Padma, Karkoṭaka, and Dhanañjaya,

1.69.s:
airāvatena nāgena takṣakeṇa balena ca ..
kaṃbalāśvatarābhyāṃ ca hyāryakeṇa mahātmanā .. 1.69.10 ..)
1.69.d:
ऐरावतेन नागेन तक्षकेण बलेन च ॥
कंबलाश्वतराभ्यां च ह्यार्यकेण महात्मना ॥ 1.69.10 ॥)
1.69.m: with the serpent Airāvata, with Takṣaka, Bala, / Kambala and Aśvatara, and the great-souled Āryaka.

1.69.s:
bālavyajanahastāstamupavījanti nimnagāḥ ..
gaṅgā ca sarayū rājan vitastā yamunā tathā .. 11 ..
1.69.d:
बालव्यजनहस्तास्तमुपवीजन्ति निम्नगाः ॥
गङ्गा च सरयू राजन् वितस्ता यमुना तथा ॥ 11 ॥
1.69.m: Rivers fanned him with chowries in their hands: / the Gaṅgā, the Sarayū, O king, the Vitastā, and the Yamunā,

1.69.s:
irāvatī candrabhāgā narmadā ca mahānadī ..
payoṣṇī brāhmaṇī gaurī vipāśā devikā tathā .. 12 ..
1.69.d:
इरावती चन्द्रभागा नर्मदा च महानदी ॥
पयोष्णी ब्राह्मणी गौरी विपाशा देविका तथा ॥ 12 ॥
1.69.m: the Irāvatī, Candrabhāgā, and the great river Narmadā, / the Payoṣṇī, Brāhmaṇī, Gaurī, Vipāśā, and the Devikā,

1.69.s:
śatadruḥ kampanā sindhustathā cānyāssahasraśaḥ ..
sevyamānastathā kūpaistaḍāgaiśca savigrahaiḥ .. 13 ..
1.69.d:
शतद्रुः कम्पना सिन्धुस्तथा चान्यास्सहस्रशः ॥
सेव्यमानस्तथा कूपैस्तडागैश्च सविग्रहैः ॥ 13 ॥
1.69.m: the Śatadru, Kampanā, and Sindhu, and thousands of others, / attended also by personified wells and ponds,

1.69.s:
sarovaraissāgaraiśca samudraiśca yadūttama ..
taṃ dṛṣṭvā varuṇaṃ rājansa vavande bhṛgūttamaḥ ..14..
1.69.d:
सरोवरैस्सागरैश्च समुद्रैश्च यदूत्तम ॥
तं दृष्ट्वा वरुणं राजन्स ववन्दे भृगूत्तमः ॥14॥
1.69.m: lakes, and oceans, O best of the Yadus. / Beholding that Varuṇa, O king, the foremost of the Bhṛgus bowed to him.

1.69.s:
pūjayāmāsa ca tathā varuṇo'pi bhṛgūttamam ..
pādyārghyācamanīyādyairāsanenodakena ca .. 15..
1.69.d:
पूजयामास च तथा वरुणोऽपि भृगूत्तमम् ॥
पाद्यार्घ्याचमनीयाद्यैरासनेनोदकेन च ॥ 15॥
1.69.m: And Varuṇa also honoured the foremost of the Bhṛgus / with foot-water, arghya, water for sipping, a seat, and water.

1.69.s:
āsīnaśca tadā rāmo daiteyānāṃ vadhe vṛtaḥ ..
mahādevavacassarvaṃ varuṇāya nyavedayata .. 16 ..
1.69.d:
आसीनश्च तदा रामो दैतेयानां वधे वृतः ॥
महादेववचस्सर्वं वरुणाय न्यवेदयत ॥ 16 ॥
1.69.m: Seated then, Rāma, chosen for the slaughter of the Daiteyas, / reported all the words of Mahādeva to Varuṇa.

1.69.s:
sa ca tenābhyanujñāto yayau daityapuraṃ mahat ..
varuṇo'pi mahātejā rāmavākyena yādava .. 17 ..
1.69.d:
स च तेनाभ्यनुज्ञातो ययौ दैत्यपुरं महत् ॥
वरुणोऽपि महातेजा रामवाक्येन यादव ॥ 17 ॥
1.69.m: Permitted by him, he set out for the great city of the Daityas. / Varuṇa too, endowed with great splendour, at Rāma's word, O Yādava,

1.69.s:
saṃvādayāmāsa tadā rāmaṃ raṇakṛtakṣaṇam ..
tadā varuṇadūtebhyo daiteyāḥ śrutavistarāḥ .. 18 ..
1.69.d:
संवादयामास तदा रामं रणकृतक्षणम् ॥
तदा वरुणदूतेभ्यो दैतेयाः श्रुतविस्तराः ॥ 18 ॥
1.69.m: then conversed with Rāma, who was eager for battle. / Then the Daiteyas, hearing the details from Varuṇa’s messengers,

1.69.s:
niṣkramya nagarādrājam̐ścaturaṅgabalānvitāḥ ..
susannaddhāḥ pratīkṣanto rāmamadbhutavikramam .. 1 9..
1.69.d:
निष्क्रम्य नगराद्राजम्̐श्चतुरङ्गबलान्विताः ॥
सुसन्नद्धाः प्रतीक्षन्तो राममद्भुतविक्रमम् ॥ 1 9॥
1.69.m: came out of their city, O king, accompanied by fourfold forces, / well-armoured, awaiting Rāma of wonderful prowess.

1.69.s:
dadṛśuśca mahābhāgaṃ varacāpadharaṃ tadā ..
mṛtyorbhujamivodagraṃ lokākarṣaṇatatparama . .. 1.69.20 ..
1.69.d:
ददृशुश्च महाभागं वरचापधरं तदा ॥
मृत्योर्भुजमिवोदग्रं लोकाकर्षणतत्परम ॥। 1.69.20 ॥
1.69.m: They saw the illustrious one holding an excellent bow, / like the raised arm of Death intent on dragging down the worlds,

1.69.s:
dīptāṃśujālaṃ raṇacaṇḍavegaṃ dhanurdharaṃ kālabhujaprakāśam ..
mahānubhāvaṃ samareṣvajeyaṃ lelihyamānaṃ bhujagendrabāhum ..23 ..
1.69.d:
दीप्तांशुजालं रणचण्डवेगं धनुर्धरं कालभुजप्रकाशम् ॥
महानुभावं समरेष्वजेयं लेलिह्यमानं भुजगेन्द्रबाहुम् ॥23 ॥
1.69.m: a blaze of radiant beams, possessing fierce speed in battle, bearing a bow, resembling the arm of Time, / of great majesty, invincible in conflicts, darting his tongue, with arms like king-serpents.

1.70.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sannaddhaṃ dānavagaṇaṃ patākāśatasaṃkulam ..
nānāprakāravāditraṃ siṃhanādabaloddhatam .. 1 ..
1.70.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
सन्नद्धं दानवगणं पताकाशतसंकुलम् ॥
नानाप्रकारवादित्रं सिंहनादबलोद्धतम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.70.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Seeing the host of Dānavas armed, dense with hundreds of banners, / with musical instruments of diverse kinds, proud in the strength of their lion-roars,

1.70.s:
dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahātejāḥ sajjaṃ cakre mahaddhanuḥ ..
śaraissaṃchādayāmāsa daityasainyaṃ mahābalama .. 2 ..
1.70.d:
दृष्ट्वा रामो महातेजाः सज्जं चक्रे महद्धनुः ॥
शरैस्संछादयामास दैत्यसैन्यं महाबलम ॥ 2 ॥
1.70.m: Rāma of great splendour strung his mighty bow, / and covered the Daitya army of great strength with arrows.

1.70.s:
abhracchāyeva saṃjajñe rāmamuktaiśśilīmukhaiḥ ..
tiryagūrdhvamadhaścaiva śarairvyāptaṃ samantataḥ .. 3 ..
1.70.d:
अभ्रच्छायेव संजज्ञे राममुक्तैश्शिलीमुखैः ॥
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव शरैर्व्याप्तं समन्ततः ॥ 3 ॥
1.70.m: It became like the shade of a cloud with the arrows shot by Rāma; / horizontally, upwards, and downwards, it was covered all around with arrows.

1.70.s:
cāpamaṇḍalamadhyasthaḥ parivepīva bhāskaraḥ ..
dṛṣṭamātreṇa sainyānāṃ cakṣūṃṣyapaharadraṇe.. 4 ..
1.70.d:
चापमण्डलमध्यस्थः परिवेपीव भास्करः ॥
दृष्टमात्रेण सैन्यानां चक्षूंष्यपहरद्रणे॥ 4 ॥
1.70.m: Standing in the midst of his circular bow like the sun within a halo, / by his mere sight he stole the eyes of the armies in battle.

1.70.s:
śarāndhakāre magnāste dānavā duṣṭacetasaḥ ..
rāmasandarśanādeva dṛṣṭe'rke kauśikā yathā .. 5 ..
1.70.d:
शरान्धकारे मग्नास्ते दानवा दुष्टचेतसः ॥
रामसन्दर्शनादेव दृष्टेऽर्के कौशिका यथा ॥ 5 ॥
1.70.m: Those evil-minded Dānavas, plunged into the darkness of arrows, / merely from the sight of Rāma, were like owls when the sun is seen.

1.70.s:
sa dānavānāṃ vyasṛjanrāmo bhāti śilīmukhān ..
sadānavānāṃ madhuvatkusumānāṃ śilīmukhaḥ .. 6 ..
1.70.d:
स दानवानां व्यसृजन्रामो भाति शिलीमुखान् ॥
सदानवानां मधुवत्कुसुमानां शिलीमुखः ॥ 6 ॥
1.70.m: Shooting arrows at the Dānavas, Rāma shone / like a bee [extracting] honey from rutting elephants.

1.70.s:
śarāndhakāre mahati magno matimatāṃ varaḥ ..
māyāṃ kṛtvā tadāgneyīṃ taṃ dadāha śarotkaram .. 7 ..
1.70.d:
शरान्धकारे महति मग्नो मतिमतां वरः ॥
मायां कृत्वा तदाग्नेयीं तं ददाह शरोत्करम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.70.m: The foremost among the intelligent, immersed in that great darkness of arrows, / produced a fiery illusion and burned that shower of arrows.

1.70.s:
śarāndhakāragahanānniṣkrāntāste diteḥ sutāḥ ..
bhārgavaṃ koṣṭakīkṛtya raṇe bibhidurañjasā .. 8 ..
1.70.d:
शरान्धकारगहनान्निष्क्रान्तास्ते दितेः सुताः ॥
भार्गवं कोष्टकीकृत्य रणे बिभिदुरञ्जसा ॥ 8 ॥
1.70.m: Having emerged from that impenetrable thicket of the darkness of arrows, the sons of Diti, / encircling the descendant of Bhṛgu, pierced him swiftly in battle

1.70.s:
pracaṇḍairardhanārācairvatsadantaissacūcukaiḥ ..
varāhakarṇairbhallaiśca kṣurapraiścaṭakānanaiḥ .. 9 ..
1.70.d:
प्रचण्डैरर्धनाराचैर्वत्सदन्तैस्सचूचुकैः ॥
वराहकर्णैर्भल्लैश्च क्षुरप्रैश्चटकाननैः ॥ 9 ॥
1.70.m: with fierce half-nārācas, vatsadanta arrows with nipples, / varāhakarṇas, bhallas, kṣurapras, and sparrow-faced arrows,

1.70.s:
tomarairbhiṇḍipālaiśca pāṣāṇairlaguḍaiśśubhaiḥ ..
khaḍgaiḥ prāsaistathā cakrai'rgadāmusala kampanaiḥ .. 1.70.10 ..
1.70.d:
तोमरैर्भिण्डिपालैश्च पाषाणैर्लगुडैश्शुभैः ॥
खड्गैः प्रासैस्तथा चक्रैऽर्गदामुसल कम्पनैः ॥ 1.70.10 ॥
1.70.m: with tomaras, bhiṇḍipālas, stones, and splendid clubs, / with swords, darts, and discuses, with maces, pestles, and clubs,

1.70.s:
parighairāyasaiśśūlaistriśūlaiśśaktibhistathā ..
sa bādhyamāno'pi raṇe daityanāthāyudhotkaraiḥ .. 11 ..
1.70.d:
परिघैरायसैश्शूलैस्त्रिशूलैश्शक्तिभिस्तथा ॥
स बाध्यमानोऽपि रणे दैत्यनाथायुधोत्करैः ॥ 11 ॥
1.70.m: with iron bars, spears, tridents, and javelins. / Even though assailed in battle by that shower of weapons from the Daitya chiefs,

1.70.s:
na vivyathe mahātejā hutāhutirivānalaḥ ..
yadā śastraprahāraistaṃ na śekussamare dvijam .. 12 ..
1.70.d:
न विव्यथे महातेजा हुताहुतिरिवानलः ॥
यदा शस्त्रप्रहारैस्तं न शेकुस्समरे द्विजम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.70.m: he of great splendour was not shaken, like a fire offered oblations. / When the foremost Daityas in the fight were unable with blows of weapons to slay that twice-born in battle,

1.70.s:
hantuṃ daityavarā yuddhe cakrurastraṃ tadā mahat ..
ayaśśaṅkurmahātejā rājā daityagaṇasya yaḥ .. 13 ..
1.70.d:
हन्तुं दैत्यवरा युद्धे चक्रुरस्त्रं तदा महत् ॥
अयश्शङ्कुर्महातेजा राजा दैत्यगणस्य यः ॥ 13 ॥
1.70.m: they then unleashed a great missile. / The mighty Ayaḥśaṅku, who was king of the host of Daityas,

1.70.s:
sametairdānavaissārdhaṃ rāmaṃ raṇakṛtakṣaṇam ..
śaraiḥ saṃchādayāmāsa divyāstrapratimantritaiḥ .. 14 ..
1.70.d:
समेतैर्दानवैस्सार्धं रामं रणकृतक्षणम् ॥
शरैः संछादयामास दिव्यास्त्रप्रतिमन्त्रितैः ॥ 14 ॥
1.70.m: together with the assembled Dānavas, covered Rāma, / who was eager for battle, with arrows consecrated with celestial missiles.

1.70.s:
astrairastrāṇi saṃvārya dānavendrasya bhārgavaḥ ..
ciccheda saśaraṃ cāpaṃ rukmadaṇḍaṃ tathā dhvajam .. 15 ..
1.70.d:
अस्त्रैरस्त्राणि संवार्य दानवेन्द्रस्य भार्गवः ॥
चिच्छेद सशरं चापं रुक्मदण्डं तथा ध्वजम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.70.m: Warding off the missiles with missiles, the descendant of Bhṛgu / cut down the bow with its arrow, the golden staff, and the banner of the Dānava king,

1.70.s:
sāratheśca śiraḥ kāyācchirastrāṇavibhūṣitam ..
etatkṛtvā raṇe karma dakṣiṇena sa pāṇinā .. 16 ..
1.70.d:
सारथेश्च शिरः कायाच्छिरस्त्राणविभूषितम् ॥
एतत्कृत्वा रणे कर्म दक्षिणेन स पाणिना ॥ 16 ॥
1.70.m: and the charioteer's head adorned with a helmet from his body. / Performing this feat in battle, with his right hand

1.70.s:
jagrāha paraśuṃ tīkṣṇaṃ daityakāyavidāraṇam ..
padbhyāmākramya vegena samare rathakūbaram .. 17 ..
1.70.d:
जग्राह परशुं तीक्ष्णं दैत्यकायविदारणम् ॥
पद्भ्यामाक्रम्य वेगेन समरे रथकूबरम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.70.m: he seized a sharp axe that tears through Daitya bodies. / Treading upon the yoke of the chariot with speed in the fight,

1.70.s:
nirjīvānpādavegena kṛtvā turagasattamān ..
gadayā ca rathasthasya dānavendrasya saṃyuge .. 18 ..
1.70.d:
निर्जीवान्पादवेगेन कृत्वा तुरगसत्तमान् ॥
गदया च रथस्थस्य दानवेन्द्रस्य संयुगे ॥ 18 ॥
1.70.m: having rendered the finest horses lifeless with the force of his feet, / and with his club [striking] the Dānava king standing in the chariot in the battle,

1.70.s:
jahāra saśirastrāṇaṃ śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam ..
ayaḥśaṅkau hate daitye bhārgavaṃ samare tadā .. 19 ..
1.70.d:
जहार सशिरस्त्राणं शिरो ज्वलितकुण्डलम् ॥
अयःशङ्कौ हते दैत्ये भार्गवं समरे तदा ॥ 19 ॥
1.70.m: he took off his head along with its helmet, with its blazing earrings. / When the Daitya Ayaḥśaṅku had been slain, then in battle

1.70.s:
sarve daityagaṇāḥ kuddhāśchādayāmāsurañjasā ..
astrapuñjaṃ raṇe cchitvā teṣāṃ bhṛgukulodbhavaḥ .. 1.70.20 ..
1.70.d:
सर्वे दैत्यगणाः कुद्धाश्छादयामासुरञ्जसा ॥
अस्त्रपुञ्जं रणे च्छित्वा तेषां भृगुकुलोद्भवः ॥ 1.70.20 ॥
1.70.m: all the hosts of Daityas, enraged, covered the descendant of Bhṛgu swiftly. / Severing their mass of weapons in the battle, the descendant of the Bhṛgu race,

1.70.s:
raṇe ciccheda gātrāṇi śirāṃsi ca mahātapāḥ ..
kṣaṇamātreṇa rāmo'pi daityadehasamākulām .. 21 ..
1.70.d:
रणे चिच्छेद गात्राणि शिरांसि च महातपाः ॥
क्षणमात्रेण रामोऽपि दैत्यदेहसमाकुलाम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.70.m: great in asceticism, severed their limbs and heads in battle. / In a mere moment Rāma also created a river with a flood of blood

1.70.s:
śoṇitaughanadīṃ cakre keśaśaivālaśādvalām ..
bāṇamīnāṃ cāpanakrāṃ chatrahaṃsāvalīṃ tathā .. 22 ..
1.70.d:
शोणितौघनदीं चक्रे केशशैवालशाद्वलाम् ॥
बाणमीनां चापनक्रां छत्रहंसावलीं तथा ॥ 22 ॥
1.70.m: crowded with Daitya bodies, with hair as moss and green grass, / arrows as fish, bows as crocodiles, and rows of parasols as swans,

1.70.s:
pretalokārṇavagamāṃ bhīrukalmaṣavarddhinīm ..
hastiśīrṣopalāṃ raudrāṃ cārutatpucchapannagāma .. 23 ..
1.70.d:
प्रेतलोकार्णवगमां भीरुकल्मषवर्द्धिनीम् ॥
हस्तिशीर्षोपलां रौद्रां चारुतत्पुच्छपन्नगाम ॥ 23 ॥
1.70.m: flowing to the ocean of the world of the dead, increasing the dread of the timid, / having elephant heads as rocks, frightful, with their lovely tails as snakes.

1.70.s:
evaṃ vidhe'pi saṃvṛtte raṇe karmaṇi dānavāḥ ..
taṃ rāmamakṣataṃ dṛṣṭvā hataśeṣāḥ pradudruvuḥ .. 24 ..
1.70.d:
एवं विधेऽपि संवृत्ते रणे कर्मणि दानवाः ॥
तं राममक्षतं दृष्ट्वा हतशेषाः प्रदुद्रुवुः ॥ 24 ॥
1.70.m: When the deed in battle had taken place in this manner, / seeing Rāma unwounded, the surviving Dānavas fled.

1.70.s:
mayatāraprabhṛtayaḥ puraṃ ca viviśustadā ..
palāyamānānsamare na jaghāna sa bhārgavaḥ ..25..||
1.70.d:
मयतारप्रभृतयः पुरं च विविशुस्तदा ॥
पलायमानान्समरे न जघान स भार्गवः ॥25॥॥
1.70.m: Maya, Tāra, and others then entered the city. / The descendant of Bhṛgu did not slay those fleeing in battle.

1.70.s:
kiñciccheṣeṣu daityeṣu vinivṛttastadā raṇāt ..
hatadaityāyutagaṇo rāmo'śmanagaraṃ yayau .. 26 ..
1.70.d:
किञ्चिच्छेषेषु दैत्येषु विनिवृत्तस्तदा रणात् ॥
हतदैत्यायुतगणो रामोऽश्मनगरं ययौ ॥ 26 ॥
1.70.m: With only a few Daityas remaining, having turned back from the fight, / having slain tens of thousands of Daityas, Rāma went to the city of stone.

1.70.s:
rāmapraveśe nagaraṃ varuṇasyājñayā tadā ..
patākādhvajasaṃbādhaṃ kṛtaṃ devairviśeṣavat..27..
1.70.d:
रामप्रवेशे नगरं वरुणस्याज्ञया तदा ॥
पताकाध्वजसंबाधं कृतं देवैर्विशेषवत्॥27॥
1.70.m: Upon Rāma's entry, by Varuṇa's command, / the city was specially crowded with banners and flags by the gods,

1.70.s:
nāgaiśca dānavaiścaiva siktaṃ candanavāriṇā..
dhūpapuñjasamutkṣiptaṃ kusumotkaramaṇḍitam..28..
1.70.d:
नागैश्च दानवैश्चैव सिक्तं चन्दनवारिणा॥
धूपपुञ्जसमुत्क्षिप्तं कुसुमोत्करमण्डितम्॥28॥
1.70.m: sprinkled with sandalwood water by Nāgas and Dānavas, / filled with rising heaps of incense, and adorned with heaps of flowers.

1.70.s:
tataśca sumahātejā varuṇastu vinirgataḥ..
putrapautraiḥ parivṛto rāmapragrahaṇakāraṇāt..29..
1.70.d:
ततश्च सुमहातेजा वरुणस्तु विनिर्गतः॥
पुत्रपौत्रैः परिवृतो रामप्रग्रहणकारणात्॥29॥
1.70.m: Then Varuṇa of great splendour came forth, / surrounded by his sons and grandsons, in order to welcome Rāma.

1.70.s:
saṃpūjyamānaṃ varuṇo rathamāropya ca svakam ..
praveśayāmāsa puraṃ bahutūryapuraskṛtam .. 1.70.30 ...
1.70.d:
संपूज्यमानं वरुणो रथमारोप्य च स्वकम् ॥
प्रवेशयामास पुरं बहुतूर्यपुरस्कृतम् ॥ 1.70.30 ॥।
1.70.m: Mounting the honoured one on his own chariot, / Varuṇa had him enter the city, preceded by many musical instruments.

1.70.s:
rāmapraveśe ca tadā nṛtyanto'psarasāṃ gaṇāḥ ..
gandharvamukhyā gāyanti saṃstuvanti ca bandinaḥ .. 31 ..
1.70.d:
रामप्रवेशे च तदा नृत्यन्तोऽप्सरसां गणाः ॥
गन्धर्वमुख्या गायन्ति संस्तुवन्ति च बन्दिनः ॥ 31 ॥
1.70.m: Upon Rāma's entry, troupes of apsarases danced, / the foremost Gandharvas sang, and bards praised him.

1.70.s:
sa praviśyātha nagaraṃ varuṇasya tathā gṛham ..
uvāsa tatra dharmātmā varuṇena supūjitaḥ .. 32 ..
1.70.d:
स प्रविश्याथ नगरं वरुणस्य तथा गृहम् ॥
उवास तत्र धर्मात्मा वरुणेन सुपूजितः ॥ 32 ॥
1.70.m: Entering the city and the house of Varuṇa, / the righteous one dwelt there, highly honoured by Varuṇa.

1.70.s: dharmāṇāmāgamaṃ kṛtvā varuṇātsasutāttadā .. 33 ...
1.70.d: धर्माणामागमं कृत्वा वरुणात्ससुतात्तदा ॥ 33 ॥।
1.70.m: having received the transmission of dharmas from Varuṇa together with his sons then.

1.70.s:
evaṃ sa rāmaḥ paravīraghātī saṃprāpya yādogaṇanāthaveśma ..
uvāsa putrairvaruṇasya sārdhaṃ saṃpūjitastena jaleśvareṇa .. 34 ..
1.70.d:
एवं स रामः परवीरघाती संप्राप्य यादोगणनाथवेश्म ॥
उवास पुत्रैर्वरुणस्य सार्धं संपूजितस्तेन जलेश्वरेण ॥ 34 ॥
1.70.m: Thus that Rāma, the slayer of enemy heroes, having reached the dwelling of the lord of aquatic creatures, / dwelt together with the sons of Varuṇa, worshipped by that lord of waters.

1.71.s:
.. vajra uvāca ... ..
yatsa śuśrāva dharmātmā varuṇādbhṛgunandana ..
tanmamācakṣva tattvena paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 1 ..
1.71.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥॥।
यत्स शुश्राव धर्मात्मा वरुणाद्भृगुनन्दन ॥
तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन परं कौतूहलं हि मे ॥ 1 ॥
1.71.m: Vajra said: / What that righteous one heard from Varuṇa, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / tell that to me accurately, for my curiosity is great.

1.71.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
jamadagnisuto rāmo varuṇasya gṛhoṣitaḥ ..
kadācidvaruṇaṃ devamidaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 2 ...
1.71.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
जमदग्निसुतो रामो वरुणस्य गृहोषितः ॥
कदाचिद्वरुणं देवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 2 ॥।
1.71.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, dwelling in the house of Varuṇa, / once spoke this word to the god Varuṇa.

1.71.s:
rāma uvāca ..
namaste devadeveśa surāsuragaṇārcita ..
gobrāhmaṇahitāsakta yādogaṇajaleśvara .. 3 ..
1.71.d:
राम उवाच ॥
नमस्ते देवदेवेश सुरासुरगणार्चित ॥
गोब्राह्मणहितासक्त यादोगणजलेश्वर ॥ 3 ॥
1.71.m: Rāma said: / Homage to you, O lord of the gods of gods, worshipped by hosts of gods and asuras, / intent on the welfare of cows and brahmins, O lord of waters and the hosts of aquatic creatures!

1.71.s:
tvaṃ tasya devadevasya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ ..
ayanamṛṣibhiryena viṣṇurnārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 4 ..
1.71.d:
त्वं तस्य देवदेवस्य विष्णोरमिततेजसः ॥
अयनमृषिभिर्येन विष्णुर्नारायणः स्मृतः ॥ 4 ॥
1.71.m: You are the abode of that god of gods, Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendour, / by virtue of which Viṣṇu is remembered by the sages as Nārāyaṇa.

1.71.s:
tvamevedaṃ jagatsarvaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamañca yat ..
brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca tvaccharīre samāśritāḥ .. 9 ..
1.71.d:
त्वमेवेदं जगत्सर्वं स्थावरं जङ्गमञ्च यत् ॥
ब्रह्मा विष्णुश्च रुद्रश्च त्वच्छरीरे समाश्रिताः ॥ 9 ॥
1.71.m: You indeed are this whole world, whatever is immobile and mobile; / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra take refuge in your body.

1.71.s:
tvamindrastvaṃ ca dhanadastvamīśastvaṃ samīraṇaḥ ..
tvamagnistvaṃ yamaścaiva sarvādhārastvamacyutaḥ .. 6 ..
1.71.d:
त्वमिन्द्रस्त्वं च धनदस्त्वमीशस्त्वं समीरणः ॥
त्वमग्निस्त्वं यमश्चैव सर्वाधारस्त्वमच्युतः ॥ 6 ॥
1.71.m: You are Indra, you are Kubera, you are the Lord, you are the wind; / you are Agni and you are Yama, the support of all, you are Acyuta.

1.71.s:
devānāmīśvaraścaiva nāgānāmīśvarastathā ..
sāgarāṇāṃ ca sarasāṃ saritāṃ ca mahābhuja ..7..
1.71.d:
देवानामीश्वरश्चैव नागानामीश्वरस्तथा ॥
सागराणां च सरसां सरितां च महाभुज ॥7॥
1.71.m: The sovereign lord of the gods and likewise the lord of the nāgas, / of oceans, lakes, and rivers, O mighty-armed one;

1.71.s:
kūpavāpītaṭākānāṃ śaucasya paramasya ca ..
viṣṇorvāmasya netrasya śaśāṅkasya mahātmanaḥ .. 8 ..
1.71.d:
कूपवापीतटाकानां शौचस्य परमस्य च ॥
विष्णोर्वामस्य नेत्रस्य शशाङ्कस्य महात्मनः ॥ 8 ॥
1.71.m: of wells, reservoirs, and ponds, and of supreme purity; / of the great-souled moon, which is the left eye of Viṣṇu.

1.71.s:
tvanmayaṃ maṇḍalaṃ deva tvanmayāssarvatārakāḥ ..
tvameva saritāṃ nāthassamudro yādasāṃ patiḥ .. 9..
1.71.d:
त्वन्मयं मण्डलं देव त्वन्मयास्सर्वतारकाः ॥
त्वमेव सरितां नाथस्समुद्रो यादसां पतिः ॥ 9॥
1.71.m: Consisting of you is the lunar orb, O god; consisting of you are all the stars; / you alone are the lord of rivers, the ocean, the master of aquatic creatures.

1.71.s:
ādhārassarvaratnānāṃ vidyānāṃ ca jagatpate ..
tvanmayo dehināṃ prāṇo jīvo rudhirasaṃjñakaḥ .. 1.71.10..
1.71.d:
आधारस्सर्वरत्नानां विद्यानां च जगत्पते ॥
त्वन्मयो देहिनां प्राणो जीवो रुधिरसंज्ञकः ॥ 1.71.10॥
1.71.m: The support of all jewels and sciences, O lord of the world; / consisting of you is the breath of embodied beings, the life known as blood.

1.71.s:
rāmastvaṃ prāṇināṃ deva sarvadevamayo vibhuḥ ..
bhavatā saṃyatā pāśairdānavā deva dāruṇaiḥ .. 11..
1.71.d:
रामस्त्वं प्राणिनां देव सर्वदेवमयो विभुः ॥
भवता संयता पाशैर्दानवा देव दारुणैः ॥ 11॥
1.71.m: You are Rāma, the all-pervading lord consisting of all the gods among living beings; / by you, O god, the dānavas were bound with dreadful nooses.

1.71.s:
pātāladvāramāśritya bhavāṃstiṣṭhati nirbhayaḥ ..
merupṛṣṭhe ca bhagavanpurī te devanirmitā ..12..
1.71.d:
पातालद्वारमाश्रित्य भवांस्तिष्ठति निर्भयः ॥
मेरुपृष्ठे च भगवन्पुरी ते देवनिर्मिता ॥12॥
1.71.m: Taking your stand at the gate of Pātāla, you abide fearless; / and on the ridge of Meru, O venerable one, is your city built by the gods.

1.71.s:
tṛtīyā ca mahābhāga mānasottaramūrdhani ..
puratraye tvaṃ vasasi prākāmyena jaleśvara .. 13..
1.71.d:
तृतीया च महाभाग मानसोत्तरमूर्धनि ॥
पुरत्रये त्वं वससि प्राकाम्येन जलेश्वर ॥ 13॥
1.71.m: And the third, O highly fortunate one, is on the crest of Mānasottara; / you dwell in these three cities according to your will, O lord of waters.

1.71.s:
sarvatra pūjyase devaissarvabhūtabhavodbhava ..
ādhārastvaṃ hi tapasāṃ śaucānāṃ bhuvanasya ca ..14..
1.71.d:
सर्वत्र पूज्यसे देवैस्सर्वभूतभवोद्भव ॥
आधारस्त्वं हि तपसां शौचानां भुवनस्य च ॥14॥
1.71.m: Everywhere you are worshipped by the gods, O origin and dissolution of all beings; / for you are the support of austerities, purities, and the world.

1.71.s:
trailokyaṃ sakalaṃ deva prakṛtirvikṛtiśca te..
mamāpi sumahābhāga prasādasumukho hyasi..15..
1.71.d:
त्रैलोक्यं सकलं देव प्रकृतिर्विकृतिश्च ते॥
ममापि सुमहाभाग प्रसादसुमुखो ह्यसि॥15॥
1.71.m: All the three worlds, O god, are your primary matter and transformation; / towards me also, O highly fortunate one, you are indeed favorably disposed with grace.

1.71.s:
tasmānme bhagavaṃśchindhi saṃśayānmanasi sthitān ..
varuṇa uvāca ..
yatrāsti te saṃśayamastradhāriñchettāsmi te tatra na saṃśayo'tra ..
yathā mameśastripurāntako'sau tathā bhavānme raṇacaṇḍavega.. ...16..
1.71.d:
तस्मान्मे भगवंश्छिन्धि संशयान्मनसि स्थितान् ॥
वरुण उवाच ॥
यत्रास्ति ते संशयमस्त्रधारिञ्छेत्तास्मि ते तत्र न संशयोऽत्र ॥
यथा ममेशस्त्रिपुरान्तकोऽसौ तथा भवान्मे रणचण्डवेग॥ ॥.16॥
1.71.m: Therefore, O venerable one, sever the doubts dwelling in my mind. / Varuṇa said: / Wherever you have a doubt, O weapon-bearer, I shall sever it for you, there is no doubt of this; / just as that destroyer of Tripura is my lord, so are you to me, O you of fierce speed in battle!

1.72.s:
rāma uvāca..
snigdhavaiḍūryasaṃkāśa yādogaṇajaleśvara ..
tvattohaṃ śrotumicchāmi kālasaṃsthā mahābhuja .. 1 ..
1.72.d:
राम उवाच॥
स्निग्धवैडूर्यसंकाश यादोगणजलेश्वर ॥
त्वत्तोहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कालसंस्था महाभुज ॥ 1 ॥
1.72.m: Rāma said: / O you who resemble smooth cat's-eye gem, O lord of waters and aquatic creatures, / I wish to hear from you the determination of time, O mighty-armed one.

1.72.s:
varuṇa uvāca ..
anādinidhanaḥ kālo rudrassaṃkarṣaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
sarvabhūtasamatvācca sa tu rudraḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..2 ..
1.72.d:
वरुण उवाच ॥
अनादिनिधनः कालो रुद्रस्संकर्षणः स्मृतः ॥
सर्वभूतसमत्वाच्च स तु रुद्रः प्रकीर्तितः ॥2 ॥
1.72.m: Varuṇa said: / Time is without beginning or end; it is remembered as Rudra, as Saṃkarṣaṇa; / and on account of its impartiality towards all beings, it is proclaimed as Rudra.

1.72.s:
anādinidhanatvena sa mahānparameśvaraḥ ..
nimeṣādapi sūkṣmatvātsūkṣmasūkṣmataro hyati .. 3 ..
1.72.d:
अनादिनिधनत्वेन स महान्परमेश्वरः ॥
निमेषादपि सूक्ष्मत्वात्सूक्ष्मसूक्ष्मतरो ह्यति ॥ 3 ॥
1.72.m: By virtue of being without beginning or end, it is the great Parameśvara; / and because it is subtler even than the twinkle of an eye, it is exceedingly subtle of the subtle.

1.72.s:
tasya sūkṣmātisūkṣmasya kālasya parameṣṭhinaḥ ..
durvibhāvyā mahābhāga yogināmapi sūkṣmatā .. 4 ..
1.72.d:
तस्य सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मस्य कालस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥
दुर्विभाव्या महाभाग योगिनामपि सूक्ष्मता ॥ 4 ॥
1.72.m: The subtlety of that time, which is subtle beyond the subtle, the supreme ruler, / is difficult to conceive, O highly fortunate one, even for yogins.

1.72.s:
padmapatrasahasraṃ tu sūcyā vai bhidyate yadā ..
samakālaṃ tu tadbhinnamabudho manyate janaḥ .. 5 ..
1.72.d:
पद्मपत्रसहस्रं तु सूच्या वै भिद्यते यदा ॥
समकालं तु तद्भिन्नमबुधो मन्यते जनः ॥ 5 ॥
1.72.m: When a thousand lotus petals are indeed pierced by a needle, / an unwise person thinks that they are pierced at the same time.

1.72.s:
kālakrameṇa tadbhinnaṃ sā tasya dvija sūkṣmatā ..
tasya sūkṣmātisūkṣmasya na cātisahate dvija.. 6 ..
1.72.d:
कालक्रमेण तद्भिन्नं सा तस्य द्विज सूक्ष्मता ॥
तस्य सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मस्य न चातिसहते द्विज॥ 6 ॥
1.72.m: They are pierced through the succession of time; that, O twice-born one, is its subtlety. / And of that which is subtle beyond the subtle, it does not brook excess, O twice-born one.

1.72.s:
nāmasaṃkhyā budhairjñeyā grahagatyanusārataḥ ..
tatra tārāgrahāḥ pañca dvau ca jñeyau mahāgrahau .. 7 ..
1.72.d:
नामसंख्या बुधैर्ज्ञेया ग्रहगत्यनुसारतः ॥
तत्र ताराग्रहाः पञ्च द्वौ च ज्ञेयौ महाग्रहौ ॥ 7 ॥
1.72.m: The enumeration of names should be understood by the wise according to the motion of the planets; / there are five star-planets, and two should be known as great planets.

1.72.s:
upagrahau ca dvau jñeyāvevaṃ proktā nava grahāḥ ..
bhaumajñajīvabhṛgujasaurāstārāgrahāssmṛtāḥ .. 8 ..
1.72.d:
उपग्रहौ च द्वौ ज्ञेयावेवं प्रोक्ता नव ग्रहाः ॥
भौमज्ञजीवभृगुजसौरास्ताराग्रहास्स्मृताः ॥ 8 ॥
1.72.m: And two minor planets are to be known; thus nine planets are spoken of. / Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn are remembered as star-planets.

1.72.s:
candrādityau tathā rāma vijñeyau dvau mahāgrahau ..
upagrahau ca dvau jñeyau rāhuḥ ketuśca bhārgava .. 9 ..
1.72.d:
चन्द्रादित्यौ तथा राम विज्ञेयौ द्वौ महाग्रहौ ॥
उपग्रहौ च द्वौ ज्ञेयौ राहुः केतुश्च भार्गव ॥ 9 ॥
1.72.m: The moon and sun are likewise to be known, O Rāma, as the two great planets; / and Rāhu and Ketu are to be known as the two minor planets, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.72.s:
caṇḍārkagatyā kālasya paricchedamukho yadā ..
tadā tayoḥ pravakṣyāmi gatimāśritya bhārgava .. 1.72.10 ..
1.72.d:
चण्डार्कगत्या कालस्य परिच्छेदमुखो यदा ॥
तदा तयोः प्रवक्ष्यामि गतिमाश्रित्य भार्गव ॥ 1.72.10 ॥
1.72.m: When one seeks the division of time by the motion of the fierce-rayed sun, / then I shall declare it relying on the motion of both, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.72.s:
bhagaṇena samagreṇa jñeyā dvādaśa rāśayaḥ ..
triṃśāṃśaśca tathā rāśerbhāga ityabhidhīyate .. 11 ..
1.72.d:
भगणेन समग्रेण ज्ञेया द्वादश राशयः ॥
त्रिंशांशश्च तथा राशेर्भाग इत्यभिधीयते ॥ 11 ॥
1.72.m: Twelve zodiacal signs are to be known through the entire circle of constellations; / and a thirtieth part of a sign is called a degree.

1.72.s:
ādityādviprakṛṣṭastu bhāge dvādaśake tathā ..
candramāssyāttadā rāma māsārdhena na saṃśayaḥ .. 12 ..
1.72.d:
आदित्याद्विप्रकृष्टस्तु भागे द्वादशके तथा ॥
चन्द्रमास्स्यात्तदा राम मासार्धेन न संशयः ॥ 12 ॥
1.72.m: When the moon is distanced from the sun by twelve degrees, / then, O Rāma, half a month passes, without doubt.

1.72.s:
bhāgadvādaśakenaiva tithyāṃtithyāṃ krameṇa tu ..
candramāḥ kṛṣṇapakṣānte sūryeṇa saha yujyate .. 13 ..
1.72.d:
भागद्वादशकेनैव तिथ्यांतिथ्यां क्रमेण तु ॥
चन्द्रमाः कृष्णपक्षान्ते सूर्येण सह युज्यते ॥ 13 ॥
1.72.m: By twelve degrees successively on each lunar day, / the moon is conjoined with the sun at the end of the dark fortnight.

1.72.s:
sannikarṣādathārabhyaṃ sannikarṣamathā param ..
caṇḍārkayorbudhairmāsaścāndra ityabhidhīyate .. 14 ..
1.72.d:
सन्निकर्षादथारभ्यं सन्निकर्षमथा परम् ॥
चण्डार्कयोर्बुधैर्मासश्चान्द्र इत्यभिधीयते ॥ 14 ॥
1.72.m: Beginning from one conjunction to the next conjunction / of the moon and the fierce-rayed sun, it is called a lunar month by the wise.

1.72.s:
sāvane ca tathā māsi triṃśatsūryodayāssmṛtāḥ ..
ādityarāśibhogena sauro māsaḥ prakīrttitaḥ .. 15 ..
1.72.d:
सावने च तथा मासि त्रिंशत्सूर्योदयास्स्मृताः ॥
आदित्यराशिभोगेन सौरो मासः प्रकीर्त्तितः ॥ 15 ॥
1.72.m: And in a civil month, thirty sunrises are remembered; / a solar month is proclaimed by the sun's passage through a zodiacal sign.

1.72.s:
sarvarkṣaparivartaiśca nākṣatro māsa ucyate ..
tithinaikena divasaścāndramāne prakīrttitaḥ .. 16 ..
1.72.d:
सर्वर्क्षपरिवर्तैश्च नाक्षत्रो मास उच्यते ॥
तिथिनैकेन दिवसश्चान्द्रमाने प्रकीर्त्तितः ॥ 16 ॥
1.72.m: And by complete revolutions through all the asterisms, a sidereal month is declared; / a day in lunar measurement is proclaimed by a single lunar day.

1.72.s:
ahorātreṇa caikena sāvano divasassmṛtaḥ ..
ādityabhāgabhogena sauro divasa ucyate .. 17 ..
1.72.d:
अहोरात्रेण चैकेन सावनो दिवसस्स्मृतः ॥
आदित्यभागभोगेन सौरो दिवस उच्यते ॥ 17 ॥
1.72.m: A civil day is remembered as a single day and night; / a solar day is declared by the sun's passage through a degree.

1.72.s:
candranakṣatrabhogena nākṣatro divasassmṛtaḥ ..
māne māsastu nākṣatraḥ saptaviṃśatibhirdinaiḥ .. 18 ..
1.72.d:
चन्द्रनक्षत्रभोगेन नाक्षत्रो दिवसस्स्मृतः ॥
माने मासस्तु नाक्षत्रः सप्तविंशतिभिर्दिनैः ॥ 18 ॥
1.72.m: A sidereal day is remembered by the moon's passage through an asterism; / but in measurement, a sidereal month consists of twenty-seven days.

1.72.s:
pariśeṣeṣu māseṣu māsastriṃśaddinaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
saureṇābdastu māsena yadā bhavati bhārgava .. 19 ..
1.72.d:
परिशेषेषु मासेषु मासस्त्रिंशद्दिनः स्मृतः ॥
सौरेणाब्दस्तु मासेन यदा भवति भार्गव ॥ 19 ॥
1.72.m: In the remaining months, a month is remembered as thirty days. / When a year consists of solar months, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

1.72.s:
sāvanena tu mānena divasaṃ kena pūryate..
ūnarātrāśca te rāma proktāssaṃvatsareṇa ṣaṭ .. 1.72.20 ..
1.72.d:
सावनेन तु मानेन दिवसं केन पूर्यते॥
ऊनरात्राश्च ते राम प्रोक्तास्संवत्सरेण षट् ॥ 1.72.20 ॥
1.72.m: by what is a day completed in civil measure? / And those deficient nights are declared to be six in a year, O Rāma.

1.72.s:
saurasaṃvatsarasyānte mānena śaśijena tu ..
ekādaśātiricyante dināni bhṛgunandana .. 21 ..
1.72.d:
सौरसंवत्सरस्यान्ते मानेन शशिजेन तु ॥
एकादशातिरिच्यन्ते दिनानि भृगुनन्दन ॥ 21 ॥
1.72.m: At the end of a solar year, by the lunar measure / eleven days are surplus, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.72.s:
samādvaye sāṣṭamāse dinaṣoḍaśakānvite .
nāḍīcatuṣṭayānte tu tasmānmāso'tiricyate .. 22..
1.72.d:
समाद्वये साष्टमासे दिनषोडशकान्विते ।
नाडीचतुष्टयान्ते तु तस्मान्मासोऽतिरिच्यते ॥ 22॥
1.72.m: In two years, eight months, and sixteen days, / at the end of four nāḍīs, a month is therefore surplus.

1.72.s:
sa cādhimāsakaḥ proktaḥ kāmyakarmasu garhitaḥ ..
yadā cāndreṇa mānena pūrṇassaṃvatsaro bhavet .. 23..
1.72.d:
स चाधिमासकः प्रोक्तः काम्यकर्मसु गर्हितः ॥
यदा चान्द्रेण मानेन पूर्णस्संवत्सरो भवेत् ॥ 23॥
1.72.m: And that is declared an intercalary month, censured in rites performed for specific desires. / And when a year is completed by lunar measure,

1.72.s:
tadā nākṣatramānena sa māso vārṣiko bhavet..
evaṃ kālasya sūkṣmasya proktaṃ mānacatuṣṭayam .. 24..
1.72.d:
तदा नाक्षत्रमानेन स मासो वार्षिको भवेत्॥
एवं कालस्य सूक्ष्मस्य प्रोक्तं मानचतुष्टयम् ॥ 24॥
1.72.m: then by sidereal measure that month belongs to the year; / thus the fourfold measure of subtle time has been declared.

1.72.s: yenayena ca mānena yadyatkāryaṃ nibodha tat .. 29 ..
1.72.d: येनयेन च मानेन यद्यत्कार्यं निबोध तत् ॥ 29 ॥
1.72.m: And understand what duty is to be performed by which measure:

1.72.s:
abdāyanaṃ tu grahacārakarma saureṇa mānena sadā vyavasyet ..
satrāṇyupāsyānyatha sāvanena loke ca yatsyādvyavahārakarma .. 26 ..
1.72.d:
अब्दायनं तु ग्रहचारकर्म सौरेण मानेन सदा व्यवस्येत् ॥
सत्राण्युपास्यान्यथ सावनेन लोके च यत्स्याद्व्यवहारकर्म ॥ 26 ॥
1.72.m: One should always determine the year, the solstices, and the motion of the planets by the solar measure, / and long sacrificial sessions and whatever business transactions occur in the world should be governed by the civil [measure].

1.72.s:
syātpūrvakālakṣayapūraṇābhyāṃ cāndreṇa mānena yugaṃ ca rāhoḥ ..
nakṣatrasatrāṇyayanāni cendormānena kuryādbhagaṇātmakena ..27..
1.72.d:
स्यात्पूर्वकालक्षयपूरणाभ्यां चान्द्रेण मानेन युगं च राहोः ॥
नक्षत्रसत्राण्ययनानि चेन्दोर्मानेन कुर्याद्भगणात्मकेन ॥27॥
1.72.m: A yuga of Rāhu and [the calendar adjustments] through subtraction and addition of prior time are determined by the lunar measure; / and one should perform asterism-sacrifices and the solstices of the moon by the measure based on revolutions of constellations.

1.73.s:
varuṇa uvāca ..
laghvakṣarasamā mātrā nimeṣaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ..
ataḥ sūkṣmataraḥ kālo nopalabhyo bhṛgūttama ..1..
1.73.d:
वरुण उवाच ॥
लघ्वक्षरसमा मात्रा निमेषः परिकीर्तितः ॥
अतः सूक्ष्मतरः कालो नोपलभ्यो भृगूत्तम ॥1॥
1.73.m: Varuṇa said: / A measure equal to a short syllable is proclaimed to be a nimeṣa. / Time subtler than this cannot be perceived, O foremost of the Bhṛgus,

1.73.s:
nopalabhyaṃ yathā dravyaṃ susūkṣmaṃ paramāṇutaḥ..
dvau nimeṣau truṭirjñeyā prāṇo daśatruṭiḥ smṛtaḥ..2..
1.73.d:
नोपलभ्यं यथा द्रव्यं सुसूक्ष्मं परमाणुतः॥
द्वौ निमेषौ त्रुटिर्ज्ञेया प्राणो दशत्रुटिः स्मृतः॥2॥
1.73.m: just as matter subtler than an atom cannot be perceived. / Two nimeṣas should be known as a truṭi; a prāṇa is traditionally called ten truṭis.

1.73.s:
vināḍikā tu ṣaṭprāṇāstāḥ ṣaṣṭirnāḍikā matā ..
ahorātraṃ ca tāṣṣaṣṭyā nityametaiḥ prakīrtitam .. 3 ..
1.73.d:
विनाडिका तु षट्प्राणास्ताः षष्टिर्नाडिका मता ॥
अहोरात्रं च ताष्षष्ट्या नित्यमेतैः प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.73.m: Six prāṇas make a vināḍikā; sixty of these are considered a nāḍikā. / And a day-and-night is constantly proclaimed by these to consist of sixty [nāḍikās].

1.73.s:
triṃśanmuhūrtāśca tathā ahorātreṇa kīrtitāḥ ..
tatra pañcadaśa proktā rāma nityaṃ divācarāḥ ||4||
1.73.d:
त्रिंशन्मुहूर्ताश्च तथा अहोरात्रेण कीर्तिताः ॥
तत्र पञ्चदश प्रोक्ता राम नित्यं दिवाचराः ॥4॥
1.73.m: And thirty muhūrtas are likewise declared in a day-and-night; / of these, fifteen, O Rāma, are always said to belong to the day.

1.73.s:
uttarāṃ tu yadā kāṣṭhāṃ kramādākramate raviḥ..
tadā tathā bhavedvṛddhirdivasasya mahābhuja..5..
1.73.d:
उत्तरां तु यदा काष्ठां क्रमादाक्रमते रविः॥
तदा तथा भवेद्वृद्धिर्दिवसस्य महाभुज॥5॥
1.73.m: When the sun gradually advances towards the northern quarter, / then, in that manner, the increase of the day occurs, O mighty-armed one.

1.73.s:
divasaśca yathā rāma vṛddhiṃ samadhigacchati ..
tadāśritamuhūrtānāṃ jñeyā hānistadā tathā .. 6 ...
1.73.d:
दिवसश्च यथा राम वृद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
तदाश्रितमुहूर्तानां ज्ञेया हानिस्तदा तथा ॥ 6 ॥।
1.73.m: And as the day, O Rāma, attains increase, / a corresponding decrease of the muhūrtas belonging to it is then to be known.

1.73.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ ca yadā kāṣṭhāṃ kramādākramate raviḥ ..
divasasya tadā hānirjñātavyā nityameva tu .. 7 ..
1.73.d:
दक्षिणां च यदा काष्ठां क्रमादाक्रमते रविः ॥
दिवसस्य तदा हानिर्ज्ञातव्या नित्यमेव तु ॥ 7 ॥
1.73.m: And when the sun gradually advances towards the southern quarter, / a decrease of the day is then always to be understood.

1.73.s:
kṣīyante dinahānau tu tanmuhūrtāstathaiva ca ..
rātryāśritāśca vardhante rātrivṛddhau tathātathā .. 8..
1.73.d:
क्षीयन्ते दिनहानौ तु तन्मुहूर्तास्तथैव च ॥
रात्र्याश्रिताश्च वर्धन्ते रात्रिवृद्धौ तथातथा ॥ 8॥
1.73.m: Its muhūrtas likewise decrease with the decrease of the day, / and those belonging to the night increase accordingly with the increase of the night.

1.73.s:
yadā meṣaṃ sahasrāṃśustulāṃ ca pratipadyate ..
samarātrirdinaḥ kālo viṣuvacchabdavācakaḥ ..9..
1.73.d:
यदा मेषं सहस्रांशुस्तुलां च प्रतिपद्यते ॥
समरात्रिर्दिनः कालो विषुवच्छब्दवाचकः ॥9॥
1.73.m: When the thousand-rayed [sun] enters Aries and Libra, / the time has equal night and day, designated by the word 'equinox'.

1.73.s:
tatra dānaṃ svalpamapi mahadbhavati bhārgava ..
śrāddhaṃ japyaṃ hutaṃ dattaṃ yaccānyatsukṛtaṃ bhavet .. 1.73.10 ..
1.73.d:
तत्र दानं स्वल्पमपि महद्भवति भार्गव ॥
श्राद्धं जप्यं हुतं दत्तं यच्चान्यत्सुकृतं भवेत् ॥ 1.73.10 ॥
1.73.m: On that [occasion], even a very small gift becomes great, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / as does a śrāddha, recitation, oblation, gift, and whatever other meritorious act there may be.

1.73.s:
sūryasaṃkramaṇasyānte sauro māsassamāpyate ..
sauramāsadvayaṃ rāma ṛturityabhidhīyate .. 11 ..
1.73.d:
सूर्यसंक्रमणस्यान्ते सौरो मासस्समाप्यते ॥
सौरमासद्वयं राम ऋतुरित्यभिधीयते ॥ 11 ॥
1.73.m: At the conclusion of the sun’s transit, a solar month is completed; / two solar months, O Rāma, are called a season.

1.73.s:
ṛtutrayaṃ cāyanaṃ syāttaddvayaṃ ca samā smṛtā ..
devatānāmahorātraṃ sa ca rāma prakīrtitaḥ .. 12 ..
1.73.d:
ऋतुत्रयं चायनं स्यात्तद्द्वयं च समा स्मृता ॥
देवतानामहोरात्रं स च राम प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 12 ॥
1.73.m: Three seasons make a solstice-half, and two of those are considered a year. / And that, O Rāma, is proclaimed to be a day-and-night of the deities.

1.73.s:
meṣādiṣaṭkage sūrye teṣāṃ divasa ucyate ...
tulādiṣaṭkage sūrye teṣāṃ rātriḥ prakīrtitā .. 13..
1.73.d:
मेषादिषट्कगे सूर्ये तेषां दिवस उच्यते ॥।
तुलादिषट्कगे सूर्ये तेषां रात्रिः प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 13॥
1.73.m: When the sun is in the six signs beginning with Aries, it is said to be their day; / when the sun is in the six signs beginning with Libra, it is proclaimed to be their night.

1.73.s:
pitṝṇāṃ cāṃdramāsena ahorātrobhidhīyate ..
kṛṣṇapakṣāṣṭamīmadhye teṣāṃ rātryudayaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 14 ..
1.73.d:
पितॄणां चांद्रमासेन अहोरात्रोभिधीयते ॥
कृष्णपक्षाष्टमीमध्ये तेषां रात्र्युदयः स्मृतः ॥ 14 ॥
1.73.m: A day-and-night of the ancestors is defined by a lunar month; / the rising of their night is remembered to take place in the middle of the eighth day of the dark fortnight.

1.73.s:
śuklapakṣāṣṭamīmadhye teṣāmastamayastathā..
ardharātraḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ pitṝṇāṃ samudāhṛtaḥ..15..
1.73.d:
शुक्लपक्षाष्टमीमध्ये तेषामस्तमयस्तथा॥
अर्धरात्रः पौर्णमास्यां पितॄणां समुदाहृतः॥15॥
1.73.m: Likewise, their sunset occurs in the middle of the eighth day of the bright fortnight; / midnight of the ancestors is said to be on the full-moon day.

1.73.s:
kṛṣṇapakṣāvasāne ca teṣāṃ madhyāhna ucyate ..
kṛṣṇapakṣakṣaye tasmātteṣāṃ śrāddhaṃ pradīyate ..
kṛṣṇapakṣakṣaye śrāddhaṃ yaśca nityaṃ kariṣyati ..
satataṃ tarpitāstena bhavanti pitaro'vyayāḥ .. 16 ..
1.73.d:
कृष्णपक्षावसाने च तेषां मध्याह्न उच्यते ॥
कृष्णपक्षक्षये तस्मात्तेषां श्राद्धं प्रदीयते ॥
कृष्णपक्षक्षये श्राद्धं यश्च नित्यं करिष्यति ॥
सततं तर्पितास्तेन भवन्ति पितरोऽव्ययाः ॥ 16 ॥
1.73.m: And their midday is said to be at the end of the dark fortnight; / therefore, a śrāddha is offered to them at the end of the dark fortnight. / And whoever will constantly perform a śrāddha at the end of the dark fortnight, / by him the imperishable ancestors are continually satisfied.

1.73.s:
samā śatairdvādaśabhirdivyaistiṣyayugaṃ smṛtam ..
dviguṇaṃ dvāparaṃ jñeyaṃ tretā triguṇamucyate .. 17 ..
1.73.d:
समा शतैर्द्वादशभिर्दिव्यैस्तिष्ययुगं स्मृतम् ॥
द्विगुणं द्वापरं ज्ञेयं त्रेता त्रिगुणमुच्यते ॥ 17 ॥
1.73.m: The Kali age is taught to consist of twelve hundred divine years; / the Dvāpara age should be known as double that, and the Tretā age is said to be triple that.

1.73.s:
caturguṇaṃ kṛtaṃ proktaṃ piṇḍitaṃ cābdasaṃkhyayā ..
caturyugaṃ sahasrāṇi rāma dvādaśa kīrtitam ..18..
1.73.d:
चतुर्गुणं कृतं प्रोक्तं पिण्डितं चाब्दसंख्यया ॥
चतुर्युगं सहस्राणि राम द्वादश कीर्तितम् ॥18॥
1.73.m: The Kṛta age is said to be quadruple; and aggregated by count of years, / the four ages are proclaimed, O Rāma, to be twelve thousand [divine years].

1.73.s:
ataḥ paraṃ yugāvasthāṃ nibodha gadato mama ..
catuṣpātsakalo dharmastathā brahmottaraṃ jagat .. 19..
1.73.d:
अतः परं युगावस्थां निबोध गदतो मम ॥
चतुष्पात्सकलो धर्मस्तथा ब्रह्मोत्तरं जगत् ॥ 19॥
1.73.m: Henceforth, hear from me as I speak the condition of the ages: / [In the Kṛta age], dharma has all four legs intact, and the world is led by the brahmins.

1.73.s:
śvetavarṇo harirdevo jñānanityāśca mānavāḥ ..
catvāryabdasahasrāṇi teṣāmāyuḥ prakīrtitam .. 1.73.20 ..
1.73.d:
श्वेतवर्णो हरिर्देवो ज्ञाननित्याश्च मानवाः ॥
चत्वार्यब्दसहस्राणि तेषामायुः प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 1.73.20 ॥
1.73.m: Lord Hari is white in color, and humans are devoted to knowledge; / their lifespan is proclaimed to be four thousand years.

1.73.s:
samānavīryyāśca narāstatra nāstyadharottaram ..
tripādavigraho dharmo rāma tretāyuge tadā .. 21 ..
1.73.d:
समानवीर्य्याश्च नरास्तत्र नास्त्यधरोत्तरम् ॥
त्रिपादविग्रहो धर्मो राम त्रेतायुगे तदा ॥ 21 ॥
1.73.m: And men are of equal strength; there is no inferiority or superiority there. / Then, O Rāma, in the Tretā age, dharma has a three-legged body.

1.73.s:
keśave raktatāṃ yāte narā daśaśatāyuṣaḥ ..
yajñe śubhe pravartante nityaṃ hiṃsātmakeṣu ca .. 22 ..
1.73.d:
केशवे रक्ततां याते नरा दशशतायुषः ॥
यज्ञे शुभे प्रवर्तन्ते नित्यं हिंसात्मकेषु च ॥ 22 ॥
1.73.m: When Keśava has assumed a red color, men have a lifespan of a thousand years; / they constantly engage in auspicious sacrifices and those that involve violence.

1.73.s:
jagatkṣatrottaraṃ caiva tadā bhavati bhārgava ..
dvipādavigraho dharmaḥ pītatāmacyute gate .. 23 ...
1.73.d:
जगत्क्षत्रोत्तरं चैव तदा भवति भार्गव ॥
द्विपादविग्रहो धर्मः पीततामच्युते गते ॥ 23 ॥।
1.73.m: And the world then becomes dominated by the kṣatriyas, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / When Acyuta has attained yellowness, dharma has a two-legged body.

1.73.s:
samāḥ śatāni catvāri tadā jīvanti mānavāḥ..
yuddhaśauṇḍā mahotsāhā lokā vaiśyottarāstadā ..24 ..
1.73.d:
समाः शतानि चत्वारि तदा जीवन्ति मानवाः॥
युद्धशौण्डा महोत्साहा लोका वैश्योत्तरास्तदा ॥24 ॥
1.73.m: Humans then live for four hundred years; / men are skilled in battle, full of great energy, and dominated by the vaiśyas.

1.73.s:
jāyante śāstrabhedāśca matibhedāstathaiva ca ..
svalpamāyurnṛṇāṃ buddhvā viṣṇurmānuṣarūpadhṛk .. 29 ..
1.73.d:
जायन्ते शास्त्रभेदाश्च मतिभेदास्तथैव च ॥
स्वल्पमायुर्नृणां बुद्ध्वा विष्णुर्मानुषरूपधृक् ॥ 29 ॥
1.73.m: Divisions of scripture arise, as well as divisions of thought. / Recognizing the short lifespan of mortals, Viṣṇu, assuming a human form,

1.73.s:
ekameva yajurvedaṃ caturdhā vyabhajatpunaḥ ..
tasya śiṣyapraśiṣyāśca vedamekaṃ punaḥpunaḥ .. 26 ..
1.73.d:
एकमेव यजुर्वेदं चतुर्धा व्यभजत्पुनः ॥
तस्य शिष्यप्रशिष्याश्च वेदमेकं पुनःपुनः ॥ 26 ॥
1.73.m: divided the single Yajurveda once again into four. / And his disciples and grand-disciples, the best of the twice-born,

1.73.s:
śākhābhedasahasreṇa vibhajanti dvijottamāḥ ..
ekapādasthite dharme kṛṣṇatāṃ keśave gate .. 27 ..
1.73.d:
शाखाभेदसहस्रेण विभजन्ति द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
एकपादस्थिते धर्मे कृष्णतां केशवे गते ॥ 27 ॥
1.73.m: divide that single Veda again and again into thousands of distinct branches. / When dharma stands on one leg and Keśava has become black,

1.73.s:
dharmabhede samutpanne devatānāmaniścaye ..
na vidyate tadā rāma āyuṣastu viniścayam .. 28..
1.73.d:
धर्मभेदे समुत्पन्ने देवतानामनिश्चये ॥
न विद्यते तदा राम आयुषस्तु विनिश्चयम् ॥ 28॥
1.73.m: when division of dharma has arisen and there is uncertainty regarding the deities, / there is then no certainty of lifespan, O Rāma.

1.73.s:
garbhasthāśca mriyantetra bālyayauvanagāstathā ..
śūdrottarastadā lokastiṣye bhavati bhrārgava .. 29 ..
1.73.d:
गर्भस्थाश्च म्रियन्तेत्र बाल्ययौवनगास्तथा ॥
शूद्रोत्तरस्तदा लोकस्तिष्ये भवति भ्रार्गव ॥ 29 ॥
1.73.m: In this [age], they die while in the womb, and likewise in childhood and youth; / in the Kali age, O descendant of Bhṛgu, the world becomes dominated by the śūdras.

1.73.s:
surapratiṣṭhā dharmaśca tadā bhavati bhūtale ..
pāpiṣṭho vardhate rāma dharmiṣṭhaḥ kṣīyate tadā .. 1.73.30 ...
1.73.d:
सुरप्रतिष्ठा धर्मश्च तदा भवति भूतले ॥
पापिष्ठो वर्धते राम धर्मिष्ठः क्षीयते तदा ॥ 1.73.30 ॥।
1.73.m: At that time, dharma on earth consists of the installation of divine images; / the most sinful person thrives, O Rāma, while the most righteous diminishes.

1.73.s:
rājānaḥ śūdrabhūyiṣṭhāścaurāścārthopajīvinaḥ ..
brāhmaṇāssarvabhakṣyāśca bhavanti bhṛgunandana .. 31 ..
1.73.d:
राजानः शूद्रभूयिष्ठाश्चौराश्चार्थोपजीविनः ॥
ब्राह्मणास्सर्वभक्ष्याश्च भवन्ति भृगुनन्दन ॥ 31 ॥
1.73.m: Kings are mostly śūdras, and thieves live by [stealing] wealth; / and brahmins become consumers of everything, O delight of the Bhṛgus.

1.73.s:
dharmaniṣṭhaściraṃ rājā na tadā rāma jīvati ..
tasminkāle sukṛtināṃ bhaktirbhavati keśave .. 32 ..
1.73.d:
धर्मनिष्ठश्चिरं राजा न तदा राम जीवति ॥
तस्मिन्काले सुकृतिनां भक्तिर्भवति केशवे ॥ 32 ॥
1.73.m: A king devoted to dharma does not live long then, O Rāma. / At that time, devotion to Keśava arises in virtuous persons;

1.73.s:
teṣāmalpena kālena toṣamāyāti keśavaḥ ..
dhanyāḥ kaliyuge rāma tapastapsyanti mānavāḥ .. 33..
1.73.d:
तेषामल्पेन कालेन तोषमायाति केशवः ॥
धन्याः कलियुगे राम तपस्तप्स्यन्ति मानवाः ॥ 33॥
1.73.m: Keśava comes to satisfaction with them in a short time. / Fortunate are the humans, O Rāma, who will practice asceticism in the Kali age;

1.73.s:
tapasālpena te siddhiṃ prāpsyantīti ca niścayaḥ ..
caturyugaikasaptatyā manvantaramihocyate .. 34..
1.73.d:
तपसाल्पेन ते सिद्धिं प्राप्स्यन्तीति च निश्चयः ॥
चतुर्युगैकसप्तत्या मन्वन्तरमिहोच्यते ॥ 34॥
1.73.m: they will attain perfection with little asceticism—this is certain. / A manvantara is declared here to consist of seventy-one cycles of the four ages.

1.73.s:
kalpastu rāma vijñeyo manavastu caturdaśa ..
ādimadhyāntarāleṣu manūnāṃ bhṛgusattam .. 39 ..
1.73.d:
कल्पस्तु राम विज्ञेयो मनवस्तु चतुर्दश ॥
आदिमध्यान्तरालेषु मनूनां भृगुसत्तम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.73.m: An aeon, O Rāma, should be known [to comprise] fourteen Manus; / at the beginning, middle, and intervals between the Manus, O best of the Bhṛgus,

1.73.s:
kṛtamānapramāṇena sandhirbhavati mānada ..
caturyugasahasraṃ tu kalpamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ .. 36 ...
1.73.d:
कृतमानप्रमाणेन सन्धिर्भवति मानद ॥
चतुर्युगसहस्रं तु कल्पमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥ 36 ॥।
1.73.m: there is a transition period of the measure of the Kṛta age, O giver of honor. / Sages declare an aeon to be a thousand cycles of the four ages.

1.73.s:
kalpaśca divasaḥ prokto brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ ..
tāvatī ca niśā tasya yasyāṃ śete sa bhārgava..37..
1.73.d:
कल्पश्च दिवसः प्रोक्तो ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः ॥
तावती च निशा तस्य यस्यां शेते स भार्गव॥37॥
1.73.m: And an aeon is declared to be a day of Brahmā Parameṣṭhin; / his night, during which he sleeps, is of the same length, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.73.s:
evaṃvidhairahorātrairdinamāsādisaṃkhyayā..
pūrṇaṃ varṣaśataṃ sarvaṃ brahmā bhārgava jīvati..38..
1.73.d:
एवंविधैरहोरात्रैर्दिनमासादिसंख्यया॥
पूर्णं वर्षशतं सर्वं ब्रह्मा भार्गव जीवति॥38॥
1.73.m: By such days-and-nights, reckoned by days, months, and the like, / Brahmā lives for a full hundred years, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.73.s:
brahmāyuṣā paricchinnaḥ pauruṣo divasaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
tāvatī ca niśā tasya yasyedaṃ sakalaṃ jagat .. 39 ..
1.73.d:
ब्रह्मायुषा परिच्छिन्नः पौरुषो दिवसः स्मृतः ॥
तावती च निशा तस्य यस्येदं सकलं जगत् ॥ 39 ॥
1.73.m: Measured by the lifespan of Brahmā is remembered to be a day of the Cosmic Person; / of the same length is his night, to whom this entire world belongs.

1.73.s:
evaṃ vidhā ye divasā vyatītā na cāgatā ye ca mahānubhāva ..
anādisattvātparameśvarasya hyānantyabhāvāśca tathā tvasaṃkhyā .. 1.73.40 ..
1.73.d:
एवं विधा ये दिवसा व्यतीता न चागता ये च महानुभाव ॥
अनादिसत्त्वात्परमेश्वरस्य ह्यानन्त्यभावाश्च तथा त्वसंख्या ॥ 1.73.40 ॥
1.73.m: Such are the days that have passed and those that are yet to come, O noble one; / indeed, because the Supreme Lord has no beginning and because He is infinite, they are countless.

1.74.s:
vajra uvāca ..
yadetaduktaṃ rāmasya varuṇena mahātmanā ..
etacchrutvā tu me jātassaṃśayo bhṛgunandana .. 1 ..
1.74.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
यदेतदुक्तं रामस्य वरुणेन महात्मना ॥
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु मे जातस्संशयो भृगुनन्दन ॥ 1 ॥
1.74.m: Vajra said: / Having heard this which was spoken to Rāma by the great-souled Varuṇa, / doubt has arisen in me, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.74.s:
asmiṃstu bhārate varṣe parikṣīṇe yuge tathā ..
avasthā yā bhavedbrahmastanme vyākhyātu marhasi .. 2 ..
1.74.d:
अस्मिंस्तु भारते वर्षे परिक्षीणे युगे तथा ॥
अवस्था या भवेद्ब्रह्मस्तन्मे व्याख्यातु मर्हसि ॥ 2 ॥
1.74.m: When an age is exhausted in this land of Bhārata, / what condition comes to pass, O holy one—that you should explain to me.

1.74.s:
..mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
yugeyuge parikṣīṇe varṣe yādava bhārate ..
saṃgrāmeṇa vinaśyaṃti prāyo varṇottamā janāḥ .. 3 ..
1.74.d:
॥मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
युगेयुगे परिक्षीणे वर्षे यादव भारते ॥
संग्रामेण विनश्यंति प्रायो वर्णोत्तमा जनाः ॥ 3 ॥
1.74.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / In each age, when it is exhausted in the land of Bhārata, O Yādava, / mostly the best people of the social classes perish in war.

1.74.s:
vajra uvāca ..
asmāccaturyugādbrahmanyadatītaṃ yugatrayam ..
teṣvahaṃ śrotumicchāmi saṃgrāmaṃ bhṛgunandana .. 4 ..
1.74.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
अस्माच्चतुर्युगाद्ब्रह्मन्यदतीतं युगत्रयम् ॥
तेष्वहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि संग्रामं भृगुनन्दन ॥ 4 ॥
1.74.m: Vajra said: / Aside from this [present] cycle of four ages, O holy one, regarding the triad of ages that has passed, / I wish to hear about the war in those, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

1.74.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
āsītkṛtayugasyānte viprāṇāṃ kṣattriyaissaha ..
vaiśyānāṃ ca saśūdrāṇāṃ yuddhaṃ paramadāruṇam .. 5 ..
1.74.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
आसीत्कृतयुगस्यान्ते विप्राणां क्षत्त्रियैस्सह ॥
वैश्यानां च सशूद्राणां युद्धं परमदारुणम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.74.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / At the end of the Kṛta age there was an exceedingly terrible war / of the brahmins together with the vaiśyas and śūdras against the kṣatriyas.

1.74.s:
varṇatrayaṃ tatra raṇe kṣatriyairvinipātitam ..
( tataśca brāhmaṇāḥ kecitkṣattriyānevamabruvan .. 6 ..
1.74.d:
वर्णत्रयं तत्र रणे क्षत्रियैर्विनिपातितम् ॥
( ततश्च ब्राह्मणाः केचित्क्षत्त्रियानेवमब्रुवन् ॥ 6 ॥
1.74.m: There in battle the three social classes were struck down by the kṣatriyas. / And then certain brahmins spoke thus to the kṣatriyas:

1.74.s:
alpairbhavadbhiḥ kāryeṇa vayaṃ kena vinirjitāḥ ..)
tānabruvanmahābhāgāḥ kṣatriyāssatyasaṃgarāḥ .. 7..
1.74.d:
अल्पैर्भवद्भिः कार्येण वयं केन विनिर्जिताः ॥)
तानब्रुवन्महाभागाः क्षत्रियास्सत्यसंगराः ॥ 7॥
1.74.m: "You are few in number: by what means have we been conquered?" / To them the illustrious kṣatriyas, true to their pledge, replied:

1.74.s:
eko'smākaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhassenānīriti viśrutaḥ ..
sarvaśastrāstrakuśalo vayaṃ tasya mate sthitā .. 8 ..
1.74.d:
एकोऽस्माकं द्विजश्रेष्ठस्सेनानीरिति विश्रुतः ॥
सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रकुशलो वयं तस्य मते स्थिता ॥ 8 ॥
1.74.m: "We have a single general renowned, O best of the twice-born, / skilled in all weapons and missiles, and we abide by his counsel.

1.74.s:
bhavatāṃ bahucittatvādvayaṃ tasmātpadepade ..
jayāmo vipulaṃ sainyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 9 ..
1.74.d:
भवतां बहुचित्तत्वाद्वयं तस्मात्पदेपदे ॥
जयामो विपुलं सैन्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 9 ॥
1.74.m: Because you have many minds, therefore at every step / we defeat your vast army; no doubt need be entertained here."

1.74.s:
kṣatriyairevamuktāste brāhmaṇānsaṃśitavratāḥ ..
śaśāṅkaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmurdvijeśaṃ somamañjasā .. 1.74.10 ..
1.74.d:
क्षत्रियैरेवमुक्तास्ते ब्राह्मणान्संशितव्रताः ॥
शशाङ्कं शरणं जग्मुर्द्विजेशं सोममञ्जसा ॥ 1.74.10 ॥
1.74.m: Having been spoken to thus by the kṣatriyas, those brahmins of strict vows / swiftly went for refuge to the moon, Soma, the lord of the twice-born.

1.74.s:
sa tānuvāca dharmātmā somo rājā dvijottamān ..
prayāge bhārgavo vidvānbrāhmaṇassaṃśitavrataḥ .. 11 ..
1.74.d:
स तानुवाच धर्मात्मा सोमो राजा द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
प्रयागे भार्गवो विद्वान्ब्राह्मणस्संशितव्रतः ॥ 11 ॥
1.74.m: King Soma, righteous in soul, said to those best of the twice-born: / "At Prayāga, a learned brahmin of the Bhṛgu lineage, of strict vows,

1.74.s:
śūra ityeva vikhyāto nityaṃ vasati dhārmikaḥ ..
pramatirnāma tasyāsti putro dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ .. 12..
1.74.d:
शूर इत्येव विख्यातो नित्यं वसति धार्मिकः ॥
प्रमतिर्नाम तस्यास्ति पुत्रो धर्मभृतां वरः ॥ 12॥
1.74.m: renowned as Śūra, virtuous, dwells continually. / He has a son named Pramati, foremost among upholders of dharma,

1.74.s:
sarvaśāstrārthakuśalo dhanurvedaparāyaṇaḥ ..
viṣṇurmānuṣyamāpanno yuṣmatkāryārthasiddhaye .. 13 ..
1.74.d:
सर्वशास्त्रार्थकुशलो धनुर्वेदपरायणः ॥
विष्णुर्मानुष्यमापन्नो युष्मत्कार्यार्थसिद्धये ॥ 13 ॥
1.74.m: skilled in the meaning of all treatises, devoted to the science of archery; / he is Viṣṇu who has assumed human form for the accomplishment of your purpose.

1.74.s:
kṛtvā senāpraṇetāraṃ taṃ tu kṛṣṇājinadhvajam ..
nirmaryādānraṇe sarvānkṣattriyāṃstānvijeṣyatha .. 14 ..
1.74.d:
कृत्वा सेनाप्रणेतारं तं तु कृष्णाजिनध्वजम् ॥
निर्मर्यादान्रणे सर्वान्क्षत्त्रियांस्तान्विजेष्यथ ॥ 14 ॥
1.74.m: Having made him—whose banner bears a black antelope skin—your army commander, / you will conquer all those unruly kṣatriyas in battle."

1.74.s:
somasya vacanaṃ sarvairevamuktairdvijaiḥ kṛtam ..
prāyaḥ kṣattriyahīneyaṃ laghvī vasumatī kṛtā .. 15 ..
1.74.d:
सोमस्य वचनं सर्वैरेवमुक्तैर्द्विजैः कृतम् ॥
प्रायः क्षत्त्रियहीनेयं लघ्वी वसुमती कृता ॥ 15 ॥
1.74.m: Thus addressed, all the twice-born carried out the word of Soma. / The earth was made light, almost bereft of kṣatriyas;

1.74.s:
ādau kṛtā kṣattrabalairviṭchūdradvijavarjitā ..
evaṃ kṛtayugasyānte yuddhamāsītsudāruṇam .. 16 ..
1.74.d:
आदौ कृता क्षत्त्रबलैर्विट्छूद्रद्विजवर्जिता ॥
एवं कृतयुगस्यान्ते युद्धमासीत्सुदारुणम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.74.m: at first, it had been made devoid of vaiśyas, śūdras, and twice-born by the forces of the kṣatriyas. / Thus at the end of the Kṛta age there was a very terrible war.

1.74.s:
tathā tretāyugasyānte rākṣasairyuddhakarkaśaiḥ ..
rāṣṭraṃ rāṣṭamathāsādya pārthivāssagaṇā hatāḥ .. 17 ..
1.74.d:
तथा त्रेतायुगस्यान्ते राक्षसैर्युद्धकर्कशैः ॥
राष्ट्रं राष्टमथासाद्य पार्थिवास्सगणा हताः ॥ 17 ॥
1.74.m: Likewise, at the end of the Tretā age, by rākṣasas fierce in battle, / kingdom by kingdom, the kings together with their hosts were slain.

1.74.s:
rājā bhīmaratho nāma viṣṇurmānuṣyarūpadhṛk ..
divodāsānvayaṃ jāto nijaghānātha rākṣasān .. 18 ..
1.74.d:
राजा भीमरथो नाम विष्णुर्मानुष्यरूपधृक् ॥
दिवोदासान्वयं जातो निजघानाथ राक्षसान् ॥ 18 ॥
1.74.m: A king named Bhīmaratha, Viṣṇu bearing human form, / born in the lineage of Divodāsa, then slew the rākṣasas.

1.74.s:
pūrvaṃ tretāyugasyānte mahāvijayakāṅkṣibhiḥ ..
rākṣasaiḥ kṣatriyā yuddhe keśavena ca te hatāḥ .. 19 ..
1.74.d:
पूर्वं त्रेतायुगस्यान्ते महाविजयकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥
राक्षसैः क्षत्रिया युद्धे केशवेन च ते हताः ॥ 19 ॥
1.74.m: Formerly, at the end of the Tretā age, by rākṣasas desiring great victory, / the kṣatriyas [were slain] in battle, and they [in turn] were slain by Keśava.

1.74.s:
tathaiva dvāparasyānte vāsudevārjunau raṇe ..
cakraturvasudhāṃ laghvīṃ naranārāyaṇau nṛpa .. 1.74.20 ..
1.74.d:
तथैव द्वापरस्यान्ते वासुदेवार्जुनौ रणे ॥
चक्रतुर्वसुधां लघ्वीं नरनारायणौ नृप ॥ 1.74.20 ॥
1.74.m: Likewise, at the end of the Dvāpara age, Vāsudeva and Arjuna in battle, / [who are] Nara and Nārāyaṇa, made the earth light, O king.

1.74.s:
dvāparedvāpare rājaṃstathaiva madhusūdanaḥ ..
ekameva yajurvedaṃ caturdhā vyabhajatpunaḥ .. 21 ..
1.74.d:
द्वापरेद्वापरे राजंस्तथैव मधुसूदनः ॥
एकमेव यजुर्वेदं चतुर्धा व्यभजत्पुनः ॥ 21 ॥
1.74.m: In Dvāpara age after Dvāpara age, O king, Madhusūdana likewise / divided the single Yajurveda again into four parts.

1.74.s:
dvāparesminnṛpātīte vasiṣṭhakulavardhanaḥ ..
pārāśarasutaśśrīmānviṣṇurdvaipāyanaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 22 ..
1.74.d:
द्वापरेस्मिन्नृपातीते वसिष्ठकुलवर्धनः ॥
पाराशरसुतश्श्रीमान्विष्णुर्द्वैपायनः स्मृतः ॥ 22 ॥
1.74.m: In this Dvāpara age that has passed, O king, the enhancer of Vasiṣṭha's lineage, / the glorious son of Parāśara, Viṣṇu Dvaipāyana is remembered,

1.74.s:
prakāśo janito yena loke bhāratacandramāḥ ..
parīkṣitputraṃ rājyasthaṃ rājānaṃ janamejayam .. 23 ..
1.74.d:
प्रकाशो जनितो येन लोके भारतचन्द्रमाः ॥
परीक्षित्पुत्रं राज्यस्थं राजानं जनमेजयम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.74.m: by whom light was brought forth in the world, the moon of the Mahābhārata. / To King Janamejaya, son of Parīkṣit, established in his kingdom,

1.74.s:
vaiśampāyana ityeva śiṣyo vyāsasya viśrutaḥ ..
ākhyāsyati mahā''khyānaṃ sarvapāpabhayāpaham .. 24 ..
1.74.d:
वैशम्पायन इत्येव शिष्यो व्यासस्य विश्रुतः ॥
आख्यास्यति महा'ऽख्यानं सर्वपापभयापहम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.74.m: the renowned disciple of Vyāsa named Vaiśampāyana / will narrate the great narrative that removes the fear of all sins,

1.74.s:
dharme cātheṃ ca kāme ca mokṣe ca yadunandana ..
pradīpabhūtaṃ sarvatra budhabuddhivivardhanam .. 29 ...
1.74.d:
धर्मे चाथें च कामे च मोक्षे च यदुनन्दन ॥
प्रदीपभूतं सर्वत्र बुधबुद्धिविवर्धनम् ॥ 29 ॥।
1.74.m: which, in dharma, in wealth, in pleasure, and in liberation, O descendant of Yadu, / serves as a lamp in all matters, enhancing the intellect of the wise,

1.74.s:
yatra viṣṇukathā devyāḥ śrutayaśca sanātanāḥ ..
tacchrotavyaṃ manuṣyeṇa paraṃ padamabhīpsatā .. 26 ...
1.74.d:
यत्र विष्णुकथा देव्याः श्रुतयश्च सनातनाः ॥
तच्छ्रोतव्यं मनुष्येण परं पदमभीप्सता ॥ 26 ॥।
1.74.m: wherein are the stories of Viṣṇu, of the Goddess, and the eternal Vedic texts; / that should be heard by a human being who desires the supreme state.

1.74.s:
bhāratātpāraṇaṃ prāpya narakaṃ tu na gacchati ..
na cetsyādyadi bhūpāla mahāpātakasaṃyutaḥ .. 27 ...
1.74.d:
भारतात्पारणं प्राप्य नरकं तु न गच्छति ॥
न चेत्स्याद्यदि भूपाल महापातकसंयुतः ॥ 27 ॥।
1.74.m: Having completed a recitation of the Mahābhārata, one does not go to hell, / unless, O protector of the earth, he is stained with a major sin.

1.74.s:
daśabhiḥ pāraṇaiḥ sthānaṃ prāpnoti jagataḥ pateḥ ..
keśavasya mahābhāga nirmitaṃ yena bhāratam .. 28 ..
1.74.d:
दशभिः पारणैः स्थानं प्राप्नोति जगतः पतेः ॥
केशवस्य महाभाग निर्मितं येन भारतम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.74.m: By ten recitations one attains the abode of the Lord of the universe, / Keśava, O illustrious one, by whom the Mahābhārata was composed.

1.74.s:
vyasya vedaṃ caturdhā tu viṣṇurdvaipāyano muniḥ .
śiṣyānadhyāpayāmāsa nāmatastānnibodha me .. 29 ..
1.74.d:
व्यस्य वेदं चतुर्धा तु विष्णुर्द्वैपायनो मुनिः ।
शिष्यानध्यापयामास नामतस्तान्निबोध मे ॥ 29 ॥
1.74.m: Having divided the Veda into four parts, the sage Viṣṇu Dvaipāyana / taught his disciples; hear them from me by name:

1.74.s:
ṛgvedamatha pailaṃ tu sāmavedaṃ tu jaiminim ..
atharvaṇaṃ sumantuṃ tu yajurvedaṃ mahāmunim .. 1.74.30 ...
1.74.d:
ऋग्वेदमथ पैलं तु सामवेदं तु जैमिनिम् ॥
अथर्वणं सुमन्तुं तु यजुर्वेदं महामुनिम् ॥ 1.74.30 ॥।
1.74.m: He taught the Ṛgveda to Paila, the Sāmaveda to Jaimini, / the Atharva[veda] to Sumantu, and the Yajurveda to the great sage

1.74.s:
adhyāpayāmāsa tadā vaiśaṃpāyanasaṃjñakam ..
vākovākyaṃ purāṇaṃ ca sūtaṃ bhāratameva ca .. 31 ..
1.74.d:
अध्यापयामास तदा वैशंपायनसंज्ञकम् ॥
वाकोवाक्यं पुराणं च सूतं भारतमेव च ॥ 31 ॥
1.74.m: named Vaiśampāyana; / then [he taught] the Vākovākya, the Purāṇa, and the Mahābhārata to Sūta.

1.74.s:
aṅgāni vedāścatvāro mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ .. •
dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇaṃ ca vidyāstvetāścaturdaśa .. .. 32 .
1.74.d:
अङ्गानि वेदाश्चत्वारो मीमांसा न्यायविस्तरः ॥ •
धर्मशास्त्रं पुराणं च विद्यास्त्वेताश्चतुर्दश ॥ ॥ 32 ।
1.74.m: The limbs, the four Vedas, Mīmāṃsā, the extensive Nyāya, / Dharmaśāstra, and Purāṇa—these are the fourteen disciplines.

1.74.s:
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ jyotiṣāṃ gatim ..
chandoviśeṣaḥ ṣaṣṭhaśca ṣaḍaṅgo veda ucyate .. 33 ...
1.74.d:
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं ज्योतिषां गतिम् ॥
छन्दोविशेषः षष्ठश्च षडङ्गो वेद उच्यते ॥ 33 ॥।
1.74.m: Phonetics, ritual procedure, grammar, etymology, the course of the heavenly bodies, / and metre as the sixth—the Veda is said to have six limbs.

1.74.s:
sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ pañcarātraṃ śaivaṃ pāśupataṃ tathā ..
kṛtāntapañcakaṃ viddhi brahmaṇaḥ parimārgaṇe .. 34 ..
1.74.d:
सांख्यं योगं पञ्चरात्रं शैवं पाशुपतं तथा ॥
कृतान्तपञ्चकं विद्धि ब्रह्मणः परिमार्गणे ॥ 34 ॥
1.74.m: Sāṃkhya, Yoga, Pañcarātra, Śaiva, and Pāśupata: / know these as the five systems in seeking Brahman.

1.74.s:
saṃsārakṣayahetvarthe bhāvopakaraṇeṣu ca ..
sottarā vaiṣṇavā dharmāssārametatprakīrtitam .. 39 ...
1.74.d:
संसारक्षयहेत्वर्थे भावोपकरणेषु च ॥
सोत्तरा वैष्णवा धर्मास्सारमेतत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 39 ॥।
1.74.m: For the purpose of ending cyclic existence and among the means for spiritual being, / the Vaiṣṇava dharmas together with their supplements are proclaimed to be the essence.

1.74.s:
etāvāneva sakalo vidyāgrāmastaveritaḥ ..
vidyāḥ praśastāścaitābhyaḥ śataśotha sahasraśaḥ .. 36 ..
1.74.d:
एतावानेव सकलो विद्याग्रामस्तवेरितः ॥
विद्याः प्रशस्ताश्चैताभ्यः शतशोथ सहस्रशः ॥ 36 ॥
1.74.m: This entire corpus of disciplines has been declared to you; / and from these, excellent disciplines [derive] by hundreds and thousands.

1.74.s:
yosau vyāsasya śiṣyobhūdāraṇeyaḥ sutaḥ śukaḥ ..
tenaiva devadevena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā .. 37 ..
1.74.d:
योसौ व्यासस्य शिष्योभूदारणेयः सुतः शुकः ॥
तेनैव देवदेवेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ॥ 37 ॥
1.74.m: He who was the disciple of Vyāsa, his son Śuka born from the fire-stick, / [and] by that very god of gods, the all-powerful Viṣṇu—

1.74.s:
tretāyuge caturviṃśe bhṛguvaṃśodbhavena tu ..
vālmīkinā tu racitaṃ svameva caritaṃ śubham .. 38 ..
1.74.d:
त्रेतायुगे चतुर्विंशे भृगुवंशोद्भवेन तु ॥
वाल्मीकिना तु रचितं स्वमेव चरितं शुभम् ॥ 38 ॥
1.74.m: in the twenty-fourth Tretā age, by Vālmīki, / born in the lineage of Bhṛgu, his own auspicious story was composed,

1.74.s:
rāmākhyānaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ śrotṝṇāṃ viṣṇulokadam ..
vartamāne kaliyuge kṣīṇe nṛpatisattam .. 39 ..
1.74.d:
रामाख्यानं महापुण्यं श्रोतॄणां विष्णुलोकदम् ॥
वर्तमाने कलियुगे क्षीणे नृपतिसत्तम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.74.m: the story of Rāma, of great merit, which grants the world of Viṣṇu to its hearers. / When the present Kali age is exhausted, O best of kings,

1.74.s:
kalkī viṣṇuyaśo nāma bhaviṣyati jagatpatiḥ..
ghātayiṣyati sarvānsa mlecchānparabalārdanaḥ..1.74.40..
1.74.d:
कल्की विष्णुयशो नाम भविष्यति जगत्पतिः॥
घातयिष्यति सर्वान्स म्लेच्छान्परबलार्दनः॥1.74.40॥
1.74.m: Kalkī Viṣṇuyaśas by name will arise as the Lord of the universe; / he, the crusher of the enemy's forces, will slay all the barbarians.

1.74.s:
mlecchākrāntāṃ vasumatīṃ kṛtvā mlecchāvivarjitām ..
dharmasaṃsthāpanaṃ kṛtvā svasthānamupayāsyati .. 41 ...
1.74.d:
म्लेच्छाक्रान्तां वसुमतीं कृत्वा म्लेच्छाविवर्जिताम् ॥
धर्मसंस्थापनं कृत्वा स्वस्थानमुपयास्यति ॥ 41 ॥।
1.74.m: Having made the earth, which had been overrun by barbarians, free of barbarians, / and having firmly established dharma, he will go to his own abode.

1.74.s:
prajāsu dharmayuktāsu tatassaṃpatsyate kṛtam ..
ityevaṃ bhagavānviṣṇuryuge kṣīṇe'bhi jāyate .. 42 ...
1.74.d:
प्रजासु धर्मयुक्तासु ततस्संपत्स्यते कृतम् ॥
इत्येवं भगवान्विष्णुर्युगे क्षीणेऽभि जायते ॥ 42 ॥।
1.74.m: When the subjects are endowed with dharma, then the Kṛta [age] will begin. / In this very way the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu is born when an age has waned,

1.74.s:
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya nityameva yadūdvaha ..
prādurbhāvasahasrāṇi samatītānyanekaśaḥ .. 43 ..
1.74.d:
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय नित्यमेव यदूद्वह ॥
प्रादुर्भावसहस्राणि समतीतान्यनेकशः ॥ 43 ॥
1.74.m: always for the sake of establishing dharma, O leader of the Yadus. / His manifestations in the past are thousands in number, manifold,

1.74.s: bhaviṣyati tathā tasya yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate ..44...
1.74.d: भविष्यति तथा तस्य येषां संख्या न विद्यते ॥44॥।
1.74.m: and so will there be of him [manifestations] in the future whose number is not known.

1.74.s:
etattavoktaṃ hi narendracandra kṣīṇe yuge yadbhavatīha loke ..
ataḥ paraṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭha prabrūhi kiṃ te kathayāmi rājan..49..
1.74.d:
एतत्तवोक्तं हि नरेन्द्रचन्द्र क्षीणे युगे यद्भवतीह लोके ॥
अतः परं धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठ प्रब्रूहि किं ते कथयामि राजन्॥49॥
1.74.m: This indeed has been told to you, O moon among kings, which happens in this world when an age has waned. / Beyond this, O foremost of the upholders of dharma, speak: what shall I tell you, O king?

1.75.s:
vajra uvāca ..
manvantare parikṣīṇe yādṛśī dvija
jāyate .. samavasthā mahābhāga tādṛśīṃ vaktumarhasi .. 1 ...
1.75.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
मन्वन्तरे परिक्षीणे यादृशी द्विज
जायते ॥ समवस्था महाभाग तादृशीं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 1 ॥।
1.75.m: Vajra said: / When a manvantara has waned, of what sort, O twice-born, / does the state [of the world] become? You ought to tell of such a [state], O fortunate one.

1.75.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
manvantare parikṣīṇe devā manvantareśvarāḥ ..
maharlokamathāsādya tiṣṭhanti gatakalmaṣāḥ .. 2 ..
1.75.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
मन्वन्तरे परिक्षीणे देवा मन्वन्तरेश्वराः ॥
महर्लोकमथासाद्य तिष्ठन्ति गतकल्मषाः ॥ 2 ॥
1.75.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When a manvantara has waned, the gods, the lords of the manvantara, / having then reached Maharloka, dwell there, free from taint.

1.75.s:
manuśca saha śakreṇa devāśca yadunandana ..
brahmalokaṃ prapadyante punarāvṛttidurlabham .. 3 ..
1.75.d:
मनुश्च सह शक्रेण देवाश्च यदुनन्दन ॥
ब्रह्मलोकं प्रपद्यन्ते पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.75.m: And Manu together with Śakra and the gods, O joy of the Yadus, / proceed to the world of Brahmā, from which return is hard to attain.

1.75.s:
ṛṣayaśca tathā sapta tatra tiṣṭhanti te sadā ..
adhikāraṃ vinā sarve sadṛśāḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ .. 4 ..
1.75.d:
ऋषयश्च तथा सप्त तत्र तिष्ठन्ति ते सदा ॥
अधिकारं विना सर्वे सदृशाः परमेष्ठिनः ॥ 4 ॥
1.75.m: And likewise the seven seers dwell there always, / all of them without office, equal to Parameṣṭhin.

1.75.s:
bhūtalaṃ sakalaṃ vajra toyarūpī maheśvaraḥ ..
ūrmimālī mahāvegaḥ sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati .. 9 ..
1.75.d:
भूतलं सकलं वज्र तोयरूपी महेश्वरः ॥
ऊर्मिमाली महावेगः सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥ 9 ॥
1.75.m: The Great Lord, taking the form of water, O Vajra, / garlanded with waves and of great velocity, stands covering the entire surface of the earth.

1.75.s:
bhūlokamāśritaṃ sarvaṃ tadā naśyati yādava ..
na vinaśyanti rājendra viśrutāḥ kulaparvatāḥ .. 6..
1.75.d:
भूलोकमाश्रितं सर्वं तदा नश्यति यादव ॥
न विनश्यन्ति राजेन्द्र विश्रुताः कुलपर्वताः ॥ 6॥
1.75.m: Everything residing in the world of the earth then perishes, O Yādava; / yet the famous principal mountains do not perish, O king of kings:

1.75.s:
mahendro malayassahyaḥ śuktimānṛkṣavānapi ..
vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca mālyavāngandhamādanaḥ .. 7 ...
1.75.d:
महेन्द्रो मलयस्सह्यः शुक्तिमानृक्षवानपि ॥
विन्ध्यश्च पारियात्रश्च माल्यवान्गन्धमादनः ॥ 7 ॥।
1.75.m: Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimat, and Ṛkṣavat, / Vindhya, Pāriyātra, Mālyavat, and Gandhamādana,

1.75.s:
himavānhemakūṭaśca niṣadho nīla eva ca ..
śvetaśca śṛṅgavānmerurna vinaśyanti parvatāḥ .. 8 ..
1.75.d:
हिमवान्हेमकूटश्च निषधो नील एव च ॥
श्वेतश्च शृङ्गवान्मेरुर्न विनश्यन्ति पर्वताः ॥ 8 ॥
1.75.m: Himavat, Hemakūṭa, Niṣadha, and Nīla, / Śveta, Śṛṅgavat, and Meru—these mountains do not perish.

1.75.s:
śeṣaṃ vinaśyati jagatsthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca yat ..
naurbhūtvā tu satī devī tadā yadukulodvaha ! .. 9 ..
1.75.d:
शेषं विनश्यति जगत्स्थावरं जङ्गमं च यत् ॥
नौर्भूत्वा तु सती देवी तदा यदुकुलोद्वह ! ॥ 9 ॥
1.75.m: The rest of the world perishes, whatever is immovable and movable. / But the virtuous goddess [Earth], having become a boat then, O scion of Yadu's lineage,

1.75.s:
dhārayatyatha bījāni sarvāṇyevā viśeṣataḥ ..
bhaviṣyaśca manustasyāṃ bhaviṣyā ṛṣayastathā .. 1.75.10..
1.75.d:
धारयत्यथ बीजानि सर्वाण्येवा विशेषतः ॥
भविष्यश्च मनुस्तस्यां भविष्या ऋषयस्तथा ॥ 1.75.10॥
1.75.m: then bears all the seeds without distinction. / And the future Manu and the future seers

1.75.s:
tiṣṭhanti rājaśārdūla sapta ye prathitā bhuvi ..
matsyarūpadharo viṣṇuḥ śṛṅgī bhūtvā jagatpatiḥ ..11..
1.75.d:
तिष्ठन्ति राजशार्दूल सप्त ये प्रथिता भुवि ॥
मत्स्यरूपधरो विष्णुः शृङ्गी भूत्वा जगत्पतिः ॥11॥
1.75.m: stand upon it, O tiger among kings, those seven who are renowned on earth. / Viṣṇu, bearing the form of a fish, having grown a horn, the Lord of the world,

1.75.s:
ākarṣati tu tāṃ nāvaṃ sthānātsthānaṃ sa līlayā ..
karṣamāṇantu tāṃ nāvaṃ devadevaṃ jagatpatim..12..
1.75.d:
आकर्षति तु तां नावं स्थानात्स्थानं स लीलया ॥
कर्षमाणन्तु तां नावं देवदेवं जगत्पतिम्॥12॥
1.75.m: pulls that boat in sport from place to place. / As he pulls that boat, that God of gods, the Lord of the world,

1.75.s:
stuvanti ṛṣayaḥ sarve divyaiḥ karmabhiracyutam ..
ghūrṇamānastadā matsyo jalavegormisaṃkule .. 13 ..
1.75.d:
स्तुवन्ति ऋषयः सर्वे दिव्यैः कर्मभिरच्युतम् ॥
घूर्णमानस्तदा मत्स्यो जलवेगोर्मिसंकुले ॥ 13 ॥
1.75.m: is praised by all the seers, Acyuta [extolled] for his celestial deeds. / Then, rolling in the turmoil of the water’s surging waves,

1.75.s:
ghūrṇamānāṃ tu tāṃ nāvaṃ nayatyamitavikramaḥ ..
himādriśikharaṃ nāvaṃ devadevo jagatpatiḥ .. 14 ..
1.75.d:
घूर्णमानां तु तां नावं नयत्यमितविक्रमः ॥
हिमाद्रिशिखरं नावं देवदेवो जगत्पतिः ॥ 14 ॥
1.75.m: the fish of boundless valor leads that rolling boat— / that God of gods, the Lord of the world, [brings] the boat to the peak of the mountain of snow.

1.75.s: matsyastvadṛśyo bhavati te ca tiṣṭhanti tatragāḥ .. 19 ..
1.75.d: मत्स्यस्त्वदृश्यो भवति ते च तिष्ठन्ति तत्रगाः ॥ 19 ॥
1.75.m: Then the fish becomes invisible, and they remain stationed there.

1.75.s:
kṛtatulyaṃ tadā kālaṃ tāvatprakṣālanaṃ smṛtam ..
āpassāmyamatho yānti yathāpūrvaṃ narādhipa ..
ṛṣayaśca manuścaiva sarvaṃ kurvanti te tadā .. 16 ..
1.75.d:
कृततुल्यं तदा कालं तावत्प्रक्षालनं स्मृतम् ॥
आपस्साम्यमथो यान्ति यथापूर्वं नराधिप ॥
ऋषयश्च मनुश्चैव सर्वं कुर्वन्ति ते तदा ॥ 16 ॥
1.75.m: That time equal to the Kṛta [age] is known as the washing. / Then the waters subside as before, O ruler of men, / and the seers and Manu then perform all [actions].

1.75.s:
manvantarānte jagatāmavasthā mayeritā te yaduvṛndanātha .
ataḥ paraṃ yattava kīrtanīyaṃ samāsatastadvada bhūmipāla..17..
1.75.d:
मन्वन्तरान्ते जगतामवस्था मयेरिता ते यदुवृन्दनाथ ।
अतः परं यत्तव कीर्तनीयं समासतस्तद्वद भूमिपाल॥17॥
1.75.m: The state of the worlds at the end of a manvantara has been told to you by me, O lord of the Yadu host. / Beyond this, what should be declared to you, speak that in brief, O protector of the earth.

1.76.s:
vajra uvāca ..
brāhmasya divasasyānte yādṛśī dvija jāyate ..
jagato'sya samāvasthā tādṛśīṃ vaktumarhasi .. 1 ..
1.76.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
ब्राह्मस्य दिवसस्यान्ते यादृशी द्विज जायते ॥
जगतोऽस्य समावस्था तादृशीं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 1 ॥
1.76.m: Vajra said: / Of what sort, O twice-born, does the state of this world / become at the end of a day of Brahmā? You ought to tell of such a [state].

1.76.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
vṛtte prakṣālane rājankalpasyānte caturdiśam ..
uttiṣṭhaṃti tadā ghorā divi sapta divākarāḥ .. 2 ..
1.76.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
वृत्ते प्रक्षालने राजन्कल्पस्यान्ते चतुर्दिशम् ॥
उत्तिष्ठंति तदा घोरा दिवि सप्त दिवाकराः ॥ 2 ॥
1.76.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the washing has taken place at the end of an aeon, O king, / seven terrible suns then rise in the sky in the four directions.

1.76.s:
te tu pītvā jalaṃ sarvaṃ śoṣayanti jagattrayam ..
vināśe sarvabhūtānāmayoguḍasamā tadā .. 3 ..
1.76.d:
ते तु पीत्वा जलं सर्वं शोषयन्ति जगत्त्रयम् ॥
विनाशे सर्वभूतानामयोगुडसमा तदा ॥ 3 ॥
1.76.m: Having drunk all the water, they dry up the three worlds. / At the destruction of all beings, then, like an iron ball,

1.76.s:
bhūmirbhavati bhūpāla dagdhāssarve ca jantavaḥ ..
vinaṣṭakilbiṣāssarve jīvamātrāvaśeṣakāḥ .. 4 ..
1.76.d:
भूमिर्भवति भूपाल दग्धास्सर्वे च जन्तवः ॥
विनष्टकिल्बिषास्सर्वे जीवमात्रावशेषकाः ॥ 4 ॥
1.76.m: the earth becomes, O protector of the earth, and all creatures are scorched. / All with their sins destroyed, with life alone remaining,

1.76.s:
janalokamathāsādyatatra tiṣṭhanti nirbhayāḥ..
bhūrbhuvassvarmahaścaiva tadā naśyanti pārthiva..5..
1.76.d:
जनलोकमथासाद्यतत्र तिष्ठन्ति निर्भयाः॥
भूर्भुवस्स्वर्महश्चैव तदा नश्यन्ति पार्थिव॥5॥
1.76.m: reaching Janaloka, dwell there without fear. / Bhūrloka, Bhuvarloka, Svarloka, and Maharloka then perish, O ruler of the earth.

1.76.s:
janalokādayo lokā na tu naśyanti pārthiva..
tato'rkāste tu naśyanti saṃhitā rudratejasā .. 6..
1.76.d:
जनलोकादयो लोका न तु नश्यन्ति पार्थिव॥
ततोऽर्कास्ते तु नश्यन्ति संहिता रुद्रतेजसा ॥ 6॥
1.76.m: The worlds beginning with Janaloka, however, do not perish, O ruler of the earth. / Then those suns perish, combined with the splendor of Rudra.

1.76.s:
uttiṣṭhanti mahāraudrāstato divicarā ghanāḥ ..
kecidañjanapuñjābhāḥ kecidgajakulopamāḥ .. 7 ..
1.76.d:
उत्तिष्ठन्ति महारौद्रास्ततो दिविचरा घनाः ॥
केचिदञ्जनपुञ्जाभाः केचिद्गजकुलोपमाः ॥ 7 ॥
1.76.m: Then clouds roaming the sky, exceedingly terrible, arise, / some resembling heaps of collyrium, some like herds of elephants,
some shaped like great cities, some resembling turmeric, / looking like orpiment and collyrium, and with the luster of cinnabar,

1.76.s:
śukapatranibhāḥ kecitkecinnīlotpalaprabhāḥ..
vidyunmālā vinaddhāṅgā garjanto'tha balāhakāḥ .. 9 ..
1.76.d:
शुकपत्रनिभाः केचित्केचिन्नीलोत्पलप्रभाः॥
विद्युन्माला विनद्धाङ्गा गर्जन्तोऽथ बलाहकाः ॥ 9 ॥
1.76.m: some resembling the wings of parrots, some with the luster of blue lotuses, / their forms entwined with garlands of lightning, thundering storm clouds.

1.76.s:
ākramya gaganaṃ rājanpūrayanti mahītalam ..
gaṅgāpravāhapratimairdhārāpātaiḥ punaḥpunaḥ .. 1.76.10 ..
1.76.d:
आक्रम्य गगनं राजन्पूरयन्ति महीतलम् ॥
गङ्गाप्रवाहप्रतिमैर्धारापातैः पुनःपुनः ॥ 1.76.10 ॥
1.76.m: Pervading the sky, O king, they fill the surface of the earth / again and again with torrents of rain resembling the currents of the Gaṅgā.

1.76.s:
tatassamudrā bhūpāla velodbhedataraṅgiṇaḥ ..
chādayanti mahīṃ sarvāṃ dagdhāṃ sūryagabhastibhiḥ .. 11 ..
1.76.d:
ततस्समुद्रा भूपाल वेलोद्भेदतरङ्गिणः ॥
छादयन्ति महीं सर्वां दग्धां सूर्यगभस्तिभिः ॥ 11 ॥
1.76.m: Then the oceans, O protector of the earth, undulating as they break their shores, / cover the whole earth that was burnt by the rays of the sun.

1.76.s:
tatassaṃvartako vāyurghanānārujati kṣaṇāt ..
tato vāyuṃ samādāya svaśarīre pitāmahaḥ .. 12 ...
1.76.d:
ततस्संवर्तको वायुर्घनानारुजति क्षणात् ॥
ततो वायुं समादाय स्वशरीरे पितामहः ॥ 12 ॥।
1.76.m: Then the cosmic wind breaks the clouds in an instant. / Then, drawing the wind into his own body, the Grandfather
sleeps upon the single ocean of the world, when the movable and immovable are destroyed, / when the moon, the sun, the wind, the planets, lunar mansions, and stars are destroyed.

1.76.s:
suptvā yugasahasraṃ tu devadevo jagatpatiḥ ..
punarvibuddhaḥ kurute sṛṣṭiṃ prāgvatpitāmahaḥ .. 14 ..
1.76.d:
सुप्त्वा युगसहस्रं तु देवदेवो जगत्पतिः ॥
पुनर्विबुद्धः कुरुते सृष्टिं प्राग्वत्पितामहः ॥ 14 ॥
1.76.m: Having slept for a thousand yugas, the God of gods, the Lord of the world, / the Grandfather, awakened again, performs creation as before.

1.76.s:
sṛṣṭiṃ karoti dharmajña kalpekalpe punaḥpunaḥ ..
pitāmahasya rātryante tasmāddhi sṛjati prajāḥ..19..
1.76.d:
सृष्टिं करोति धर्मज्ञ कल्पेकल्पे पुनःपुनः ॥
पितामहस्य रात्र्यन्ते तस्माद्धि सृजति प्रजाः॥19॥
1.76.m: He performs creation, O knower of dharma, in aeon after aeon again and again. / At the end of the Grandfather’s night, he therefore creates the creatures.
[That world] is called Jana, O king, because of the generating of creatures.

1.76.s:
etāvaduktaṃ tava bhūmipāla kalpe gate yadbhavatīha loke ..
ataḥ paraṃ sarvayadupradhāna vadasva kiṃ te kathayāmi rājan .. 17 ..
1.76.d:
एतावदुक्तं तव भूमिपाल कल्पे गते यद्भवतीह लोके ॥
अतः परं सर्वयदुप्रधान वदस्व किं ते कथयामि राजन् ॥ 17 ॥
1.76.m: Thus much has been told to you, O protector of the earth, of what happens in this world when an aeon has elapsed. / Beyond this, O foremost of all Yadus, speak: what shall I tell you, O king?

1.77.s:
vajra uvāca ..
mahākalpakṣaye brahmansamavasthāṃ vadasva me ..
bhavāñjñānanidhiḥ sphīto yathā brahmā pitāmahaḥ .. 1 ..
1.77.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
महाकल्पक्षये ब्रह्मन्समवस्थां वदस्व मे ॥
भवाञ्ज्ञाननिधिः स्फीतो यथा ब्रह्मा पितामहः ॥ 1 ॥
1.77.m: Vajra said: / Tell me, O holy one, of the state [of the world] at the end of a great aeon. / You are an abundant treasure of knowledge, like Brahmā the Grandfather.

1.77.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
pūrṇe saṃvatsaraśate saṃhṛtya sakalaṃ jagat .
śete brahmā mahārāja prāgvadekārṇave tadā . 2 .
1.77.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
पूर्णे संवत्सरशते संहृत्य सकलं जगत् ।
शेते ब्रह्मा महाराज प्राग्वदेकार्णवे तदा । 2 ।
