1.77.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When a hundred years are complete, having withdrawn the entire world, / Brahmā then sleeps upon the single ocean as before, O great king.

1.77.s:
saṃnyasya dehaṃ yogena puruṣaṃ pratipadyate ..
mokṣasthānamanuprāpte devadeve pitāmahe .. 3 ..
1.77.d:
संन्यस्य देहं योगेन पुरुषं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
मोक्षस्थानमनुप्राप्ते देवदेवे पितामहे ॥ 3 ॥
1.77.m: Having cast off his body through yoga, he attains the Cosmic Person. / When the God of gods, the Grandfather, has attained the abode of liberation,

1.77.s:
ye gatā brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ mucyante sarva eva te ..
aṇḍasyābhyantaraṃ sarvaṃ tadāmbhobhiḥ prapūryate .. 4 ..|
1.77.d:
ये गता ब्रह्मणः स्थानं मुच्यन्ते सर्व एव ते ॥
अण्डस्याभ्यन्तरं सर्वं तदाम्भोभिः प्रपूर्यते ॥ 4 ॥।
1.77.m: All those who have reached the abode of Brahmā are liberated. / Then the entire interior of the cosmic egg is filled with water.

1.77.s:
śarīradhāriṇassarve tadā naśyanti pārthiva ..
antargatena toyena bhinnamaṇḍe jagatpate .. 5 ..
1.77.d:
शरीरधारिणस्सर्वे तदा नश्यन्ति पार्थिव ॥
अन्तर्गतेन तोयेन भिन्नमण्डे जगत्पते ॥ 5 ॥
1.77.m: All embodied beings perish then, O earthly king, / when the egg is broken by the water within it, O lord of the world.

1.77.s:
pūrṇe brahmāyuṣi tadā bāhyasthe'mbhasi līyate ..
evaṃ sā jagadādhārā dhārā toye pralīyate .. 6 ..
1.77.d:
पूर्णे ब्रह्मायुषि तदा बाह्यस्थेऽम्भसि लीयते ॥
एवं सा जगदाधारा धारा तोये प्रलीयते ॥ 6 ॥
1.77.m: When Brahmā's lifespan is complete, it dissolves into the external water. / Thus that earth, the supporter of the world, dissolves into water.

1.77.s:
jyotiṣyāpaḥ pralīyante jyotirvāyau pralīyate ..
khe vāyuḥ pralayaṃ yāti manasyākāśameva ca .. 7 ..
1.77.d:
ज्योतिष्यापः प्रलीयन्ते ज्योतिर्वायौ प्रलीयते ॥
खे वायुः प्रलयं याति मनस्याकाशमेव च ॥ 7 ॥
1.77.m: Water dissolves into light, light dissolves into wind; / wind dissolves into space, and space into mind.

1.77.s:
manaḥ pralīyate buddhau buddhiścātmani līyate ..
avyakte līyate cātmā avyaktaḥ puruṣe pare .. 8 ..
1.77.d:
मनः प्रलीयते बुद्धौ बुद्धिश्चात्मनि लीयते ॥
अव्यक्ते लीयते चात्मा अव्यक्तः पुरुषे परे ॥ 8 ॥
1.77.m: Mind dissolves into intellect, and intellect dissolves into the self; / the self dissolves into the unmanifest, and the unmanifest into the supreme Cosmic Person.

1.77.s:
anantāni tathoktāni yānyaṇḍāni mayā purā ..
sarvāṇi tāni saṃhṛtya samakālaṃ jagatpatiḥ .. 9 ..
1.77.d:
अनन्तानि तथोक्तानि यान्यण्डानि मया पुरा ॥
सर्वाणि तानि संहृत्य समकालं जगत्पतिः ॥ 9 ॥
1.77.m: The endless cosmic eggs that were described by me before— / having withdrawn all of them at that same time, the Lord of the world

1.77.s:
prakṛtau tiṣṭhati tadā sā rātristasya kīrtitā ..
brāhme samāśate pūrṇe punareva jagatpatiḥ .. 1.77.10 ..
1.77.d:
प्रकृतौ तिष्ठति तदा सा रात्रिस्तस्य कीर्तिता ॥
ब्राह्मे समाशते पूर्णे पुनरेव जगत्पतिः ॥ 1.77.10 ॥
1.77.m: remains then in nature; that is called his night. / When a hundred years of Brahmā are complete, once again the Lord of the world,

1.77.s:
( sarvaṃ vidhatte dharmajña yathāpūrvamudāhṛtam ..
avyaktādikrameṇātha vidhāyāṇḍaṃ maheśvaraḥ .. 11 ..
1.77.d:
( सर्वं विधत्ते धर्मज्ञ यथापूर्वमुदाहृतम् ॥
अव्यक्तादिक्रमेणाथ विधायाण्डं महेश्वरः ॥ 11 ॥
1.77.m: O knower of dharma, arranges everything just as was related before. / Then, having formed the cosmic egg through the order beginning with the unmanifest, the Great Lord

1.77.s:
aṇḍe śarīre bhavati svayaṃbhūramṛtadyutiḥ .. )
svayaṃ sa eva dharmajña brahmā śubhacaturmukhaḥ .. 12 ..
1.77.d:
अण्डे शरीरे भवति स्वयंभूरमृतद्युतिः ॥ )
स्वयं स एव धर्मज्ञ ब्रह्मा शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥ 12 ॥
1.77.m: becomes the self-born one of immortal radiance in the body of the cosmic egg. / He himself is Brahmā, O knower of dharma, auspicious and four-faced.

1.77.s:
sarveṣvaṇḍeṣu dharmajñassamakālaṃ jagatpatiḥ ..
svayaṃ śarīre bhavati prākāmyānmanujeśvara .. 13 ..
1.77.d:
सर्वेष्वण्डेषु धर्मज्ञस्समकालं जगत्पतिः ॥
स्वयं शरीरे भवति प्राकाम्यान्मनुजेश्वर ॥ 13 ॥
1.77.m: In all cosmic eggs, O knower of dharma, at the same time the Lord of the world / becomes embodied of his own accord through his irresistible will, O ruler of men.

1.77.s:
brahmāyuṣonte jagatāmavasthā mayeritā te yaduvṛndanātha ..
ataḥ paraṃ kiṃ kathayāmi tubhyaṃ tanme vadasvāyatalohitākṣa .. 14 ..
1.77.d:
ब्रह्मायुषोन्ते जगतामवस्था मयेरिता ते यदुवृन्दनाथ ॥
अतः परं किं कथयामि तुभ्यं तन्मे वदस्वायतलोहिताक्ष ॥ 14 ॥
1.77.m: The state of the worlds at the end of Brahmā’s life has been told to you by me, O leader of the host of the Yadus. / What more shall I tell you beyond this? Speak that to me, O you with long, reddish eyes!

1.77.s: iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mā0 saṃ0 mahākalpavarṇano nāma saptasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ.. .. 77 ..
1.77.d: इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मा0 सं0 महाकल्पवर्णनो नाम सप्तसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः॥ ॥ 77 ॥
1.77.m: Thus ends the seventy-seventh chapter, entitled 'Description of the Great Aeon,' in the conversation of Mārkaṇḍeya, in the first book of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.

1.78.s:
.. vajra uvāca ..
saptamaste mahābhāga jātasya divasastvayam ..
vartate brahmaṇo brahmam̐statra manvantarakṣaye .. 1 ..
1.78.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
सप्तमस्ते महाभाग जातस्य दिवसस्त्वयम् ॥
वर्तते ब्रह्मणो ब्रह्मम्̐स्तत्र मन्वन्तरक्षये ॥ 1 ॥
1.78.m: Vajra said: / This is the seventh day of your life, O fortunate one, / since the birth of Brahmā, O brahmin; there, at the destruction of a manvantara,

1.78.s:
kathaṃ kālastvayā nītaḥ purā kalpakṣaye tadā ..
etanme saṃśayaṃ chindhi tvaṃ samaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ .. 2 ..
1.78.d:
कथं कालस्त्वया नीतः पुरा कल्पक्षये तदा ॥
एतन्मे संशयं छिन्धि त्वं समः परमेष्ठिनः ॥ 2 ॥
1.78.m: how was time spent by you formerly at the end of an aeon? / Dispel this doubt of mine; you are equal to Parameṣṭhin.

1.78.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
naugatena mayā nītaḥ kālo manvantarakṣaye ..
bhūyobhūyo mahābhāga devadevaprasādataḥ .. 3 ..
1.78.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
नौगतेन मया नीतः कालो मन्वन्तरक्षये ॥
भूयोभूयो महाभाग देवदेवप्रसादतः ॥ 3 ॥
1.78.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Sitting in a boat, time was spent by me at the destruction of a manvantara / again and again, O fortunate one, by the grace of the God of gods.

1.78.s:
kalpakṣayanuprāpya dāhakāla upasthite ..
janalokagatenātha kālo nītassa vai mayā .. 4 ..
1.78.d:
कल्पक्षयनुप्राप्य दाहकाल उपस्थिते ॥
जनलोकगतेनाथ कालो नीतस्स वै मया ॥ 4 ॥
1.78.m: When the end of an aeon arrived and the time of burning was present, / having gone to Janaloka, that time was indeed spent by me.

1.78.s:
dāhakāle tadā vṛtte pralayāmbhodhisaṃplave ..
janalokādahaṃ bhraṣṭaḥ patito dharaṇītale .. 5 ..
1.78.d:
दाहकाले तदा वृत्ते प्रलयाम्भोधिसंप्लवे ॥
जनलोकादहं भ्रष्टः पतितो धरणीतले ॥ 5 ॥
1.78.m: When the time of burning was over, in the inundation of the ocean of dissolution, / I fell from Janaloka and landed upon the surface of the earth.

1.78.s:
nūnaṃ tasyaiva devasya sā māyā bhīmavikramā ..
ekārṇave bhūmitale patitasyāpi me nṛpa .. 6 ..
1.78.d:
नूनं तस्यैव देवस्य सा माया भीमविक्रमा ॥
एकार्णवे भूमितले पतितस्यापि मे नृप ॥ 6 ॥
1.78.m: Surely that was the wondrous power of terrible might belonging to that very God: / though I had fallen to the surface of the earth in the single vast ocean, O king,

1.78.s:
jīvitaṃ na paribhraṣṭaṃ nūnaṃ tasya prasādataḥ ..
tadāhaṃ naṣṭavijñānaḥ patitoṃ'bhasi dāruṇe .. 7 ..
1.78.d:
जीवितं न परिभ्रष्टं नूनं तस्य प्रसादतः ॥
तदाहं नष्टविज्ञानः पतितोंऽभसि दारुणे ॥ 7 ॥
1.78.m: my life was not lost, surely by his grace. / Then, my consciousness lost, I fell into the dreadful water.

1.78.s:
ūhyamānombukallolairitaścetaśca yādava ..
apaśyamāno jagatīṃ saśailavanakānanām .. 8 ..
1.78.d:
ऊह्यमानोम्बुकल्लोलैरितश्चेतश्च यादव ॥
अपश्यमानो जगतीं सशैलवनकाननाम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.78.m: Carried hither and thither by the billows of water, O descendant of Yadu, / seeing no land with mountains, woods, and forests,

1.78.s:
nirvedaṃ jīvite dīrghe tadā bhūtosmi śatruhan ..
so'hamārto'tha nirviṇṇastasmiṃstūdakasaṃplave .. 9 ..
1.78.d:
निर्वेदं जीविते दीर्घे तदा भूतोस्मि शत्रुहन् ॥
सोऽहमार्तोऽथ निर्विण्णस्तस्मिंस्तूदकसंप्लवे ॥ 9 ॥
1.78.m: I became despondent with my long life then, O slayer of foes! / In that deluge of water, distressed and dejected,

1.78.s:
paśyāmi jalamadhyasthaṃ vipulaṃ vaṭapādapam ..
mahāśākhaṃ ghanacchāyaṃ snigdhapallavaśobhitam .. 1.78.1 0 ..
1.78.d:
पश्यामि जलमध्यस्थं विपुलं वटपादपम् ॥
महाशाखं घनच्छायं स्निग्धपल्लवशोभितम् ॥ 1.78.1 0 ॥
1.78.m: I saw a vast banyan tree standing in the midst of the water, / with great branches, thick shade, and adorned with glossy shoots.

1.78.s:
tamahaṃ bāhubhirgatvā tasminnyagrodhapādape ..
(śākhāsaktaṃ tu paśyāmi savitāraṃ tathojjvalam .. 11 ..
1.78.d:
तमहं बाहुभिर्गत्वा तस्मिन्न्यग्रोधपादपे ॥
(शाखासक्तं तु पश्यामि सवितारं तथोज्ज्वलम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.78.m: Approaching that banyan tree with my arms, / I saw, resting upon a branch, a radiant couch,

1.78.s:
divyaṃ paśyāmi paryaṅkaṃ sarvaratnopaśobhitam ..)
paryaṅke tatra paśyāmi bālaṃ kamalalocanam ..12..
1.78.d:
दिव्यं पश्यामि पर्यङ्कं सर्वरत्नोपशोभितम् ॥)
पर्यङ्के तत्र पश्यामि बालं कमललोचनम् ॥12॥
1.78.m: a divine couch adorned with all gems. / On that couch I saw a child with lotus eyes,

1.78.s:
atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ pītavāsasamacyutam ..
padmapatrābhacaraṇaṃ tadākārakaraṃ tathā .. 13 ..
1.78.d:
अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पीतवाससमच्युतम् ॥
पद्मपत्राभचरणं तदाकारकरं तथा ॥ 13 ॥
1.78.m: resembling an atasī flower, clad in yellow garments, the Imperishable One, / his feet resembling lotus petals, his hands formed in the same likeness,

1.78.s:
alaṅkṛtaṃ cābharaṇaiḥ śikhaṇḍaikavibhūṣitam ..
ekaṃ sāhasramadhyasthaṃ bhrājamānamiva śriyā .. 14 ..
1.78.d:
अलङ्कृतं चाभरणैः शिखण्डैकविभूषितम् ॥
एकं साहस्रमध्यस्थं भ्राजमानमिव श्रिया ॥ 14 ॥
1.78.m: adorned with ornaments and decorated with a single crest of hair, / alone in the midst of a thousand, shining as if with splendor.

1.78.s:
sa māṃ dṛṣṭvā tadā bālaḥ smitapūrvamuvāca ha ..
yadi śrānto'si dharmajña vigrahaṃ vadanena me .. 15 ..
1.78.d:
स मां दृष्ट्वा तदा बालः स्मितपूर्वमुवाच ह ॥
यदि श्रान्तोऽसि धर्मज्ञ विग्रहं वदनेन मे ॥ 15 ॥
1.78.m: Seeing me then, that child said with a smile: / 'If you are tired, O knower of dharma, enter my body

1.78.s:
praviśya viśramasvādya yāvadvā rucitaṃ tava ..
evamuktasya sañjātā vrīḍā yadukulodvaha .. 16 ..
1.78.d:
प्रविश्य विश्रमस्वाद्य यावद्वा रुचितं तव ॥
एवमुक्तस्य सञ्जाता व्रीडा यदुकुलोद्वह ॥ 16 ॥
1.78.m: through my mouth and rest today, for as long as you please.' / When he spoke thus, modesty arose in me, O uplifter of the Yadu race.

1.78.s:
tato'hamavaśastasya praviṣṭo nṛpa vigraham ..
jagatīṃ tatra paśyāmi saśailavanakānanām .. 17 ..
1.78.d:
ततोऽहमवशस्तस्य प्रविष्टो नृप विग्रहम् ॥
जगतीं तत्र पश्यामि सशैलवनकाननाम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.78.m: Then, helpless, I entered his body, O king. / There I saw the earth with its mountains, woods, and forests,

1.78.s:
yathāpūrvaṃ mahābhāga nagarākāraśālinīm ..
devadaityoragākīrṇāṃ samudravarabhūṣaṇām .. 18 ..
1.78.d:
यथापूर्वं महाभाग नगराकारशालिनीम् ॥
देवदैत्योरगाकीर्णां समुद्रवरभूषणाम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.78.m: just as before, O fortunate one, endowed with the form of cities, / filled with gods, Daityas, and serpents, adorned with the excellent oceans,

1.78.s:
nṛparāṣṭrasamākīrṇāṃ vaṇigbhirupaśobhitām ..
dvijādhyayanasaṃghuṣṭāṃ varṇāśramasamākulām ..19..
1.78.d:
नृपराष्ट्रसमाकीर्णां वणिग्भिरुपशोभिताम् ॥
द्विजाध्ययनसंघुष्टां वर्णाश्रमसमाकुलाम् ॥19॥
1.78.m: crowded with kings and kingdoms, graced by merchants, / resounding with the Vedic study of brahmins, filled with the classes and stages of life,

1.78.s:
saritparvatavṛkṣāḍhyāṃ yajñotsavasamākulām ..
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kautukaṃ jātaṃ tasya bālasya karmaṇā..1.78.20..
1.78.d:
सरित्पर्वतवृक्षाढ्यां यज्ञोत्सवसमाकुलाम् ॥
तां दृष्ट्वा कौतुकं जातं तस्य बालस्य कर्मणा॥1.78.20॥
1.78.m: abounding in rivers, mountains, and trees, crowded with sacrifices and festivals. / Seeing it, wonder arose in me at the deed of that child.

1.78.s:
draṣṭumicchāmi tasyāntaṃ bhramamāṇastatastataḥ ..
yadā nāsādayāmyatra tasya bālasya ceṣṭitam ..21..
1.78.d:
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि तस्यान्तं भ्रममाणस्ततस्ततः ॥
यदा नासादयाम्यत्र तस्य बालस्य चेष्टितम् ॥21॥
1.78.m: I wished to see its end, wandering here and there. / When I could not comprehend the act of that child,

1.78.s:
pūrṇe yugasahasre'pi tamevāhaṃ tadā śiśum ..
saṃprāptaḥ śaraṇaṃ rājannahaṃ bhāvyarthena coditaḥ .. 22 ..
1.78.d:
पूर्णे युगसहस्रेऽपि तमेवाहं तदा शिशुम् ॥
संप्राप्तः शरणं राजन्नहं भाव्यर्थेन चोदितः ॥ 22 ॥
1.78.m: even when a thousand ages were complete, urged by what was destined, / I then took refuge in that very infant, O king.

1.78.s:
tato'haṃ vadanāttasya nirgataśśaśisannibhāt ..
yadā tasyodare'paśyaṃ trailosya sacarācaram ..23 ..
1.78.d:
ततोऽहं वदनात्तस्य निर्गतश्शशिसन्निभात् ॥
यदा तस्योदरेऽपश्यं त्रैलोस्य सचराचरम् ॥23 ॥
1.78.m: Then I emerged from his moon-like mouth. / Just as I had seen the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings in his belly,

1.78.s:
tathā paśyāmi sakalaṃ bahirbhūmipasattama ..
tato'haṃ patitastasya pādayossumahātmanaḥ..24..
1.78.d:
तथा पश्यामि सकलं बहिर्भूमिपसत्तम ॥
ततोऽहं पतितस्तस्य पादयोस्सुमहात्मनः॥24॥
1.78.m: so I saw everything outside, O best of earthly kings. / Then I fell at the feet of that great-souled one.

1.78.s:
tatasso'ntarhito bālassaha tenaiva śākhinā..
evaṃ mayā tasya niśā narendra saṃprāpya puṇyaṃ jaṭhare hi nītā.
mahāśarīrasya mahānubhāva mahāprameyasya pitāmahasya..29..
1.78.d:
ततस्सोऽन्तर्हितो बालस्सह तेनैव शाखिना॥
एवं मया तस्य निशा नरेन्द्र संप्राप्य पुण्यं जठरे हि नीता।
महाशरीरस्य महानुभाव महाप्रमेयस्य पितामहस्य॥29॥
1.78.m: Then that child vanished along with that very tree. / Thus, O ruler of men, having attained his belly, that auspicious night was spent by me / inside the grandfather of vast body, of great majesty and immeasurable greatness.
